audits.method_verdict: The weighted BLS statistic is mathematically sound and correctly implemented on every default path I exercised. The device power P = (sum_in w(y-ybar))^2 / (W(1-W)) / sum w(y-ybar)^2 is exactly 1 - chi2/chi2_0 of Kovacs+2002 with normalized 1/dy^2 weights; on the pod (RTX 4090, astropy 8.0.1) the 'snr' conversion equals astropy BoxLeastSquares(method='slow', objective='snr') at the same (period, duration, phase) to all printed digits (14.27136 vs 14.27136) and 'loglik' equals astropy's likelihood times (1-r) exactly as the docstring states (105.69362). Against an independent float64 numpy re-implementation of the binned algorithm (scratchpad/bls-audit/blsref.py) the fast kernels (bls.cu, bls_optimized.cu, fused bls_common.cuh) agree to |dP| <= 3e-8 (corr 1.0000000) for 5 (qmin,qmax,dlogq,noverlap,dphi) settings, for t starting at 0 and for BJD-scale t=2.46e6, and eebls_gpu (multifreq global-atomic kernel + store_best_sols) agrees to 9e-8 with (q,phi) solutions that reproduce the power via single_bls to 5e-6. The compiled fold mod1(t*f) was verified bit-identical to numpy float32 (5000/5000 points, with and without --use_fast_math/--fmad=false). Wrapped-boundary transits (phi0=0.98, 0.0) are recovered at 100% of the exact power on the fast path; results are invariant to time order, duplicated points and dy rescaling; the Keplerian helpers reproduce sqrt(G rho_sun/3pi) and the b=0 duration to 0.03%. What is NOT sound: (1) eebls_gpu (the default path of eebls_transit for ndata >= 500) does not apply the per-frequency Keplerian q bounds the docs promise -- it collapses them to the batch-wide min/max, so 87% of eebls_transit's default solutions fall outside the [0.5,2]*q_kep window, the noise floor is inflated and depends on freq_batch_size; (2) the same kernel silently returns garbage (P up to 1.68, 65075/66000 zeros) when ndata*freq_batch_size exceeds 2^32 (66000 x 66000 with scalar q bounds); (3) the fast path's box grid never tests qmax and its phase resolution (qmin/noverlap) costs 15-50% of the exact power for boxes near qmin, well beyond astropy's default oversample=10. Everything else is precision/hygiene and large, easy performance wins (default path 47-520x slower than eebls_gpu_fast, recompiles per call, allocates 20 GB for 10 frequencies, transit_autofreq's Python loop dominates the fast path 30:1).

audits.method_verdict: Sparse BLS (Panahi & Zucker 2021) is algorithmically correct on its default path: I wrote an independent float64 reference from the paper (every cyclic-contiguous run of phase-sorted points, maximizing s^2/(r(1-r))/YY = SR^2/YY, with the paper's Eq. 8-10 midpoint duration) and, on exact-phase data (t=k/1024, f=1.25, no fold rounding), sparse_bls_cpu and both GPU kernels agree with it to 5e-8..1e-6 relative for mean-subtracted data, with the candidate set complete (all N(N-1)+1 runs, wrap-around included) and the qmin/qmax filter honored. Batch BLS is a faithful port: full_bls_batch/full_bls_batch_fused reproduce eebls_gpu_fast to <=6e-8 absolute (corr 1.000000, identical argmax) at ndata 150/2000/20000, noverlap 1,2,3,4,8, dphi 0 and 0.25, ragged 7-LC batches (63..20000 points incl. a BJD-scale LC), chunked and memory-reused runs, and per-frequency Keplerian q bounds in all three conventions; the padded layout cannot read across LC boundaries (k < ndata_per_lc <= max_ndata enforced host-side) and a stale-tail probe (20000-pt LC then a 100-pt LC in the same slot) was clean. The real defects are numerical and in the non-default/dispatch layer: (1) the `use_simple` sparse kernel still carries the pre-PR#65 no-op W bound (1E-9) and produces non-finite/garbage power on single-site data in 30/40 seeds; (2) the full GPU kernel accumulates UNCENTERED w*y prefix sums in float32, giving 0.3-1.4% power errors on magnitude-scale input and power=306 (>1, impossible) when one point carries ~all the weight; (3) the float32 fold makes the exact-set statistic sort-order dependent at phase ties (26% at one frequency, N=300) and loses up to 30% at f_inj for 10-yr baselines at 4.7 c/d; (4) eebls_transit's sparse default recompiles the kernel on every call (1.2-1.6 s vs 2 ms of compute) and its sparse_threshold=500 is not supported by measurement: on the GPU sparse is 3.6-135x slower than eebls_gpu_fast at every N in 50..500, and the docs claim the opposite.

audits.method_verdict: The TLS engine (both the exact per-point legacy kernel and the default phase-binned batch kernel + top-K refinement) is mathematically sound and correctly implemented for what it computes: on 7 batman-injected transits (P=1.3-25 d, rp=0.02-0.10, b=0/0.85, 60-120 d baselines) run on the reference's own period grid, cuvarbase recovers the reference period to within one grid step in 7/7, depth within 2-5% of the reference and of the true maximum depth, duration within ~5-15%, chi2-spectrum correlation 0.94-0.997 (0.70-0.89 only for the b=0.85 grazing case where the duration grids differ), SDE within 5-10% of the reference in the SDE 15-30 regime, and the legacy exact kernel matches the fast path to <1% SDE at every injected epoch. The null SDE distribution (400 noise LCs) is 6.4+/-1.0 vs the reference's 6.5+/-1.1 on the same LCs, and the 500k-point/178k-period path runs with no memory growth. The defects found are at the edges of that: (1) the DEFAULT single-lightcurve path (tls_search_gpu/tls_search without qmin/qmax) uses a fixed phase-duration window [0.005,0.15] that cannot represent Keplerian durations beyond P~70 d while the default grid runs to span/2, so a 365-d transit on a 1400-d light curve is returned at half the period with half the depth (blocker); (2) the returned FAP is an uncalibrated heuristic that labels 23% of pure-noise light curves FAP<1%; (3) 'T0' is a phase on one path and an absolute time on the other, with the docstrings wrong; (4) the SR statistic is not the reference's definition and diverges 2x for strong signals; (5) no free baseline term, so a 0.5-sigma normalization offset halves or doubles the SDE (shared with the reference); plus several medium/low items (unsorted period grids, medfilt edge bias, coarse-epoch losses larger than documented for narrow transits, dead parameters, stale docs). Reference: transitleastsquares (installed on the pod) and a numpy re-derivation of the templates/statistics.

audits.method_verdict: The GLS math is sound: the lomb.cu tau-rotation formulas (lspow_flmean/lspow0), the CPU direct sums (mhdirect_sums/_mh_assemble_from_centered/mhgls_from_sums incl. add_regularization = ridge on amplitudes), fap_baluev (Baluev 2008 z_1 form) and the GPU direct-sums kernel all match independent references to float64 roundoff (direct-sums GPU vs astropy 3e-14; CPU multiharmonic vs weighted lstsq 3e-14 for H=1,2,3; fap_baluev vs astropy fap_baluev 1e-14). The DEFAULT NFFT path, however, is NOT correctly implemented on the device: (1) the w-spectrum NFFT reuses the psi table precomputed for the yw grid although its grid size differs (lombscargle_memory.py:186-190), which corrupts sum w e^{i2pi f t} by ~0.1 and the power by 3e-3 (N=300) to 2.4e-2 (N=1000, peak power 0.83 -> 0.81) in BOTH float32 and float64, for every default-grid call; (2) the NFFT grids are sized with k0 shaved off (lines 193-194), so any grid whose fmin is comparable to (fmax-fmin) - e.g. run(..., freqs=grid(5,10)) or minimum_frequency/maximum_frequency kwargs - reads modes beyond the alias-free band and returns powers of 1e10-1e36 (argmax wrong); with the shipped sigma=2 option even k0/nf=0.33 is garbage; (3) fast_gaussian_grid uses floorf() on a double, mis-binning ~1-2% of points once ng*xval > ~3e4, giving 1.5e-2 power errors in double precision on survey-scale grids (T=3650 d, fmax=50). With all three patched at runtime (scratch monkeypatch, tree untouched) the GPU GLS matches astropy LombScargle(fit_mean=True, normalization='standard', method='cython') to 2e-8 in float64 and 1.7e-4 (2.6e-3 at f*T~2e5) in float32 on every case tested, including narrow high bands and multiharmonic H=2,3 (2e-8 vs lstsq), and the float64 error then tracks the sigma=4 aliasing rate exp(-4 pi m/7) exactly across m=2..12. The cufinufft backend is correct on all bands (2e-5 to 3e-3, float32-limited) but rejects use_double=True. Performance: the GPU work is ~0.6 ms/LC (ZTF-like), everything else is host overhead - Python builtin sum/min/max in weights()/setdata (107 ms/LC at N=65K, 3x end-to-end), np.array([True]*nf) mask (8-17 ms/call), Baluev FAP evaluated at all nf (35-111 ms/LC at survey nf), and an 18-180 us/freq Python loop in the multiharmonic solve (18 s for 1e5 freqs; 96x faster vectorized).

audits.method_verdict: PDM: the four dispersion statistics (binned step, binned linear-interp, binless tophat, binless Gaussian) are implemented as documented in docs/source/pdm.rst and agree with an independent float64 numpy re-implementation of the same weighted 1 - SS_within/SS_tot to the level expected from float32 phase folding (max |GPU-ref| 5e-4 to 3.6e-2, entirely explained by bin-edge flips: a float32-phase reference matches to <6e-7), the _fast kernels reproduce the original kernels to <=1.2e-6 as the docs claim, batch/multi-LC/per-LC-grid paths are bit-identical to single runs, and the deprecated (t,y,w,freqs) path equals the (t,y,err) path exactly when w is normalized. Two caveats: the returned statistic is NOT Stellingwerf's dof-corrected Theta (for pure noise mean P = (M-1)/(N-1), i.e. 0.40 at N=20, while the notebook/docs quote the (N-M)/(N-1) formulas), and everything folds in float32 (no double option) so t*f beyond ~1e5 cycles changes the argmax. CE: the count histogram + H = sum N log(dm*Nphi/N)/sum N matches a numpy implementation of Graham et al. (offset by log(1/mag_bins), undocumented) to ~1e-7 ONLY when the reference reproduces two real defects: (1) on every default-path run the maximum-magnitude point is binned at index mag_bins (out of range) and spills into the next phase row / next frequency / one element past bins_g (verified: per-frequency count sums [100, 99, 100]), which makes standard_ce and ce_classical_fast disagree by ~1e-2 and both deviate from the correct CE by 1-2e-2 (N=300); (2) weighted CE truncates the Gaussian mass asymmetrically (39% of points lose >5% of their mass, the brightest point loses 100%), changing the spectrum by up to 8.6e-2 and shifting the argmin. Additionally use_double+use_fast crashes the CUDA context (misaligned shared-memory pointer) whenever (mag_bins+1)*phase_bins is odd, and balanced_magbins passed to the constructor is silently ignored (the test parametrization is a no-op). All experiments were run on the RTX 4090 pod against the tree at 7d55ea2 (md5 of ce.cu/pdm.cu/ce.py/pdm.py verified identical to local).

audits.method_verdict: The matched-filter core (Re sum_k Y_k T_k*/P_k / sqrt(sum_k |T_k|^2/P_k) over GPU adjoint-NFFT modes) is implemented as documented, and the Detector A algebra (Woodbury form of the c-marginalized covariance, depth profiled as a GLRT) is verified correct against a dense inverse (repo test), against basis-rescaling invariance and the K=0 limit (my CPU checks). But the statistic is NOT sound as an SNR on its default path, and several default-path behaviours give wrong science: (1) the whitened sums run over all nf modes although modes k>=nf/2 are outside the Gaussian-window NFFT's accurate band (device: max|dG|/rms = 1.28 vs the exact adjoint DFT even in double precision, run-to-run non-deterministic) and, for uniform sampling, modes k>=n are exact aliases of k<n, so the null std with the TRUE white PSD is sqrt(nf/n) (device: 0.97/1.38/1.95 for nf=n/2n/4n) and the statistic grows with nf for a fixed, fully-resolved template (28.6 -> 51.3, nf=n -> 8n) - restricting to k<nf/2 gives std 1.04; (2) with irregular ground-based sampling the null std with the oracle PSD is 2.0-2.2 (frequency-diagonal whitening is not the GLS whitening under a spectral window), contradicting the README's explanation that the over-dispersion comes from the estimated PSD; (3) epochs=None (the shipped example, README example 1, class docstring) tests a single phase, so a transit at epoch P/2 returns the wrong period (2.656 vs 5.3, SNR@true = -1.6) while an epoch grid recovers it at 22.6; (4) t is cast to float32 before folding/gridding, so BJD-scale times (+2457000) corrupt the template (25 vs 18 in-transit points, corr 0.73 with the local-time result; use_double fixes); (5) detector='sequential' is an OLS without intercept on un-demeaned y, so any basis not orthogonal to constants destroys the search (residual std 0.43, wrong period); (6) Detector A with the default estimate_psd=True is defeated by the systematics it models (SNR 2.1 vs 12.1 with a systematics-free PSD) because the periodogram PSD absorbs their window-spread power - the running campaign's lrt_marg arm uses exactly this configuration. The self-whitening loss is 24-28% of SNR at the detection threshold (not "mild"). A compact 10-trial device injection-recovery vs BLS showed no red-noise advantage (whitened LRT tied the flat-PSD arm and BLS within noise); the full campaign is the authoritative test and was still in its first config when I stopped. Reference used: exact float64 adjoint DFT for the transform; analytic N(0,1) expectation / Monte-Carlo null for the statistic; dense-inverse and limit checks for Detector A; cuvarbase eebls_gpu_fast for BLS. Performance: one NFFTMemory allocation (incl. cufft.Plan and pinned buffer) per template costs 0.9-14.5 ms vs 0.11-0.33 ms with a persistent buffer (8-44x per template, identical results in the accurate band), but the cunfft memory-reuse path itself returns unsynchronized, un-zeroed results and must be fixed first.

audits.method_verdict: Cross-cutting verdict (RTX 4090 pod, tree verified identical to local 7d55ea2 by per-file md5): the default paths of the core methods are numerically sound and BJD-safe: every BLS variant (fast/optimized/adaptive/standard/custom/batch/sparse/transit), TLS (fast, batch, transit), Lomb-Scargle (NFFT, direct-sum, cufinufft, multiharmonic, double), CE (standard/fast/weighted/batched/large_run) and PDM (8 kinds + batched) give results at t+2460000.0 that match t~0..100 to <=1e-6 relative (most bit-exact), are invariant to input order (<=1e-5, CE/PDM bitwise), invariant to dy rescaling where they should be (bitwise), batch==single to ~1e-7, and repeat to ~1e-8 (float atomics). References used: astropy LombScargle (cuvarbase direct sums agree to 3.6e-6 rel; the default NFFT path agrees only to 0.3-0.6% at fmin~0 and diverges to garbage once fmin >= fmax/2), an independent CPU conditional-entropy implementation (which exposed a systematic misbinning of the brightest point, matched to 3e-7 by a model of the bug), exact adjoint DFT for the NFFT, and point-dropped re-runs for NaN handling. Two public entry points are NOT BJD-safe and give wrong science on their default path with float64 input: cuvarbase.nufft_lrt (all three detectors; corr -0.1..0.7 vs the same data at t~0) and NFFTAsyncProcess (|ghat| rel error 0.94), both because absolute times are cast to float32 / folded with float32 fast-math trig; host-side epoch subtraction restores agreement to 5e-7 (verified). The dominant cross-cutting weakness is the total absence of input validation: NaN/inf/zero-dy/NaN-frequency/NaN-q inputs produce silent finite garbage, silent -1 sentinels, or (for BLS q-bounds/Keplerian grids with N<5) an illegal-memory-access that permanently kills the CUDA context of the process. CE additionally has two silent-wrong-result bugs in preallocate() and one in its binning, and the standard eebls_gpu allocates ~90% of free GPU memory on every call.

audits.method_verdict: The fast BLS family (eebls_gpu_fast / _optimized / batch, fused-noverlap kernels) is numerically consistent on its default path: on TESS-like (20K x 1788) and ZTF-like (150 x 60K) injected transits all five paths (fast, optimized, adaptive, batch, eebls_transit use_fast/use_optimized) agree to max |dP| <= 2.3e-6 with identical argmax, the fast/optimized/batch trio agree to 1.2e-7 (the kernels' own run-to-run atomic nondeterminism is 6e-8..9e-8), and astropy BoxLeastSquares (objective='likelihood', Keplerian duration window) recovers the same peak period (2.52494 d on the grid, corr 0.992 over the grid). BUT the DEFAULT eebls_transit / eebls_transit_gpu path for ndata >= 500 (use_fast=False -> eebls_gpu) is not sound as shipped: (1) with per-frequency Keplerian q bounds and frequency batching it sizes the device bin arrays from count_tot_nbins(global nbins0_max, global nbinsf_max), which is NOT an upper bound over batches (a batch starting at a larger nbins0 ends closer to nbinsf and sums more bins) -> compute-sanitizer-confirmed out-of-bounds global atomics in bin_and_phase_fold_bst_multifreq and an 'illegal memory access' crash (or silent corruption when the overrun lands inside a neighbouring stream's buffer); the trigger depends on max_memory/free device memory and on the grid, so it is invisible to the current tests (narrow fmin..fmax grids); (2) eebls_gpu reduces the per-frequency q arrays to a batch-wide [min qmin, max qmax] (locext), so 37% of its reported solutions on a Keplerian TESS grid lie outside the caller's per-frequency bounds and its power exceeds the (bound-honouring) fast path by >1% at 57% of frequencies (up to 3.6x), contradicting the eebls_transit docstring's implication that the standard path honours the Keplerian bounds. Performance-wise the July campaign left the kernels in good shape (fused kernel faster than a single pass of the old kernel; the packed-64-bit-CAS idea I prototyped is 5x slower and should not be pursued), and the remaining low-hanging fruit is almost entirely host-side and routing: adaptive/eebls_transit(use_optimized) miss the fused kernel (2-2.5x GPU time), the naive eebls_gpu_fast path allocates 6 pinned buffers per call of which 3-4 are immediately discarded (6x on ZTF-scale calls), sparse-BLS pair decode is O(N) per pair (5-30x with a bit-identical fix), kernels are recompiled per call on the eebls_gpu/eebls_gpu_custom/sparse paths (0.4-1.3 s each because pycuda runs nvcc --preprocess even on cache hits), the eebls_transit frequency grid is a scalar Python loop (0.2-1.2 s per LC), eebls_gpu grabs 0.9 x free device memory by default and still uses np.dot (BLAS threadpool CFS-throttle cliff: 92 ms vs 0.4 ms prologue). All timings were taken on a shared RTX 4090 in a CPU-quota-limited container (container-wide CFS throttle counters advanced by ~400-650 events during each run; wall clocks >= ~5 ms quantize to 100 ms), so GPU numbers are CUDA-event medians/mins and host numbers are process_time/min-of-N, reported as relative comparisons only.

audits.method_verdict: Scope: TLS fast path, Lomb-Scargle/NFFT, and NUFFT-LRT (matched / Detector A 'marginal' / 'sequential'), plus their low-hanging performance fruit. TLS default path is sound and correctly implemented: on a limb-darkened batman injection (N=1310, P=7.7 d) the GPU recovers P=7.70003, T0 within 0.001 d (1% of a duration), the refined chi2_min equals an independent numpy per-point chi2 at the reported solution to 1.6e-4 (of ~1247), the binned coarse spectrum sits 0.65% of delta-chi2 above an exact per-point scan on the same trial grid, BJD-scale inputs are bit-for-bit consistent, batch/single agree to 6e-5. Lomb-Scargle's math is right (direct-sum and cufinufft paths match astropy exact to 5e-5/8e-5) but the DEFAULT NFFT path carries two implementation defects verified on device: (1) LombScargleMemory shares the precompute_psi tables between the yw grid and the 2x larger w grid although they depend on frac(ng*x) -> a systematic 0.3-0.9% (sigma=4) / 2-3% (sigma=2) bias in the power that is independent of m and of float64; giving the w grid its own tables reduces the error from 7.1e-3 to 1.3e-5 (matching the slow-gridding path). (2) fast_gaussian_grid uses float32 floorf() for the grid index even in DOUBLE_PRECISION, so use_double=True is WORSE than float32 (top-band error 1.9e-3 = 12% of local power); floorf->floor takes it to 9e-9. Both were hidden by the LS tests' 1e-2 tolerance. NUFFT-LRT's matched/marginal/sequential detectors implement the stated statistics correctly (the Woodbury statistic tracks the exact time-domain Detector A up to a constant ~1.5 across prior strengths, i.e. it is a monotone transform of the true statistic), but (a) the module casts absolute times to float32 (BJD-scale input gives the wrong period and halves the SNR: corr 0.50 vs relative-time result), and (b) with the default estimate_psd=True the marginal detector estimates the PSD from data that still contains the systematics realization, double-counting them: the statistic collapses ~7x (null 0.5-1.0 vs 4.7-6.0; injected 2.7-6.3 vs 17-27 when the PSD is estimated from the cotrended residual). Performance: per-call host overhead dominates every path I profiled (LS: 18 ms allocation + 36 ms full-array FAP per 1.6 ms of GPU work; TLS single-LC: 96 ms unused duration table + 27 device allocations per 0.3-63 ms of kernel; TLS batch: the thread pool for per-LC stats halves throughput; NUFFT-LRT: 2.5-12 ms per template vs 0.08 ms with reused memory). All timings are from a shared RTX 4090 (medians of 3-7 repeats) and are only meaningful as relative comparisons.

audits.method_verdict: On their default paths the core periodograms are mathematically sound and correctly implemented, verified on the RTX 4090 pod against independent references: all 8 PDM kinds match float64 replicas of the kernel algorithm (max |dP| <= 5e-4, identical argmax) and the O(N^2) binless CPU references; GPU GLS matches astropy LombScargle (cython) in all 7 configurations tested (argmax identical; peak power within 0.13-1.3% in float32 at grids up to 894K frequencies over a 3650-d baseline); fap_baluev equals astropy's Baluev FAP to 4 digits at every z; the weighted CE kernel matches a numpy normcdf reference to 2.5e-7; the Detector A (marginal) Woodbury algebra reproduces a dense real-space Cov_z^{-1} construction to 1.5e-16 with correct prior->0 / prior->inf limits; eebls_gpu_fast agrees with astropy BoxLeastSquares (corr 0.984, same peak frequency) and its float32 fold is exact to 5 decimals at f=2/d, q=0.03 even at a 3650-d baseline. The defects found are (1) the NUFFT-LRT default float32 path casts absolute times to float32 before folding/gridding, halving the SNR on BJD-scale input (30.5 -> 16.3; blocker under the release rubric), (2) the unweighted CE binning sends the brightest point to mag bin == mag_bins, an out-of-bounds histogram write that corrupts neighbouring bins/frequencies (bit-exactly reproduced), (3) use_double NFFT/LS is LESS accurate than float32 because fast_gaussian_grid uses floorf on a double grid coordinate (reproduced to 2e-16 by a replica; LS peak error 2.2% vs 0.76% at survey scale), (4) the 'sequential' NUFFT-LRT detector fits its cotrend without an intercept/demeaning (SNR 5.1 instead of 25.8 with a non-zero-mean basis), plus large low-hanging performance items: CE recompiles its module on every run() (124-132 ms of a 142-174 ms call), eebls_transit's default path recompiles per call and is 65x slower than the cached fast path, the CE fast kernel launches 5 blocks on a 128-SM GPU when the light curve fits shared memory (65x kernel slowdown), and NUFFT-LRT re-allocates memory and a cuFFT plan per template (15-17x available).
