findings.title: eebls_gpu silently returns garbage when ndata * freq_batch_size exceeds 2^32 (uint32 thread-index overflow)
findings.method: eebls_gpu / eebls_transit(default, ndata>=500) / eebls_gpu_custom (same guard)
findings.evidence: bls_common.cuh:304 `if (i < ndata * nfreq){` (unsigned int product; same at :349 for bin_and_phase_fold_custom). bls.py:1504 `freq_batch_size = int(float(max_memory - mem0) / (mem_per_f))` sizes the batch from free GPU memory with no cap, and bls.py:1581 launches `bin_grid = ceil(ndata*nf/block_size)` blocks whose threads all exit the wrapped bound. Verified on device (exp4.log): ndata=66000, nfreq=66000, qmin=0.2, qmax=0.5: `auto batch: eebls_gpu max=1.6780 at f=0.3001 | fast max=0.0041 at f=0.4994 | #zero powers gpu=65075 fast=0; corr(gpu, fast)=-0.0034`; with `freq_batch_size=20000` the same call gives max=0.0041 at f=0.4994, corr with eebls_gpu_fast 0.996. A power of 1.68 is impossible (P<=1). Reachable with a Kepler-length LC (65K pts) and any scalar-q grid of >=66K frequencies on a 24 GB GPU (nbins_tot=1968 -> auto batch 126K freqs).
findings.reproduction: bash scratchpad/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch/blsaudit && python exp4_overflow.py'  (local copy: scratchpad/bls-audit/exp4_overflow.py, log exp4.log)
findings.recommendation: Compute the thread bound in 64-bit (`size_t n = (size_t)ndata * nfreq; if (i < n)` with `unsigned long long i`), and on the host cap `freq_batch_size` so that `ndata * freq_batch_size < 2**31` (and at `len(freqs)`, see the allocation finding). Add a regression test with ndata*nfreq > 2^32 but small nbins (it runs in ~1 s because most threads exit).

findings.title: eebls_gpu (eebls_transit's default for ndata >= 500) ignores per-frequency q bounds: Keplerian window collapsed to batch-wide min/max, results depend on freq_batch_size, docs claim the opposite
findings.method: eebls_gpu, eebls_transit (default path), eebls_transit_gpu
findings.evidence: bls.py:1558-1562 `minq = locext(min, qmin, imin, imax); maxq = locext(max, qmax, imin, imax); nbins0 = int(np.floor(1./maxq)); nbinsf = int(np.ceil(1./minq))` -- one scalar pair per batch is passed to bin_and_phase_fold_bst_multifreq, so every frequency in the batch searches q in [min(qmin), max(qmax)]. bls.py:2253-2256 docstring: 'honors the same per-frequency Keplerian qmin_fac/qmax_fac duration bounds as the standard path, so results are comparable across the sparse_threshold boundary'; docs/source/bls.rst:151-155 repeats it. Verified on device (exp3.log): Keplerian grid, 3049 freqs, ndata=1200: `eebls_gpu (array bounds): 2669/3049 solutions have q OUTSIDE [qmin_f, qmax_f]; q_sol/q0 range [0.0195, 15.7]`; `array bounds vs scalar (min,max) bounds: max|diff| = 2.4e-08 (identical=True)`; `eebls_transit default (ndata=1200): nfreqs=36585, 31969 solutions outside Keplerian q window`; off-peak noise median 0.0115 (eebls_gpu) vs 0.0069 (eebls_gpu_fast, which does honor per-frequency bins); at f>2 the slow path returns q_sol median 0.0046 where qmin_f >= 0.0616. exp10b.log: with array bounds the periodogram changes with the performance knob freq_batch_size (`None vs 200: max|diff|=1.743e-02 (#>1e-4: 1653/2033)`, median off-peak 0.0115 vs 0.0079). Across the sparse threshold on identical 501-point data: `fraction of solutions with q outside [0.5,2]*q_kep: standard 0.776  sparse 0.000`.
findings.reproduction: bash scratchpad/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch/blsaudit && python exp3_qcollapse.py && python exp10b_batchdep.py'  (logs exp3.log, exp10b.log)
findings.recommendation: Make bin_and_phase_fold_bst_multifreq / binned_bls_bst / store_best_sols take per-frequency nbins0/nbinsf arrays (the fast kernels already do), or -- simpler and much faster -- route eebls_transit's default through eebls_gpu_fast and recover (q, phi) with a cheap follow-up eebls_gpu_custom at the top peaks. Until then, correct the eebls_transit docstring and docs/source/bls.rst: the standard path searches the batch-wide q range, and the sparse and standard results are not comparable.

findings.title: Default eebls_transit path (eebls_gpu) is 47-520x slower than eebls_gpu_fast on the same grid, recompiles the kernels on every call, and allocates 0.9 x free GPU memory regardless of problem size
findings.method: eebls_gpu, eebls_gpu_custom, eebls_transit (default), hone_solution
findings.evidence: bls.py:1469 `functions = functions if functions is not None else compile_bls(**kwargs)` (no cache; same at :1217 for eebls_gpu_custom and :2738 in hone_solution). bls.py:1504-1530: `freq_batch_size` is derived from 0.9*free memory, never capped at len(freqs), and `gs = freq_batch_size * nbins_tot_max * noverlap` is allocated x4 arrays x nstreams and zero-filled per batch. Verified on device (exp6.log, exp10.log; medians of repeated runs on a shared 4090, relative only): ground-based 1200 pts/46K Keplerian freqs: eebls_gpu 607.6 ms vs eebls_gpu_fast 12.8 ms (47x); TESS-like 18000 pts/5456 freqs: 1092 ms vs 2.1 ms (520x); `eebls_transit() default` 1172 / 1459 ms. `compile_bls() uncached: 372-440 ms`; `eebls_gpu x3: compile_bls called 3 times`, `eebls_transit (default) x3: 3 times`, `eebls_gpu_custom x3: 3 times`. `eebls_gpu(10 freqs, defaults): free before=22.58 GB; total gpuarray.zeros allocated during call = 20.31 GB; needed for 10 freqs ~ 1.3 MB`; eebls_gpu(10 freqs) wall 542 ms default vs 333 ms with precompiled functions (the remaining 333 ms is mostly the 20 GB allocation+fills).
findings.expected_gain: Kernel cache: -370..440 ms per eebls_gpu/eebls_transit/eebls_gpu_custom call (measured compile time). Capping freq_batch_size at len(freqs): ~200 ms and ~20 GB per small call (542 -> ~100 ms class). Switching the default to the fast kernel: 47-520x on the periodogram itself (measured).
findings.reproduction: bash scratchpad/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch/blsaudit && python exp6_perf.py && python exp10_alloc.py'
findings.recommendation: (1) Use `_get_cached_kernels(...)` in eebls_gpu, eebls_gpu_custom and hone_solution when `functions is None` (one line each). (2) `freq_batch_size = min(freq_batch_size, len(freqs))` before computing `gs`, and allocate `gs` from the capped value. (3) Make `use_fast=True` (fused kernel) the eebls_transit default, or at least document that the default path is ~50-500x slower than use_fast=True.

findings.title: transit_autofreq's Python while-loop dominates the fast Keplerian path (561 ms for the grid vs 12.8 ms for the BLS)
findings.method: transit_autofreq, eebls_transit(use_fast=True), eebls_transit_gpu
findings.evidence: bls.py:369-373 `freqs = [fmin]; while freqs[-1] < fmax: df = qmin_fac * q_transit(freqs[-1], rho=rho) / (samples_per_peak * T); freqs.append(freqs[-1] + df)` -- one numpy scalar q_transit call per frequency. Verified on device (exp6.log): 1200 pts / 200 d: `transit_autofreq alone median 561.1 ms (python while-loop)` vs `eebls_gpu_fast (fused nov=2) median 12.8 ms`; `eebls_transit(use_fast=True) median 370.0 ms`. TESS-like (5456 freqs): 47.8 ms vs 2.1 ms. exp8.log confirms the grid's physics is fine (df = q0/(4.29 T) at f=0.5; on-grid vs mid-grid recovery 86% vs 91%, samples_per_peak 1/2/5 changes recovery by only 2%).
findings.expected_gain: ~30x on eebls_transit(use_fast=True) end-to-end for ground-based grids (370 ms -> ~15-20 ms), based on the measured 561 ms loop vs 12.8 ms kernel.
findings.reproduction: bash scratchpad/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch/blsaudit && python exp6_perf.py'  (see the 'transit_autofreq alone' lines)
findings.recommendation: Vectorize: q(f) varies slowly, so generate the grid in numpy blocks (e.g. compute df on a coarse log-spaced f grid, cumulatively integrate 1/df to get N(f), invert with np.interp), or evaluate q_transit on the running array with a small fixed number of numpy refinement passes. Keep the current loop as the reference in a test (grids must agree to ~1 ulp of df).

findings.title: sparse_bls_simple.cu still has the float32 no-op MAX_W_COMPLEMENT (1E-9): use_simple=True returns non-finite / >300 power on single-site data
findings.method: Inspection of the two kernels' bounds + device experiment on single-site (nightly) data at f=1/day where the all-weight box is a candidate; 40 seeds.
findings.evidence: sparse_bls_simple.cu:4 `#define MAX_W_COMPLEMENT 1E-9` and :27 `if (W < MIN_W || W > 1.f - MAX_W_COMPLEMENT)` -- 1e-9 < ulp(1)/2 so this compiles to `W > 1.f` (exactly the PR #65 root cause fixed in sparse_bls.cu:9 with 1E-4 by commit 2cc1f96, which touched bls_common.cuh, bls_batch.cu and sparse_bls.cu but not the simple kernel). Reachable: bls.py:2005 `kernel_name = 'sparse_bls_simple' if use_simple else 'sparse_bls'`, and eebls_transit forwards `use_simple` (bls.py:2306). Verified on device (sparse_drill.py section 3): "simple: 30/40 seeds with non-finite or >0.3 power; full: 0/40; worst |simple - cpu| = 4.636e+00". With a single 1000x-precise point (sparse_more.py B, R=1e6): gpu-simple max power 317.1 vs cpu 0.146. The only test exercising use_simple=True (test_bls.py:818 test_sparse_bls_gpu_q_bounds) uses qmin=0.03/qmax=0.2 so the all-weight box is always filtered out.
findings.reproduction: pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python sparse_drill.py' (section 3) -- or: t=concat([n+0.3*sort(rand(6)) for n in range(30)]); y=12+0.01*randn; dy=0.01; sparse_bls_gpu(t,y,dy,linspace(0.995,1.005,101),use_simple=True) -> inf/NaN or power>0.3 in pure noise
findings.recommendation: Set MAX_W_COMPLEMENT to 1E-4 in sparse_bls_simple.cu (or delete the simple kernel / drop the use_simple kwarg entirely, since it is slower and never selected by default); add the single-site all-weight test with use_simple=True to TestAllWeightBoxStability.

findings.title: GPU sparse kernels build float32 prefix sums of UNCENTERED w*y: 0.3-1.4% power error on magnitude-scale data, 8% with one 100x-precise point, power=306 (>1) with one 1000x-precise point
findings.method: Exact-phase data (t=k/1024, f=1.25 so t*f is exact in float32 and there are no ties) so that only arithmetic differs from the float64 reference; then the same data pre-centered (y - ybar) to prove the fix.
findings.evidence: sparse_bls.cu:210-217 (Step 6) accumulates `sh_cumsum_yw[i] = sh_cumsum_yw[i-1] + sh_w[i]*sh_y[i]` with raw sh_y (~12 for magnitudes) and later subtracts `ybar*W` -- catastrophic cancellation of two O(ybar) float32 numbers to get an O(depth*W) quantity. Device (sparse_drill.py section 2, relative error vs float64 reference): N=500 'mag 12, 5 mmag' gpu-full 1.1e-02, 'normflux 300 ppm' 1.4e-02, 'raw counts 1e4' 3.9e-03; N=300 'mag 12' 4.1e-03; centered data 6e-07. The test fixture itself uses ybar=12 (test_bls.py:64 `data(... ybar=12.)`) so this is the default-style input. sparse_more.py B (N=200, one point with dy/sqrt(R)): R=1e3 gpu-full 0.1386 vs ref 0.1420 (2.4%); R=1e4 0.1582 vs 0.1458 (8%); R=1e6 gpu-full 306.11, simple 317.13, cpu 0.1463, fast 0.1401, 201/201 frequencies with power>1 (impossible for 1-chi2/chi2_0). Pre-centering y before the call gives 0.1443/0.1458/0.1420 and, in section C (N=500 mag 12), gpu-full rel error drops 2.6e-03 -> 8.2e-08 and cpu 3.3e-04 -> 1.2e-08. sparse_bls_cpu also casts y to float32 before computing ybar/YY (bls.py:1864, :1890) -> 6e-4 errors.
findings.reproduction: pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python sparse_drill.py' (section 2) and 'python sparse_more.py' (sections B, C)
findings.recommendation: In both kernels subtract ybar from sh_y right after Step 3 (ybar is already computed) before the sort/prefix sums, and drop the `YW -= ybar*W` term; in sparse_bls_cpu compute ybar/YY and the prefix sums from float64 y (only the fold needs float32 parity). One-line kernel change, bit-neutral for centered input.

findings.title: eebls_transit default sparse path recompiles the sparse kernel on every call: 1.2-1.6 s compile vs 2 ms of compute (no LRU cache, unlike the standard kernels)
findings.method: Inspection + timed on device (repeated min-of-5; shared 4090, relative numbers only).
findings.evidence: bls.py:2101-2103 `if kernel is None: kernel = compile_sparse_bls(block_size=block_size, use_simple=use_simple)` -- compile_sparse_bls calls SourceModule directly with no cache, while the standard paths use _get_cached_kernels / _get_cached_batch_kernels (whose docstring notes per-call compilation was 'the entire batch regression'). eebls_transit (bls.py:2278, 2306-2312) never passes `kernel=`. Device (sparse_speed.py): "compile_sparse_bls: 4.101s first, 1.601s second call"; "sparse_bls_gpu N=200 nf=500: kernel=None 1.196s | precompiled kernel 0.002s"; eebls_transit default at N=50..500 is 1.4-2.4 s per light curve on a 50k-frequency Keplerian grid. (The standard branch has the same disease: eebls_gpu(functions=None) 1.104 s vs 0.402 s precompiled, batch_more.py.)
findings.expected_gain: ~600x per call for ndata<500 through eebls_transit (1.2-1.6 s -> ~2-10 ms); basis: measured 1.196 s vs 0.002 s at N=200, 500 freqs
findings.recommendation: Route compile_sparse_bls through the existing _kernel_cache keyed on (block_size, 'sparse', use_simple) exactly like _get_cached_batch_kernels; do the same for eebls_gpu's `compile_bls(**kwargs)` default.

findings.title: sparse_threshold=500 is not justified by measurement: on GPU sparse BLS is 3.6-135x SLOWER than eebls_gpu_fast at every N in 50..500; docs claim it is 'more efficient'
findings.method: Timed sparse_bls_gpu (precompiled) vs eebls_gpu_fast (cached, noverlap=2) on eebls_transit's own Keplerian grid (365 d baseline, ~50k freqs), min of 3, shared 4090 -- relative comparison only.
findings.evidence: sparse_speed.py crossover: N=50 sparse 0.315s vs fast 0.088s (3.6x); N=100 0.303 vs 0.007 (42x); N=200 0.312 vs 0.006 (55x); N=300 0.496 vs 0.005 (109x); N=500 0.917 vs 0.007 (135x); N=1000 10.3 s vs 0.005 s. No benchmark of the crossover exists in the repo (`grep -rln sparse benchmarks/` is empty). docs/source/bls.rst:121: "For small datasets (typically N_data < 500), sparse BLS can be more efficient as it avoids testing redundant parameter combinations"; RELEASE_NOTES_v1.0.0.md:66 "for small datasets (<=500 points); eebls_transit auto-selects it by dataset size". The paper's speed claim (Fig. 6) is CPU-vs-CPU; on a GPU the binned kernel is memory-trivial at N<=500. The defensible reason to default to sparse is detection efficiency (no phase grid, paper Fig. 5), not speed -- and even that is undercut by finding 'float32 fold' below.
findings.expected_gain: 40-135x per eebls_transit call for 100<=N<500 if the default switches to the fast kernel (or ~20x if sparse is kept but the decode loop is fixed, see next finding)
findings.recommendation: Either lower/remove the auto-sparse default (use_sparse=None -> False) and keep sparse as an explicit opt-in for its grid-free statistics, or document honestly that sparse is chosen for detection efficiency and costs 10-100x more GPU time; fix bls.rst:121 and the release notes. Add a crossover benchmark under benchmarks/ before claiming a threshold.

findings.title: Default tls_search_gpu/tls_search duration window [0.005,0.15] cannot fit Keplerian durations beyond P~70 d; returns half the period and half the depth at P=365 d
findings.method: experiment on device (exp_j_longperiod.py) + inspection
findings.evidence: tls.py:596-597 `qmin_arr = np.full(nperiods, 0.005); qmax_arr = np.full(nperiods, 0.15)` is the path taken whenever qmin/qmax are None (the default of tls_search_gpu and tls_search), while the default Ofir grid runs to span/2. q_kep(Sun, 1 R_earth) = 0.0035 at P=100 d, 0.0015 at 365 d, 0.00097 at 700 d (exp_g_grid.py output: 'P=100 ... std window [0.005,0.15] MISSES q_kep'). Verified on device: 1400-d LC, 30-min cadence, sigma=3e-4, rp=0.04, P=365 d (q_true=0.00154, 3.2x below qmin): default tls_search_gpu -> 'P=182.507 SDE=25.53 depth=0.00092 (true 0.00198) dur=0.808 (true 0.562)'; tls_search_batch (Keplerian window) on the same grid -> 'P=364.995 SDE=31.35 depth=0.00200 dur=0.602'. At P=120 d (q_true=0.0032): default path depth 0.00092 vs true 0.00111 (-17%), dur 0.531 vs 0.384. R_star/M_star are accepted by tls_search_gpu but only used for the period grid, not the duration window.
findings.reproduction: scp exp_j_longperiod.py + audit_common.py to /workspace/scratch; pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python exp_j_longperiod.py'
findings.recommendation: Make the no-qmin/qmax default a per-period physically motivated window: either the reference's [T14(R=0.13,M=0.1,P,small), T14(R=3.5,M=1,P,large)] bounds, or the Keplerian window from the R_star/M_star the function already takes (qmin_fac*q_kep .. qmax_fac*q_kep), and keep the fixed [0.005,0.15] only as an explicit opt-in. At minimum raise a warning when any trial period's q_kep falls outside the fixed window.

findings.title: Returned FAP is an uncalibrated heuristic: 23% of pure-noise light curves get FAP<0.01
findings.method: experiment on device (exp_c_null.py, exp_l_nulloutliers.py, exp_k_followup.py (f))
findings.evidence: 400 pure-noise LCs (2880 pts, 60 d, 6157-period Ofir grid) through tls_search_batch: 'null SDE mean=6.43 std=1.00 q50=6.26 q90=7.61 q99=9.20 max=13.00'; 'frac SDE>5.7: 0.767 >7: 0.233 >8.3: 0.045'; "cuvarbase 'empirical' FAP: median=0.236; frac FAP<0.01: 0.233". The reference package on the same 24 LCs gives 'mean=6.54 std=1.14 max=9.05' (cuvarbase 6.40/0.80/8.14), so the null distribution is not a cuvarbase defect, but the FAP formula (tls_stats.py:250-255: FAP=1 below 5, 10^(-0.5(SDE-5)) to 7, 10^-(SDE-5) above) has no relation to it. The null SDE also depends on the grid: the same injected signal gives SDE 8.24 (256 periods) / 14.43 (2055) / 21.49 (6157) (exp_k (f)), so no fixed SDE->FAP map can be right. The worst null LC (SDE 13.0 at P=0.602 d, the Roche-limit grid edge) is confirmed by the reference (SDE 11.7 at the same period). docs/TLS_GPU_README.md:221 'SDE > 7 typically indicates a robust detection' is contradicted (23% of noise exceeds 7 here; 25% for the reference).
findings.reproduction: pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python exp_c_null.py' (14 s for the 400-LC batch; ~12 min for the 24 reference runs); python exp_l_nulloutliers.py
findings.recommendation: Do not return a number called FAP from the heuristic. Either return NaN and document, or calibrate empirically per search configuration (a null bootstrap on the actual grid is cheap on the batch path: 400 noise LCs took 14 s). If the reference fap.csv table is ever adopted, it is only valid once SR matches the reference definition (see the SR finding) and the grid matches the table's configuration. Remove the 'SDE > 7 robust' language.

findings.title: 'T0' is a fold phase on tls_search_gpu/tls_transit (different phase convention on fast vs legacy paths) but an absolute time on tls_search_batch; docstrings say mid-transit time
findings.method: experiment on device (exp_d_semantics.py) + inspection
findings.evidence: tls.py:631 `'T0': r['t0_phase']` vs tls.py:1589 `'T0': epochs[lc_idx] + best_t0 * best_period`. Measured (P=3 d, rp=0.08, transit at t_start+1.11): t_start=0 -> fast T0=0.3690, batch T0=1.1013 (true 1.11), legacy T0=0.3676; t_start=100.3 -> fast T0=0.4692 (phase relative to floor(min t)=100), legacy T0=0.8140 (phase of t/P relative to t=0), batch T0=101.4075 (true 101.41); t_start=2457000.3 -> fast T0=0.4692, batch T0=2457001.4075. tls_transit on a P=7.3 transit at t0=2.0 returns T0=0.2748 (=2.0/7.3). Docstrings tls.py:530 ('best_t0': Best mid-transit times), tls.py:906 ('T0': Best mid-transit time) and docs/TLS_GPU_README.md:156 ('T0: Best-fit transit epoch (days)') say time; docs/source/tls.rst:62 says 'phase in [0,1)' but does not say relative to which epoch. Batch T0 = epoch + phase*P can also precede the first observation when min(t)-floor(min(t)) > phase*P (by inspection).
findings.recommendation: Return the absolute mid-transit time under 'T0' on every path (fast path already has epochs; legacy path can add floor(min t) back) and keep the phase under 't0_phase'; define T0 as the first transit at or after min(t) like the reference; fix the three docstrings/README lines.

findings.title: Default NFFT path: w-spectrum gridded with psi table precomputed for the other (different-size) grid -> 3e-3..2e-2 power errors on every call, float32 and float64
findings.method: Ran LombScargleAsyncProcess.run on synthetic sinusoid+noise LCs (N=300 T=365; N=1000 T=1000 heteroscedastic) with the default k0=1 grid; extracted memory.nfft_mem_w.ghat_g / nfft_mem_yw.ghat_g and compared each to an exact float64 DFT of w and w*(y-ybar); compared power to astropy LombScargle(fit_mean=True, center_data=True, normalization='standard', method='cython'); re-ran with fast_grid=False (slow kernel, no shared psi) and with the w memory given its own allocate_precomp_psi.
findings.evidence: lombscargle_memory.py:186-190 `# Only one precomp psi needed` / `self.nfft_mem_w.precomp_psi = False; self.nfft_mem_w.q1 = self.nfft_mem_yw.q1 ...` while :193-194 allocate the yw grid with nf=fft_size-k0 (ng=sigma*nf) and the w grid with nf=2*fft_size-k0 (ng=sigma*(2nf+k0)). cunfft.cu:106-108 computes q1/q2 from frac(ng*xval) with the yw ng, cunfft.cu:151 uses the w ng for u: the Gaussian is centred a random fraction of a cell off for every point. Device (exp2/exp2b, RTX 4090): sigma=4 m=12 double: max|sw-exact|=9.24e-02 vs max|syw-exact|=1.35e-11; power vs astropy maxabs=3.094e-03 at the peak (ref 0.6072, got 0.6103), identical for m=4/8/12 and float32; hetero N=1000: maxabs 2.30e-02 (ref 0.8335 got 0.8105), peak_err 8.4e-03. Same data with fast_grid=False: sw err 5.7e-11, power maxabs 1.5e-11. With own psi for the w memory (+floor fix, exp2c): power maxabs 2.2e-08 (double) / 1.7e-04 (float32). A 0.83->0.81 peak error at N=1000 changes the Baluev FAP by ~e^55. The unit tests use atol=rtol=1e-2 (test_lombscargle.py:13-14) and never saw it.
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python exp2b_bugs.py'  (scripts in <scratchpad>/ls-audit/: exp2_nfft.py, exp2b_bugs.py; fix verified by exp2c_fixed.py via patches.py apply(F=True,P=True,B=False))
findings.recommendation: In LombScargleMemory.allocate_grids give nfft_mem_w its own precomp_psi=True + allocate_precomp_psi(n0=n0) (or share only when both grids have the same n). Add a device test asserting sw/syw against an exact DFT to 1e-8 in double and a power test at atol 1e-6 (double).

findings.title: NFFT grids shave k0 off their size: any frequency grid with fmin comparable to (fmax-fmin) reads aliased modes -> powers of 1e10-1e36 and wrong argmax (default sigma=4; sigma=2 breaks at k0/nf>=0.33)
findings.method: run(data, freqs=df*(k0+arange(nf))) for bands 0.5-20, 5-20, 5-10, 10-20, 20-30, 20-50, 40-50 c/d (k0/nf = 0.03..4) on N=300 T=365 (also N=100/1000/20000 via the cufinufft comparison), float32/64, sigma 2/4, vs astropy 'cython'; bare NFFT error measured vs exact DFT as a function of mode fraction k/ng; then re-ran with the grids resized to fft_size and 2*fft_size (patches.py B).
findings.evidence: lombscargle_memory.py:192-194 `fft_size = H*(nf+k0); nfft_mem_yw.allocate_grid(nf=fft_size - k0); nfft_mem_w.allocate_grid(nf=2*fft_size - k0)` but lomb.cu:212-214 reads sw[i], sw[2i+k0], syw[i] i.e. modes up to k0+nf-1 and 2(k0+nf)-1, so the top used mode sits at fraction (k0+nf)/(sigma*nf) of the yw FFT; the Gaussian alias ratio exp(-b*pi^2*(1-2k/ng)) reaches 1 at k=ng/2 (k0=nf for sigma=4). Device exp1 section D (sigma=4, m=8): band 5-10 (k0/nf=1) maxabs 2.7e-02 (double 2.6e-02, top-quartile err 2.6e-02); band 20-30 (k0/nf=2) maxabs 6.4e+10, argmax 29.78 vs true 22.98; band 40-50 (k0/nf=4) maxabs 6.6e+35; sigma=2: band 5-20 (k0/nf=0.33) maxabs 4.1e+08 and wrong argmax, band 5-10 1e+24. Bare NFFT (exp2 sec.2): sigma=2 m=8 err 5e-03 at k/ng 0.25-0.30, 2.1e-02 at 0.30-0.40, 26 at 0.40-0.50. Reachable via the documented `freqs=` argument and via run(..., minimum_frequency=, maximum_frequency=) (utils.py:189-192). With grids sized fft_size / 2*fft_size (exp2c, F+P+B): band 5-10/20-30/40-50 maxabs 3.2e-08/3.5e-08/3.5e-08 (double), 1.2e-04/2.5e-04/4.2e-04 (float32). sigma=2 still aliases at the top of every band after the fix (maxabs 6e-02 at k0=1) because the design uses modes up to ng/sigma, not ng/(2 sigma). The cufinufft backend (nf_total=2*(max_mode+1)) is correct on all these bands (exp5: 4e-04..3e-03).
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python exp1_gls.py'  (section D/D2); fix: 'python exp2c_fixed.py' (fixes {'F':True,'P':True,'B':True})
findings.recommendation: Allocate nfft_mem_yw with nf=fft_size and nfft_mem_w with nf=2*fft_size (i.e. do not subtract k0); update memory_requirement accordingly. Additionally either require sigma>=4 (validate in NFFTAsyncProcess) or size the FFT as sigma*2*(nf+k0) so the used band is within the alias-free half band for any sigma (sigma=2 with N=2(nf+k0) costs the same FFT as today's sigma=4). Add regression tests with k0/nf in {1, 4}.

findings.title: fast_gaussian_grid uses floorf() on a double: points within a float32 ulp below an integer are gridded one cell off -> 1.5e-2 power errors in use_double=True on survey-scale grids
findings.method: T=3650 d, fmax=50 c/d, spp=5 grid (nf=912,499, ng=3.65M/7.3M): counted on CPU how many points have floor(float32(ng*xval-m)) != floor(ng*xval-m); compared GPU sw/syw and power (double, own-psi patched) with fast_grid=True vs fast_grid=False; then rebuilt the kernel from a scratch copy with floorf->floor (patches.py F).
findings.evidence: cunfft.cu:151 `int u = (int) floorf(ng * xval - m);` (FLT xval is double under DOUBLE_PRECISION). exp2b: ng=3.65M -> 3/300 points mis-binned, ng=7.3M -> 6/300; double, psi-fixed, fast_grid: max|sw-exact|=2.74e-02, |syw-exact|=3.57e-03, power maxabs 1.47e-02 (ref 0.5048 got 0.4901); same with slow_gaussian_grid (uses floor via diffmod): 9.4e-08 / 2.0e-08 / 3.9e-08. Even at ng=292K (k0=1, T=365 case) one mis-binned point left sw off by 4.7e-03 after the psi fix; with floor() (exp2c F+P): 2.2e-08. Also explains exp2 sec.4 where the bare double NFFT at T=3650 was WORSE than float32 (2.4 vs 1.2 abs).
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python exp2b_bugs.py'  (section 'BUG 2'); patched kernel: exp2c_fixed.py
findings.recommendation: Replace floorf with floor (resolves to floorf for float, floor for double); keep precompute_psi's modflt and the grid index derived from the same expression.

findings.title: nharmonics>1 with use_fft=False silently returns the H=1 periodogram
findings.method: LombScargleAsyncProcess(nharmonics=2/3).run(..., use_fft=False) vs weighted lstsq with H harmonics and with H=1.
findings.evidence: lombscargle.py:442-457 the use_fft=False branch calls lomb_dirsum, which (lomb.cu:151-172) only forms C,S,C2,S2,YCh,YSh, and ignores memory.nharmonics; the multiharmonic host solve at :482-496 is only on the FFT branch. exp3: 'GPU H=2 use_fft=False vs lstsq H=2' maxabs 5.98e-01 (peak 0.606 -> 0.008, argmax wrong) while 'vs lstsq H=1' maxabs 5.5e-15; identical for H=3.
findings.recommendation: Either route use_fft=False with nharmonics>1 through lomb_scargle_direct_sums(nharms=H) (host, already correct) or raise NotImplementedError; add a test.

findings.title: amplitude_prior is silently ignored on the GPU path when nharmonics>1
findings.method: run(..., amplitude_prior=0.3) with nharmonics=1 and 2 (fast_grid=False to remove the psi bug) vs ridge-regularised lstsq (lambda=1/s^2 on amplitudes, offset unpenalised) and vs the unregularised reference.
findings.evidence: lombscargle.py:493-494 calls _mh_power_from_spectra(sw, syw, k0, nharm, nf, memory.yy) without reg_kwargs (signature :279 has reg_kwargs=None), and memory.reg/amplitude_prior is only consumed by the H=1 kernel. exp3: H=1 amplitude_prior=0.3 vs ridge maxabs 4.4e-10 (correct); H=2 amplitude_prior=0.3 vs ridge maxabs 5.8e-01, vs UNregularised 1.2e-08. The CPU add_regularization itself is correct (exp3: vs ridge 5e-16 for H=1,2).
findings.recommendation: Pass reg_kwargs=dict(amplitude_priors=memory.amplitude_prior) into _mh_power_from_spectra when amplitude_prior is set; test H=2 against the CPU regularised direct sums.

findings.title: Multiharmonic host solve is a per-frequency Python loop (28-180 us/freq): 18 s per light curve at 1e5 frequencies; a batched np.linalg.solve is 96x faster and bit-identical
findings.method: Timed _mh_power_from_spectra on synthetic spectra (pod: nf=1e4/1e5, H=2; local: nf=2e4, H=2/3) and compared against a vectorised implementation built from the same _mh_assemble_from_centered algebra using stacked (nf,2H,2H) systems.
findings.evidence: lombscargle.py:319-324 `for j in range(nf): sums = _mh_assemble_from_centered(...); power[j] = mhgls_from_sums(...)` (each iteration builds Python lists and calls np.linalg.solve on a 2Hx2H). Pod (exp3): nf=10000 H=2 1.83 s (183 us/freq), nf=100000 17.8 s. Local (mh_vec_local.py): H=2 nf=20000 loop 0.56 s vs vectorised 0.0058 s (96x), H=3 95x, max|diff|=5.6e-17. A ZTF-scale grid (365K freqs) would take ~1 min per LC on the host vs <1 ms of GPU time.
findings.reproduction: python3 <scratchpad>/ls-audit/mh_vec_local.py  (CPU only); pod: exp3_mhgls.py last section
findings.recommendation: Vectorise _mh_power_from_spectra: build A as an (nf,2H,2H) array and b as (nf,2H), np.linalg.solve once, power = einsum(theta,b)/YY (regularisation adds lambda to the diagonal). ~100x, no change in results.
findings.expected_gain: ~96x on the host solve (measured, numpy float64); multiharmonic survey runs go from tens of seconds to <0.1 s per LC

findings.title: weights()/setdata use Python builtins sum/min/max over numpy arrays: 107 ms per light curve at N=65K (63% of the Kepler-like LS time); numpy reductions give 3x end-to-end
findings.method: cProfile of batched_run_const_nfreq (10 LCs, N=65000, nf=210K, float32) plus per-stage timing; then monkeypatched weights() to np.sum and the module-level min/max names to numpy reductions and re-timed (5 repeats, median; shared RTX 4090, relative comparison only).
findings.evidence: lombscargle_memory.py:31 `return w/sum(w)` (builtin sum), :325-326 `self.tmin = min(t); self.tmax = max(t)` (builtins over a 65K float32 array). cProfile (exp8): setdata 1.227 s cumulative for 10 LCs of which builtins.sum 0.598 s, builtins.max 0.216 s, builtins.min 0.134 s; per-stage: setdata 106.8 ms vs GPU nfft x2+lomb+D2H 0.58 ms, H2D 0.11 ms. exp9: Kepler-like 149.8 -> 50.2 ms/LC (3.0x) with numpy reductions; ZTF-like (N=300) unchanged 2.2 ms/LC. cuvarbase/utils.py:10 weights() already uses np.sum.
findings.recommendation: Use np.sum / t.min() / t.max() (and float64 for tmin/tmax before the float32 cast). Remaining Kepler-like cost is also host-side (normalize_light_curves deepcopy+nanmean 9 ms, pinned copies) and worth a second pass.
findings.expected_gain: 3.0x per LC at N=65K (measured); ~100 ms/LC saved

findings.title: only_return_best_freqs evaluates the Baluev FAP at all nf frequencies (35-111 ms/LC at survey nf) though only the peak is used
findings.method: Timed fap_baluev on arrays of 365K and 1.825M values vs a 1-element array (pod CPU, 5 repeats, median).
findings.evidence: lombscargle.py:981 `fap = fap_baluev(batch[i][0], batch[i][2], p[mask], np.max(freqs[mask]))` then :982 uses only fap[best_index]. exp7: nf=365000 full-array 34.5 ms vs scalar 0.099 ms; nf=1825000 111.3 ms vs 0.098 ms. The whole GPU pipeline for a ZTF-like LC is 0.6-0.7 ms (exp7 stage breakdown), so this is the dominant per-LC cost of the 'best frequency' API at survey grids (consistent with the 50-70% overhead recorded in the project notes).
findings.recommendation: Compute fap_baluev(t, dy, p[mask][best_index], fmax) only.
findings.expected_gain: 35-110 ms per LC at survey grids (measured), i.e. up to ~50x on the best-frequency path

findings.title: CE: maximum-magnitude point is always binned at index mag_bins (out of range) -> cross-phase/cross-frequency spill and 1-element OOB write on every default run
findings.method: Conditional Entropy (all unweighted kernels: histogram_data_count/standard_ce/constdpdm_ce/log_prob and ce_classical_fast/faster)
findings.evidence: ce_memory.py:317 `y = np.floor(y * self.mag_bins).astype(self.ytype)` on y=(y-min)/(max-min) gives floor(1.0*NMAG)=NMAG for the max point. ce.cu:93 uses it unclipped: `atomicInc(&(bin[offset + posmod(n, NPHASE) * NMAG + m]) ...)` -> index (n+1, 0), and for n=NPHASE-1 the NEXT frequency's (0,0) bin, and for the last frequency one element past bins_g. In ce_classical_fast/faster the same index lands on block_bin_phi[0] (shared-memory Nphi of phase bin 0). Verified on device (ce_audit.py hist): GPU bins_g vs correct histogram differ in 100 bins (50 freqs x 2), match an emulation of the spill in 0 bins; 'counts spilled into the NEXT frequency's (phase0,mag0) bin: 5 of 50 freqs' (10/50 with phase_overlap=1). ce_followup.py san_oob: 'bins total=299 (expected 300); per-freq sums=[100 99 100]' -- one count written past the array. Effect on CE (ce_audit.py kernels, N=400): max|gpu-correct ref| = 1.7e-2 (standard), 8.9e-3 (fast), 390/400 frequencies off by >1e-4; ce_followup.py stdvsfast: 'max|standard-fast|=6.8e-3..1.1e-2'; with N=3 the two kernels return entirely different spectra (standard {-1.61,-1.26,-1.15,-0.97}, fast {-1.61,-1.15,-1.07,-0.97,-0.34}). Same root cause makes compute_mag_bin_fracs (ce_memory.py:247, `y == i` for i<mag_bins) sum to 0.9975 instead of 1 for log_prob. argmin was unchanged in the N>=300 tests; magnitude is ~1/N of the data per frequency.
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python ce_audit.py hist && python ce_followup.py san_oob && python ce_followup.py stdvsfast'  (scripts: <scratchpad>/pdm-ce/ce_audit.py, ce_followup.py)
findings.recommendation: Clip the bin index: `np.minimum(np.floor(y*self.mag_bins), self.mag_bins-1)` in ce_memory.py:317 (and clamp m0 in histogram_data_weighted ce.cu:65 for consistency); add a regression test asserting sum(bins) per frequency == N*(PO+1)*(MO+1) and standard_ce == ce_classical_fast to 1e-6.

findings.title: Weighted CE truncates Gaussian probability mass asymmetrically (distance to the LOWER bin edge only) -> biased histogram, brightest point dropped entirely
findings.method: Conditional Entropy, weighted=True (histogram_data_weighted)
findings.evidence: ce.cu:69 `if (abs(z) > max_phi * DY && m != m0) continue;` where z = m/NMAG - Y is the distance to the lower edge of bin m. A point just above the lower edge of its own bin m0 has |z| ~ 1/NMAG to bin m0-1's lower edge and is skipped even though that bin's upper edge is adjacent; bins above the point are never skipped this way. Verified on device (ce_audit.py weighted; N=300, mag_bins=5, max_phi=3 default): 'per-point retained prob mass: min=0.000 mean=0.9068 ... frac points losing >5%: 0.390'; 'mean assigned-mag bias (units of mag bin width): kernel=0.057 exact=-0.002'; GPU bins match an emulation of the truncation rule to 4e-6 and the exact Gaussian-integrated histogram to 3.1 counts; with max_phi=1e6 GPU matches exact to 4.5e-6 (so the integration itself is right). CE differs from the exact-mass CE by up to 4.1e-2 (mag_bins=5), 1.9e-2 (mag_bins=10), 0.21 (mag_overlap=1). Full spectrum: 'argmin f: max_phi=3 -> 1.3000, max_phi=1e6 -> 1.2991 ...; max|p3-pinf|=8.570e-02' (one grid step shift, injected f0=1.3).
findings.recommendation: Skip a bin only when the whole bin is beyond max_phi sigma: `if (z > max_phi*DY || zmax < -max_phi*DY) continue;` (zmax computed before the test), or drop the truncation entirely since normcdf is already evaluated per bin (cost is NMAG normcdf per point-frequency either way). Add a test comparing bins_g against scipy.special.ndtr-integrated masses.

findings.title: CE use_double=True + use_fast=True crashes the CUDA context ('misaligned address') whenever (mag_bins+1)*phase_bins is odd
findings.method: Conditional Entropy fast kernels (ce_classical_fast / ce_classical_faster) in double precision
findings.evidence: ce.cu:144-145: `unsigned int r = ((nmag * nphase + nphase) * sizeof(unsigned int)) % sizeof(FLT); FLT * Hc = (FLT *)&block_bin_phi[nphase + r];` -- r is a BYTE remainder (4 when (nmag+1)*nphase is odd and FLT=double) but is used as an ELEMENT offset (4 uints = 16 bytes), so Hc starts at byte (nmag*nphase+nphase)*4+16, which is 4 mod 8: misaligned for double. Python side (ce.py:131 `shmem += shmem % r`) only adds 4 bytes, so the kernel also runs 12 bytes past its dynamic shared allocation. Verified on device (ce_audit.py align): phase_bins=5, mag_bins=4, use_double=True, use_fast=True -> `pycuda._driver.LogicError: cuStreamSynchronize failed: misaligned address` followed by 'PyCUDA WARNING: a clean-up operation failed (dead context maybe?)' for every subsequent call. Default (10,5) has remainder 0, which is why test_ce.py never hits it.
findings.recommendation: Compute the padding in elements: `unsigned int pad = (((nmag*nphase + nphase) * sizeof(unsigned int)) % sizeof(FLT)) / sizeof(unsigned int);` and use `&block_bin_phi[nphase + pad]` in both kernels (Python's +4 bytes then matches). Parametrize test_fast over (phase_bins, mag_bins) with odd/even combinations and use_double.

findings.title: CE: balanced_magbins passed to the ConditionalEntropyAsyncProcess constructor is silently ignored (test parametrization is a no-op)
findings.method: Conditional Entropy, balanced_magbins option
findings.evidence: ce.py:224 only reads `kwargs.get('balanced_magbins', False)` for the mag_overlap check; `self.balanced_magbins` is never set, and the kw dicts in allocate_for_single_lc (ce.py:341-350), preallocate (432-443) and batched_run_const_nfreq (677-687) forward phase_bins/mag_bins/weighted/compute_log_prob but not balanced_magbins, so ConditionalEntropyMemory gets its default False. Verified on device (ce_followup.py balanced): 'proc has attribute balanced_magbins: False'; 'max|ctor(balanced=True) - plain|=0.000e+00   max|run(balanced=True) - plain|=4.648e-02'; 'memory.balanced_magbins via allocate() on a proc constructed with balanced_magbins=True: False'. test_ce.py:198 `@pytest.mark.parametrize('balanced_magbins', [True, False])` feeds the constructor, so both parametrizations run the plain kernel. (constdpdm_ce itself is correct when reached via run(balanced_magbins=True): matches numpy to 1.7e-7.)
findings.recommendation: Store `self.balanced_magbins = kwargs.get('balanced_magbins', False)` (and widen_mag_range) in __init__ and forward it in the three kw dicts; make test_ce assert balanced != unbalanced results.

findings.title: epochs=None default runs a single-phase 'period search' and returns the wrong period for transits not at phase 0 (shipped example, README example 1, class docstring all use it)
findings.method: Device experiment: 600-pt ground-like sampling, injected box P=5.3 d, dur=0.22 d, depth 0.01, white noise 3e-3; run(t,y,periods,durations) with epochs=None vs an explicit 48-epoch grid per period.
findings.evidence: nufft_lrt.py:451 `epochs_arr = np.array([0.0], ...)` and :527 `self._generate_template(t, period, 0.0, duration, depth)`. t3.log: 'injected epoch=2.65  epochs=None: shape=(32, 1) best P=2.656 (true 5.3)  SNR@true=-1.64  max=5.66' vs 'with 48-epoch grid: best P=5.300  SNR@true=22.57'. With injected epoch 0.0 both agree (best P=5.300, SNR 21.06) - which is why test_detection_of_known_transit (true_epoch=0.0) passes. The shipped example (true_epoch=0.5, dur 0.3, template half-width <=0.25 at phase 0) reports 'Period: 3.59 days (true: 3.50) Duration: 0.37 (true 0.30) SNR: 5.50' - a period-drift coincidence, not a detection.
findings.reproduction: bash scratchpad/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch/lrtaud && python lrtaud_exp3_epoch_bjd.py'  (local copy: scratchpad/lrt/lrtaud_exp3_epoch_bjd.py); also bash scratchpad/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/cuvarbase && python examples/nufft_lrt_example.py'
findings.recommendation: Make epochs=None mean an automatic epoch grid (np.linspace(0,P, ceil(oversample*P/duration)) per period, as the validation harness does) and return the max (or the full 3-D array); alternatively refuse epochs=None. Fix the class docstring, README example 1 and examples/nufft_lrt_example.py; add a test with a non-zero injected epoch.

findings.title: Whitened sums run over all nf adjoint-NFFT modes: the upper half band (k>=nf/2) is outside the NFFT's accurate band (O(1) error, non-deterministic) and the lower/upper halves double-count, so the statistic scales as ~sqrt(nf/n) instead of being ~N(0,1)
findings.method: Device: compute_nufft vs exact float64 adjoint DFT per band (float32 and use_double=True); Monte-Carlo null (200 white-noise realizations, fixed template) with the TRUE white PSD n*sigma^2 at nf=n,2n,4n for uniform and ground sampling; same with weights restricted to k<nf/2; statistic at the true template of a fully-resolved 0.6 d transit vs nf.
findings.evidence: exp1 (float32): 'data k<nf/2 max|dG|/rms|E|=1.80e-04' but 'data k>=nf/2 max|dG|/rms|E|=1.28e+00 max rel=6.52e+00'; use_double=True: 'k<nf/2 9.99e-10' vs 'k>=nf/2 1.28e+00' (algorithmic aliasing, not roundoff). exp9: upper band run-to-run 'cur repeat max|d|/rms=6.3e-01' at n=50000 (atomic-order noise amplified by exp(b*khat^2)). SNR spectrum GPU vs exact-DFT pipeline: max|d|=0.37 on max SNR 14.9 (corr 0.9995). exp2 uniform sampling, true white PSD: 'nf=600 std=0.970 | nf=1200 std=1.378 | nf=2400 std=1.952 (sqrt(nf/n)=1,1.414,2)'. exp10 uniform: 'all nf modes std=1.478 -> k<nf/2 only std=1.040' (estimated PSD 1.455 -> 1.028). exp9 fixed 0.6 d transit, true white PSD: 'nf=1*n SNR=28.62, 2*n 33.57, 4*n 39.41, 8*n 51.25' - the README's 'raise nf for short transits' advice inflates the number without adding information. Code sums all nf bins: nufft_lrt.py:490 `weights = np.ones(nf)`; the comment at :328-332 acknowledges the upper band 'carries growing deconvolution error' but claims it 'largely cancels' - it does not (0.37 SNR-unit differences).
findings.reproduction: bash scratchpad/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch/lrtaud && python lrtaud_exp1_nfft_band.py; python lrtaud_exp2_null.py; python lrtaud_exp9.py; python lrtaud_exp10.py'
findings.recommendation: Transform with 2*nf modes and keep k<nf (or set weights[nf//2:]=0 and document that the usable band is k<nf/2). This drops the garbage band and, for uniform sampling, restores std~1 with a correct PSD. Document that the statistic's scale then depends on the sampling pattern only (finding on irregular sampling). Add a regression test comparing compute_nufft to the exact adjoint DFT over the FULL returned band.

findings.title: BJD-scale times are broken on the default path: t is cast to float32 before template folding and gridding (no subtract_epoch, unlike BLS)
findings.method: Device: identical lightcurve with t, t+2000 (BTJD-like) and t+2457000 (BJD), epoch grid of 48 at the true period; compare SNR-vs-epoch curves and the template's in-transit membership; repeat with use_double=True.
findings.evidence: nufft_lrt.py:411 `t = np.asarray(t, dtype=self.real_type)` (float32 by default) precedes :557 `phase = np.fmod(t - epoch, period) / period`. t3.log: 't offset 0.0: max SNR=16.60 corr vs local=1.0000 in-transit pts=18', '+2000.0: 16.61 corr 1.0000 pts 18', '+2457000.0: max SNR=17.20 corr vs local=0.7285 in-transit pts in template=25 (local 18)', 'use_double=True at offset 2457000: corr 1.0000'. float32 ulp at 2.457e6 is 0.25 d, larger than the 0.22 d transit. bls.py:584,1263,... all call subtract_epoch; nufft_lrt.py never does.
findings.recommendation: In run(): `t, t0 = subtract_epoch(np.asarray(t, np.float64)); epochs -= t0` before any float32 cast (the adjoint NFFT's absolute-phase factor is common to Y and T, so the shift is harmless for the statistic); keep the fold in float64. Add a BJD-offset regression test.

findings.title: detector='sequential' fits OLS without an intercept on un-demeaned y: any basis not orthogonal to constants absorbs the mean flux and wrecks the residual and the period search
findings.method: CPU: _sequential_detrend with V=[t] (raw), [t-mean], [1,t] on y=1+trend+noise, measure residual slope/std. Device: period scan (24 periods x 32 epochs) with a non-zero-mean sinusoidal basis, detector='sequential' vs the same basis demeaned vs 'marginal'.
findings.evidence: t4.log: 'sequential detrend basis=raw t residual slope*std(t)=-0.43204 (trend amp 0.004) resid std=0.43204' vs 'demeaned t ... resid std=0.00100'. Device scan: 'sequential raw basis: bestP=2.931 snr@true=3.44 max=8.48' vs 'sequential demeaned : bestP=5.300 snr@true=21.86' and 'marginal raw basis : bestP=5.300 snr@true=11.07'. The 'marginal' path demeans V (nufft_lrt.py:496 `V[:, j] - V[:, j].mean()`) but _sequential_detrend uses the raw basis and raw y (:101 `np.linalg.lstsq(V, y)`). Real cotrending bases (Kepler/TESS CBVs) are not zero-mean; the repo test passes only because its basis is `(t - t.mean())/t.std()`.
findings.recommendation: Demean y and every basis column (or append a constant column) inside _sequential_detrend, mirroring the 'marginal' path; add a test with a non-zero-mean basis.

findings.title: Detector A on its default path (estimate_psd=True) is defeated by the systematics it models: the periodogram PSD estimate absorbs the window-spread systematics power, so the marginalized statistic loses ~6x SNR; the running campaign's lrt_marg arm uses this configuration
findings.method: Device: red+white noise, 0.006-depth transit, plus a 10-sigma-amplitude basis-aligned systematic; compare 'matched' and 'marginal' at the true template with the PSD estimated from y (default) vs a PSD from the systematics-free noise realization; also vs prior variance 1e-4..1.
findings.evidence: exp8: 'noise+transit+10sigma systematics: matched est-PSD 1.57 | matched clean-PSD 13.29 | marginal est-PSD 2.11 | marginal clean-PSD 12.07' (without systematics: matched est 8.97 / clean 11.96; marginal est 9.04 / clean 11.92 - the marginalization itself works). exp4: 'marginal prior_var=1e-4/1e-2/1: SNR@true with PSD estimated from y = 3.28/3.27/3.29 | with noise-only PSD = 14.27/14.25/14.24'. The PSD is estimated at :476 from Y_nufft of y - V mu, i.e. with V(c-mu) still present; with gappy ground sampling the systematics' power is spread across the whole band by the spectral window (daily aliases), whitening away the transit. scripts/nufft_lrt_validation.py:355-359 builds lrt_marg with no psd= (default estimate).
findings.reproduction: bash scratchpad/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch/lrtaud && python lrtaud_exp8_misc.py; python lrtaud_exp4_detectors.py'
findings.recommendation: For detector='marginal' estimate the PSD from the basis-projected residual (OLS or MAP y - V c_hat) rather than from y; document that psd= from a systematics-free model is strongly preferred. Re-run the campaign's lrt_marg arm with that change before quoting a Detector-A result.

findings.title: One NFFTMemory allocation (5 gpuarrays + cufft.Plan + pinned host buffer) per template: 8x-44x per-template speedup available by reusing a single NFFT buffer set
findings.method: Device timing (shared RTX 4090, repeated medians and minima, relative only): proc.compute_nufft per template vs NFFTAsyncProcess.run(memory=persistent) with the grid zeroed and the stream synchronized; equality of results in the accurate band.
findings.evidence: nufft_lrt.py:338 `ghat = self.nufft_proc.run([(t, y, int(nf))], **kwargs)[0]` -> cunfft.py:445 `memory = self.allocate(data)` -> NFFTMemory.allocate -> nfft_memory.py:122 `cufft.Plan(...)` + gpuarray.zeros x5 + pinned host_array, per template. exp8/exp5: 'n=600: current 0.91 ms (min 0.76) | reuse(zero+sync) 0.11 ms (min 0.09)'; 'n=5000: 1.43 (min 1.20) | 0.17 (min 0.12)'; 'n=50000: 14.53 (min 11.52) | 0.33 (min 0.24)'; 'allocate() alone 0.82-1.29 ms'. exp9: low-band 'max|cur-reuse|/rms=1.4e-06' (same as run-to-run atomic noise). The campaign runs 4982 templates per search (campaign.log), i.e. the allocation overhead is ~90% of its GPU time.
findings.expected_gain: 8x (n=600), 8x (n=5000), 44x (n=50000) per template on the measured 4090 relative timings; campaign-scale runs (~6M NFFTs) drop from ~1.5 h to ~10-15 min.
findings.reproduction: bash scratchpad/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch/lrtaud && python lrtaud_exp8_misc.py; python lrtaud_exp9.py'
findings.recommendation: In run(): allocate one NFFTMemory for (t, nf) (m from the largest expected ||y||_1, e.g. the template's) and per template set mem.y, mem.ghat_g.fill(0), run(memory=[mem]), mem.stream.synchronize(). Requires the cunfft fix below. A second-order win (medium effort): batch all epoch templates of a period as one complex GEMM with a precomputed phasor matrix, or reformulate the numerator in the time domain (z = whitened data computed once; per template a masked sum), which makes the search BLS-like in cost.

findings.title: NUFFT-LRT (all detectors) gives wrong results for absolute (BJD-scale) times: t is cast to float32 before folding and transforming
findings.method: nufft_lrt.NUFFTLRTAsyncProcess.run (detector='matched', 'marginal', 'sequential')
findings.evidence: nufft_lrt.py:411 `t = np.asarray(t, dtype=self.real_type)` (real_type=float32 by default) and :557 `phase = np.fmod(t - epoch, period) / period`; float32 spacing at 2457000.5 is 0.25 d (printed by h1b), so the box template is wrong (in-transit points 25 vs 36 correct, 575/600 membership agreement). Device results, N=600, 21 periods x 3 durations, same data at t~0..100 vs t+2457000.5: matched corr=-0.12 argmax DIFF; marginal corr=-0.12; sequential corr=-0.03 (h1). Fair comparison with epochs shifted consistently (h6): float32 offset 2.457e6 -> maxabs=5.42 rel=0.55 corr=0.717 argmax DIFF; offset 1000.5 already rel=8.7e-3; use_double=True -> rel 1.8e-9; host pre-subtracted epoch (t+0.5) -> rel 5e-4. The Jul-11 audit noted only the DEAD kernel folded float32 absolute times; the host path does the same.
findings.reproduction: bash pod.sh 'cd /workspace/cuvarbase && python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h6_lrt_bjd.py'  (and h1b_alignment.py section 'NUFFT-LRT at BJD')
findings.recommendation: In run(): t64 = np.asarray(t, float64); epoch0 = floor(t64.min()); t = (t64 - epoch0); epochs -= epoch0; keep the float32 cast only after that (mirrors utils.subtract_epoch as BLS/TLS do). Do the same in compute_nufft for the systematics basis path. Add a BJD-invariance test like test_bls.py:1598.

findings.title: NFFTAsyncProcess returns wrong magnitudes for absolute-time input (float32 phase factors on un-reduced 2*pi*t0*k arguments)
findings.method: cunfft.NFFTAsyncProcess.run / nfft_adjoint_async (public, in __all__)
findings.evidence: kernels/cunfft.cu:239-244 `FLT n0 = (x0 / sT) * ng; ... theta_k = (2.f * PI * n0 * (k0 + k)) / ng; G *= CMPLX(cos(theta_k), sin(theta_k))` with x0=min(t) (absolute) and --use_fast_math float32 trig: for t0~2.457e6 the argument is ~1e7 rad. Device: |ghat| for t vs t+2457000.5: maxabs=566 rel=0.94 corr=0.68 (use_double=False); use_double=True rel=3.9e-10; vs exact adjoint DFT at t~0: rel 2.1e-6, at t+1000.5: rel 3.4e-5. Host-side subtraction of floor(min(t)) restores rel=5.3e-7 (h9 nfft_epoch_fix). This is the second cause of the NUFFT-LRT failure above (compute_nufft passes absolute t).
findings.reproduction: bash pod.sh 'cd /workspace/cuvarbase && python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h1b_alignment.py'  (section 'NFFT magnitude at BJD') and 'python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h9_last.py nfft_epoch_fix'
findings.recommendation: Subtract floor(min(t)) (float64, host) in NFFTMemory.setdata / NFFTAsyncProcess.allocate and document that ghat phases are then relative to that epoch (or apply the exact float64 phase factor exp(2*pi*i*f_k*epoch) on the host if absolute-t phases are required). Add a BJD test for the NFFT.

findings.title: GPU Lomb-Scargle (default NFFT backend) is only accurate when the grid starts near zero frequency: garbage without warning for fmin >= fmax/2, and a 0.3-2% error floor everywhere with the default sigma=4
findings.method: LombScargleAsyncProcess.run / batched_run_const_nfreq / lomb_scargle_simple (use_fft=True default), nharmonics>=1
findings.evidence: The Gaussian-window NFFT is only accurate for modes |k| < n/2 with n = sigma*nf (cunfft.py:212 default sigma=4), but LS evaluates modes k0..k0+nf-1 after the nfft_shift, so accuracy needs (k0+nf) << sigma*nf/2. Device vs astropy LombScargle, N=600, T=100d, 5 samples/peak (h8 ls_k0): fmin=0.1,fmax=3 (k0/nf=0.03) rel=3.2e-3; fmin=1 (k0/nf=0.5) rel=2.1e-2; fmin=1.5 (k0/nf=1.0) rel=0.15 corr=0.988; fmin=2 (k0/nf=2) rel=1e12 corr=-0.02; fmin=5..10 rel=0.51 corr=0.96. Small grids fail the same way: nf<=8 with k0=50 returns the -1 sentinel at every frequency, nf=12-32 returns 1e11-1e23 (h5). Direct sums (use_fft=False) and use_cufinufft=True agree with astropy to 4.5e-5/1.2e-4 on the failing grid. sigma=8/16/32 reduce the k0/nf=2 error to 1.6e-2/8.3e-3/3.8e-3 (h9 ls_sigma_fix); m (8 vs 12) has no effect; sigma=2 gives rel 0.52 even at k0=50. lombscargle.py:589-596 has an `autoadjust_sigma` (sigma*(nf+k0)/nf) but only inside memory_requirement, never applied. Tests use lsrtol=lsatol=1e-2 (test_lombscargle.py:13-14), which hides the floor.
findings.reproduction: bash pod.sh 'cd /workspace/cuvarbase && python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h8_more.py ls_k0 && python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h9_last.py ls_sigma_fix && python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h7_followups.py ls_accuracy'
findings.recommendation: In LombScargleAsyncProcess.run/batched_run_const_nfreq choose the NFFT grid from the top mode: n >= 2*sigma0*(k0+nf) (i.e. sigma_eff = max(sigma, 4*(k0+nf)/nf)) so the evaluated band stays in the accurate half; raise or warn when the resulting grid would exceed memory; document the residual ~1e-3 error of the float32 NFFT path and point users at use_fft=False / use_cufinufft for fmin>0 grids. Tighten test tolerance to 1e-3 once fixed.

findings.title: Conditional entropy misbins the brightest point (bin index == mag_bins) in every kernel; the standard kernel additionally spills it into the next frequency's histogram and writes one element past the end of bins_g at the last frequency
findings.method: ConditionalEntropyAsyncProcess.run/large_run/batched_run_const_nfreq (weighted=False; use_fast True and False)
findings.evidence: ce_memory.py:317 `y = np.floor(y * self.mag_bins).astype(self.ytype)` after `y = (y - y0) / yscale` puts the maximum point at exactly 1.0 -> bin index mag_bins (out of [0, mag_bins-1]); ce.cu:93/98 (`m0 = y[j_data]`, `atomicInc(&bin[offset + posmod(n,NPHASE)*NMAG + m])`) and :178/183, :304/309 use it unclamped, so the count lands at flat index (n+1)*NMAG (phase n+1, mag 0), and for n = NPHASE-1 at NMAG*NPHASE, i.e. block_bin_phi[0] in the shared-memory kernels or the NEXT frequency's bin[0] in the global kernel (out of bounds at the last frequency). Device proof: an independent CPU CE reference with the point clipped into the top bin differs from the GPU by rel 6-9e-3 (N=600) and 28-30% (N=5), while a reference that emulates the spill matches the fast kernel to 2.1e-7 and the standard kernel (with the next-frequency spill) to 3.1e-7 (h7 ce_spill, h8 ce_spill2). Symptom visible from the outside: the standard kernel's output depends on the ORDER of the frequency array (reversed grid: maxabs 7e-3 vs base, h2f 'ce' unsorted) whereas ce_fast is order-invariant.
findings.reproduction: bash pod.sh 'cd /workspace/cuvarbase && python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h7_followups.py ce_spill && python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h8_more.py ce_spill2'
findings.recommendation: ce_memory.py:317: `y = np.minimum(np.floor(y * self.mag_bins), self.mag_bins - 1).astype(self.ytype)` (and clamp m0 in histogram_data_weighted); optionally guard `m < NMAG` in the kernels. Add a regression test comparing against a CPU reference at N=5 where the effect is 30%.

findings.title: ConditionalEntropyAsyncProcess.preallocate() never uploads the frequency grid, so run() after preallocate() evaluates every frequency at f=0 (constant output); with streams=None the results are also read before the D2H copy completes (stale data)
findings.method: ConditionalEntropyAsyncProcess.preallocate + run
findings.evidence: ce.py:414-458 preallocate builds ConditionalEntropyMemory(..., freqs=freqs) and calls mem.allocate(**kwargs) but never mem.transfer_freqs_to_gpu() (batched_run_const_nfreq does, ce.py:683); run() with memory given (ce.py:516-519) only calls set_gpu_arrays_to_zero/setdata. Device: after preallocate(max_nobs=900, freqs=F) the returned CE has std=0 and freqs_g.get()[:3] == [0,0,0] (h7 ce_prealloc). Second defect: ce.py:452 `stream = None if streams is None else streams[i]` -> memory.stream=None, so transfer_ce_to_cpu's get_async runs on the null stream and proc.finish() (which syncs only proc.streams) returns before the copy lands: after a manual freq upload, the 2nd LC (N=300 after N=900) read after finish() is rel 0.26 / argmax DIFF vs fresh, and exact after cuda.Context.synchronize() (h8 prealloc_race). LombScargleAsyncProcess.preallocate has the same stream=None pattern (lombscargle.py:711) but did not show stale reads in the same test.
findings.reproduction: bash pod.sh 'cd /workspace/cuvarbase && python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h7_followups.py ce_prealloc && python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h8_more.py prealloc_race'
findings.recommendation: preallocate(): call mem.transfer_freqs_to_gpu() after allocate, and default streams to self.streams (create them) instead of None; make run() upload freqs when a memory's freqs differ; have finish() also synchronize memory streams (or Context.synchronize() when any memory has stream=None). Add a preallocate-then-run regression test with two LCs of different length.

findings.title: No input validation on any GPU entry point: NaN/inf/zero uncertainties give silent garbage or silent sentinels, and NaN q-bounds / NaN frequencies / Keplerian grids with N<5 raise an illegal memory access that permanently kills the CUDA context of the process
findings.method: all public entry points (tabulated per method in the evidence)
findings.evidence: Isolated per-entry-point runs (h2_edge_iso.out), one poisoned point out of 600 unless noted. SILENT GARBAGE (finite output, rel diff ~1 vs the point-dropped reference): eebls_gpu_fast/optimized/adaptive/eebls_gpu/eebls_gpu_custom with NaN in t (rel 1.0); sparse_bls_gpu/cpu with dy=0, dy=NaN, y=NaN, y=inf, t=NaN (rel 1.0; sparse_bls_gpu also silently accepts len(y)!=len(t)); eebls_gpu_batch with dy=0/dy=NaN/y=NaN (rel 1.0, because bls_memory.py:292 `if self.yy[i] > 0` skips the normalization when yy is NaN); all NFFT-based Lomb-Scargle paths with dy=0, dy=NaN, y=NaN, y=inf (power == -1 sentinel at every frequency, or corr 0.007 for dy=1e-9; cunfft.cu:160 `if (!(isnan(dg)||isinf(dg))) ... else break` silently drops NaN contributions from the yw grid but not the w grid); CE standard/fast/batched/large with dy=0/y=NaN (rel 0.03, argmax DIFF); TLS fast/batch/transit with dy=0 (chi2 rel 1.3e3 via tls.py:1156 `s2 = dy64*dy64 + 1e-10`); NUFFT-LRT with dy is ignored, N=1 raises a broadcast error. SILENT NaN: eebls_gpu_fast with dy=0/NaN, y=NaN/inf, constant y (RuntimeWarning at bls.py:561 only), N=1; PDM all kinds with any NaN/dy=0. CONTEXT-KILLING (sticky 'illegal memory access', every later GPU call in the process fails with 'cuMemAlloc failed: an illegal memory access'): eebls_gpu_fast with per-frequency qmin/qmax containing NaN (h7 nan_q; bls.py:579 casts 1/NaN to uint32 -> nbf/nb0 of 0 or 2^31 -> division by zero and out-of-range shared-memory indexing in bls.cu:70-90), eebls_transit_gpu(use_fast=True) with N<=4 (fmin_transit bls.py:256 gives q=5/N>1 -> freq_transit NaN -> freqs=[nan], q=[nan]) or with a NaN in t; eebls_gpu_fast with qmax>=1 or qmax=inf returns finite garbage (nb0=0). Also LS 'freqs' as a plain Python list in batched_run_const_nfreq -> 'number of frequency grids (300) does not match number of lightcurves (1)'; integer dy -> 'Integers to negative integer powers are not allowed' (BLS/LS/PDM); empty freqs -> 'required argument is not an integer' (BLS/CE); tls_search_batch with a period <= 0 -> 'nbins must be a power of two' while tls_search_gpu silently returns chi2 for period 0; LS freqs of length 1 -> IndexError. Only sparse_bls_* (bls.py:1803 _validate_q_bounds) and tls_search_batch (length/emptiness) validate anything.
findings.reproduction: bash pod.sh 'bash /workspace/scratch/xcut/h2_driver.sh' ; bash pod.sh 'cd /workspace/cuvarbase && python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h7_followups.py nanfreq nan_q; python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h4_state.py sticky_nanfreq'
findings.recommendation: Add one shared validator (utils._validate_lightcurve(t,y,dy, min_n) and _validate_grid(freqs/periods)) called at the top of every public entry point: equal lengths, all finite, dy>0, N>=2 (N>=min_obs for Keplerian grids), frequencies finite and >0, q bounds finite with 0<qmin<=qmax<=1, and extend _validate_q_bounds to the eebls_gpu_fast/batch paths before any uint32 cast. Raise ValueError with the offending index. This also removes every context-killing path found.

findings.title: GPU Lomb-Scargle silently evaluates a non-uniform frequency grid on the implied uniform grid df*(k0+arange(nf)) (only freqs[0] and freqs[1] are inspected)
findings.method: LombScargleAsyncProcess.run / batched_run_const_nfreq (use_fft=True and False)
findings.evidence: lombscargle.py:35-43 check_k0 only tests freqs[0] against k0*df with df=freqs[1]-freqs[0]; the kernels use `fmin + i*df` (lomb.cu:181) / the FFT index. Device: a grid that is uniform for its first two points and then 3x coarser passes check_k0 and returns power that has corr=0.017 with astropy at the user's frequencies but matches the GPU power at the implied uniform grid to 1.2e-7 (h5 'non-uniform grid'). The constraint is stated in the run() docstring but never enforced.
findings.recommendation: In check_k0 also require np.allclose(np.diff(freqs), df, rtol=1e-6) and len(freqs)>=2 (raise ValueError naming the first non-uniform index); document that non-uniform grids need use_fft=False.

findings.title: eebls_gpu and eebls_gpu_custom size freq_batch_size from 90% of free GPU memory without capping at len(freqs): every call zero-fills ~22 GB of scratch, is ~9x slower than necessary, and is OOM-prone on shared GPUs
findings.method: bls.eebls_gpu (standard BLS with solutions), bls.eebls_gpu_custom, hence eebls_transit/eebls_transit_gpu default path
findings.evidence: bls.py:1504 (and :1247 for _custom) `freq_batch_size = int(float(max_memory - mem0) / (mem_per_f))` with max_memory = 0.9*free and no min(..., len(freqs)); then 5 streams x 4 gpuarray.zeros(gs) with gs = freq_batch_size*nbins_tot*noverlap. Device (h9 bls_std_alloc): for a 300-frequency grid the computed freq_batch_size is 169027 (21.99 GB of grid arrays); call times with precompiled functions: default 0.373/0.401/0.391 s vs freq_batch_size=300 0.043/0.042/0.043 s (identical results, rel 3.4e-7) vs max_memory=2e8 0.044 s; eebls_gpu_custom for 100 freqs takes 1.58 s (its sizing would be 2.7M frequencies per batch). One nf=1e6 call during the concurrent campaign failed with 'cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory' (h3 bls_bignf) and succeeded when re-run alone. Timings are repeated relative measurements on a shared RTX 4090.
findings.expected_gain: ~9x per call for eebls_gpu/eebls_gpu_custom at typical grid sizes (0.39 s -> 0.043 s measured), removal of the 22 GB transient allocation; basis: repeated timings with functions= precompiled
findings.recommendation: Cap: freq_batch_size = max(1, min(len(freqs), computed)) in both functions; also use a fixed default memory budget (e.g. min(0.9*free, 2 GB)) rather than all free memory. Also route these two functions through _get_cached_kernels instead of compile_bls per call.

findings.title: eebls_gpu (default eebls_transit path for ndata>=500) sizes bin buffers with a non-upper-bound and writes out of bounds with per-frequency q arrays + batching
findings.method: Reproduced the crash on device, replicated the sizing arithmetic in pure numpy, confirmed OOB with compute-sanitizer
files: cuvarbase/kernels/bls_common.cuh bin_and_phase_fold_bst_multifreq (atomicAdd into yw_bin/w_bin at offset i_freq*nbins_tot*noverlap)
findings.evidence: HAT-like Keplerian grid (keplerian_freq_grid(0.5,100,3650), first 20000 freqs, qmin=0.5q, qmax=2q), ndata=600, max_memory=1.5e9: global nbins0_max=81 nbinsf_max=570 nbins_tot_max=2565 -> freq_batch_size=2435, gs=18,737,325 floats/array; batch 0 has nbins0=131 nbinsf=570 nbins_tot=2706 -> all_bins=19,767,330 > gs. Plain run: 'pycuda._driver.LogicError: cuMemcpyDtoH failed: an illegal memory access was encountered' (bls.py:1614 bls_best_q.get()). compute-sanitizer memcheck: 'Invalid __global__ atomic of size 4 bytes at bin_and_phase_fold_bst_multifreq+0x14d0 ... Address ... is out of bounds and is 2854081 bytes after the nearest allocation ... of size 74949300 bytes' (=gs*4). Local replication (local_eebls_gpu_sizing.py): full ZTF/HAT/Kepler grids at 1.5 GB and 20 GB caps happen not to overflow (worst batch/global ratio 0.80-0.95) - i.e. safety depends on free device memory and grid extent; a small overrun that lands inside the adjacent stream buffer would corrupt results silently instead of faulting. Existing tests (test_bls.py:425-470 test_transit) use fmin=0.9f..fmax=1.1f grids where batch and global ranges coincide.
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python repro_oob.py 600 1.5e9'   (prints the per-batch arithmetic and the LogicError);  sanitizer: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && /usr/local/cuda-12.4/bin/compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --print-limit 2 python repro_oob_cubin.py 600 1.5e9';  local arithmetic: /usr/bin/python3 <scratchpad>/blsperf/local_eebls_gpu_sizing.py
findings.recommendation: Compute the batch table (imin, imax, nbins0, nbinsf, nbins_tot) up front and size gs = freq_batch_size * max_over_batches(nbins_tot) * noverlap (or derive freq_batch_size from that max); add an assertion all_bins <= gs before every launch; add a regression test with a Keplerian q array, a narrow max_memory and a grid whose batches start at different nbins0 (the repro config).

findings.title: eebls_gpu collapses per-frequency q bounds to batch-wide [min qmin, max qmax]: eebls_transit's default standard path does not honour the Keplerian duration constraint it documents
findings.method: Device experiment comparing eebls_gpu vs eebls_gpu_fast on the same Keplerian TESS grid; code inspection
files: cuvarbase/bls.py:1476-1490 (locext(min/max, qmin/qmax) over the whole grid)
cuvarbase/kernels/bls_common.cuh bin_and_phase_fold_bst_multifreq / store_best_sols (scalar nbins0, nbinsf per launch)
cuvarbase/bls.py:2261-2266 eebls_transit docstring ('The sparse-BLS path ... honors the same per-frequency Keplerian qmin_fac/qmax_fac duration bounds as the standard path')
findings.evidence: TESS-like (20000 x 1788, qmin=0.5 q_kep, qmax=2 q_kep, one batch): eebls_gpu reported solutions with q in [0.0079, 0.25] while per-frequency bounds are e.g. [0.0067,0.0267] at the lowest frequency and [0.0616,0.246] at the highest; 660/1788 (36.9%) solutions lie outside their own frequency's [qmin,qmax]; power_std > 1.01*power_fast at 1023/1788 frequencies, max ratio 3.63, corr(std,fast)=0.989 (argmax identical in this injected case). With default max_memory the whole grid is one batch, so every frequency is searched over the union of all durations; with batching the searched range is batch-dependent (undocumented).
findings.recommendation: Either (a) pass per-frequency nbins0/nbinsf arrays into bin_and_phase_fold_bst_multifreq and store_best_sols (as the fast kernels already do) so eebls_gpu honours the bounds, or (b) document loudly on eebls_gpu/eebls_transit that array q bounds are reduced to the batch-wide range on the standard path, and make eebls_transit default to the fast (bound-honouring) kernel and obtain (q,phi) solutions by a follow-up eebls_gpu_custom/single_bls at the top-K frequencies.

findings.title: eebls_gpu_fast_adaptive and eebls_transit(use_optimized=True) never use the fused-noverlap kernel: 2 launches and 2.0-2.5x the GPU time of eebls_gpu_fast on identical inputs
findings.method: Launch counting through proxied prepared functions + CUDA-event timing on device
files: cuvarbase/bls.py:1138 (adaptive: _get_cached_kernels(block_size, use_optimized, [fname]) - fused name not requested)
cuvarbase/bls.py:1002 docstring 'Expected speedup: 20-30% over standard version'
findings.evidence: Kernel launches per call (parity_paths.py / prof_stages2.py): fast -> full_bls_no_sol_fused x1; optimized -> fused x1; adaptive -> full_bls_no_sol_optimized x2; eebls_transit(use_optimized=True) -> optimized x2. Event GPU time (min of 9): ZTF fast 0.196 ms vs adaptive 0.389 ms; TESS 0.197 vs 0.480 ms; HAT 8.28 vs 20.2 ms. Whole-call medians (ZTF): adaptive 2.41 ms vs fast 1.26 ms. _get_cached_kernels(256, True, ['full_bls_no_sol_optimized']) has no 'full_bls_no_sol_fused' key (printed False). Results still agree (max |dP| 2.3e-6, argmax same) - it is purely a speed regression.
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python parity_paths.py'  -> see *_launches and kernel_only_ms; also prof2_*.json adaptive_kernel_events
findings.recommendation: Request ['full_bls_no_sol_optimized' or fname, 'full_bls_no_sol_fused'] in both call sites (one-line change each); add a test asserting one launch of the fused kernel for adaptive/use_optimized at noverlap=2; retire the '20-30%' claim (both paths now run the same fused kernel: 0.205 vs 0.196 ms).

findings.title: Naive eebls_gpu_fast path allocates 6 pinned host buffers per call, 3-4 of which are immediately discarded (freqs/nbins replaced in setdata, bls replaced in transfer_data_to_cpu): 6x on ZTF-scale calls, 1.5x on HAT-scale
findings.method: Stage decomposition + prototype (monkeypatched allocate_host_arrays that pins only t/yw/w) with bitwise comparison
files: cuvarbase/bls.py:561 transfer_data_to_cpu (self.bls = self.bls_g.get()/self.yy when stream is None, the default)
cuvarbase/bls.py:724-728 (BLSMemory.fromdata per call when memory is None)
findings.evidence: After setdata: type(mem.freqs.base)=ndarray, nbinsf=ndarray (not PagelockedHostAllocation); after transfer_data_to_cpu: bls=ndarray. Pinned alloc+free costs ~2.6-6.5 ms per buffer regardless of size on this host (host_proto.py: 4 floats 2.57 ms min, 301000 floats 3.77 ms; pageable np.zeros 0.001-0.04 ms). Stock BLSMemory(ndata,nfreq): ZTF 3.31 ms min, HAT 8.45 ms; lean (t/yw/w pinned only): 0.05 / 0.10 ms. Whole eebls_gpu_fast naive call, min of 15: ZTF stock 5.55 ms -> lean 0.86 ms (6.4x); HAT 23.7 -> 15.5 ms (1.5x); TESS 1.75 -> 1.74 (pinned allocs happened to be cheap in that section). Periodogram differences vs stock 6e-8..1.2e-7 = the kernel's own run-to-run atomic nondeterminism (stock vs stock: 6e-8..9e-8). Naive-vs-reuse gap that remains after this (auto-reusable memory would close it): ZTF 0.86 vs 0.40-0.44 ms; HAT 15.5 vs 10.7-12 ms.
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python host_proto.py'  (see *_BLSMemory_init, stock_fast_naive vs lean_alloc_fast_naive, pinned_alloc_free_*)
findings.recommendation: In allocate_host_arrays pin only t/yw/w (or write freqs/nbins INTO the pinned buffers with slice assignment and use bls_g.get(ary=self.bls)); additionally keep a small module-level LRU of BLSMemory keyed by (max_ndata, max_nfreqs, stream) so the documented 'reuse' speed becomes the default. Bit-parity: yes (only host staging changes).

findings.title: sparse_bls_kernel decodes each pair index with an O(N) while-loop -> O(N^3/blockDim) per frequency; incremental decode is bit-identical and 5-30x faster
findings.method: Patched-kernel prototype compiled from the shipped source, bit-level comparison of powers and (q,phi), CUDA-event timing (min of 7) at N=150/300/499, 60K-frequency ZTF grid
findings.evidence: sparse_proto2.py (stock vs incremental decode, same thread<->pair assignment): N=150 Keplerian bounds bs=64 41.5 -> 5.45 ms (7.6x), bs=256 18.7 -> 3.58 ms (5.2x); N=300 bs=64 170 -> 10.5 ms (16x); N=499 bs=64 811 -> 26.9 ms (30x), unbounded q: N=499 829 -> 50 ms (16.5x). bit_identical=True for powers, q and phi in all 18 configs once the wrapped-section start index preserves the stock thread mapping (tie-breaking between complement boxes). Stock is also 1.5-2.2x faster at block_size=256 than the default 64 (N=150: 18.7 vs 41.5 ms). Note both stock and patched differ from sparse_bls_cpu identically (max |dP| 0.0208, corr 0.99959, argmax same) - pre-existing float32-vs-float64 prefix-sum gap.
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python sparse_proto2.py'  (patched Step 7 is inline in the script; json in sparse_proto2.json)
findings.recommendation: Replace the per-pair while-loop decode with the incremental (i, idx) advance shown in sparse_proto2.py (keep p0 = (tid - total_nonwrap) mod blockDim for the wrapped section so solutions stay bit-identical); change the default block_size to 256; consider skipping j beyond the qmax window when sorted phases make the bound monotone (further 2-3x for Keplerian bounds, not prototyped).

findings.title: eebls_transit's default paths recompile kernels every call: compile_sparse_bls / compile_bls (eebls_gpu, eebls_gpu_custom) bypass the LRU cache, and pycuda runs an nvcc --preprocess subprocess on every SourceModule even on a cache hit (0.4-1.3 s per call)
findings.method: Stage timing (wall vs process_time) on device + pycuda source/traceback inspection
files: cuvarbase/bls.py:2101-2103 (sparse_bls_gpu: kernel = compile_sparse_bls(...) when kernel is None)
cuvarbase/bls.py:1469-1470 (eebls_gpu: compile_bls(**kwargs) when functions is None)
/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/pycuda/compiler.py:90 (checksum.update(preprocess_source(...)) -> nvcc --preprocess subprocess before the disk-cache lookup)
findings.evidence: prof_stages2: compile_bls() warm (31 cubins already in ~/.cache/pycuda/compiler-cache-v1): wall 418-699 ms, process CPU 12-13 ms (the rest is the nvcc subprocess); compile_sparse_bls(block_size=64) warm: wall 903-997 ms, CPU 14 ms. transit_default.py: eebls_transit(t,y,dy) DEFAULT at ZTF (150 pts): 3.2 s per call (grid 117K freqs), TESS (20K pts): 1.34 s per call vs use_fast=True 0.20 s; with freqs given the TESS standard path still costs 1.58 s (compile 0.62 s + eebls_gpu). The fast/batch paths use _get_cached_kernels and pay 0.004 ms.
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python transit_default.py'; per-call compile cost: prof2_ZTF_TESS.json ['ZTF']['sparse']['compile_sparse_bls(per-call)'] and ['std']['compile_bls(per-call, pycuda cache warm)']
findings.recommendation: Route compile_sparse_bls (key: block_size, use_simple) and compile_bls for eebls_gpu/eebls_gpu_custom/hone_solution through _kernel_cache exactly like _get_cached_batch_kernels; this removes ~0.5-1.3 s per eebls_transit call on both default branches. Bit-parity: yes.

findings.title: transit_autofreq / keplerian_freq_grid build the frequency grid with a scalar Python while-loop: 0.2-1.2 s per eebls_transit call (default freqs=None), dwarfing the GPU work
findings.method: Local numpy timing of the shipped functions (copied verbatim) vs a vectorized form; device timing of eebls_transit stages
files: cuvarbase/bls.py:2286-2290 eebls_transit (calls transit_autofreq every call when freqs is None)
findings.evidence: Local (M-series Mac, uncontended): transit_autofreq with eebls_transit defaults (qmin_fac=0.5): ZTF-like T=730 d 118,617 freqs 220 ms; HAT-like T=3650 d 919,520 freqs 1156 ms; Kepler-like 366,401 freqs 470 ms; TESS 5,456 freqs 6.9 ms. keplerian_freq_grid(0.5..100 d): 77 / 381 / 152 ms. A vectorized cumulative-integral form of the same ODE (df/dn = qmin_fac q(f)/(OS T)) takes 3-6 ms and reproduces the grid count to within 2 frequencies (not bit-identical: Euler recursion vs integral). On the throttled pod the same call took 2.8 s (ZTF) and the ZTF eebls_transit default call 3.2 s, of which the sparse kernel itself is 20 ms.
findings.recommendation: Vectorize the grid (closed-form cumulative integral, documented as the Ofir-2014 spacing) or, if the exact recursion must be preserved, memoize the grid on (fmin, fmax, T, rho, samples_per_peak, qmin_fac) since survey runs share it; document that passing freqs= to eebls_transit avoids the cost. Not bit-parity for the grid itself if vectorized (2 fewer/more frequencies at the top end) - keep the recursion behind a flag if grids must stay identical.

findings.title: eebls_gpu, eebls_gpu_custom and sparse_bls_cpu still use np.dot for the per-LC normalization: the OpenBLAS threadpool CFS-throttle cliff the July campaign fixed for setdata is still on the default eebls_transit standard path
findings.method: Device experiment: same eebls_gpu call with and without OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1, cgroup cpu.stat throttle counters
files: cuvarbase/bls.py:1514-1517 (eebls_gpu: ybar = np.dot(w, y); YY = np.dot(...))
findings.evidence: blas_throttle.py, TESS-like (20000 pts): eebls_gpu prologue (np.power/np.dot x2) median 0.41 ms with OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 vs 92.2 ms in the pod's default env, with 27 extra cgroup throttle events (+217 s throttled_usec) in 50 calls; whole eebls_gpu call median 329 ms (pinned) vs 599 ms (default env). Pod: 96 visible CPUs, cpu.max 1020000/100000 (10.2 cores).
