findings.recommendation: Replace the three np.dot pairs with the einsum form already used in BLSMemory.setdata/_chi2_null (last-ulp float64 ordering change only), and note the residual paths in the SUMMARY claim.

findings.title: Lomb-Scargle NFFT path shares precompute_psi tables between the yw grid and the 2x larger w grid -> systematic 0.3-3% bias in the periodogram
findings.method: Device experiment: LS vs astropy exact (method='cython') at N=300 (nf=3750, 15000) and N=1000/nf=365000, sweeping sigma, m, use_double, fast_grid=False, and a monkeypatch that gives the w grid its own psi tables (LombScargleMemory.allocate_grids -> nfft_mem_w.precomp_psi=True + allocate_precomp_psi).
findings.evidence: lombscargle_memory.py:186-190 `# Only one precomp psi needed / self.nfft_mem_w.precomp_psi = False / self.nfft_mem_w.q1 = self.nfft_mem_yw.q1 ...` while allocate_grids gives the two grids different sizes (`allocate_grid(nf=fft_size - k0)` vs `allocate_grid(nf=2 * fft_size - k0)`, lines 193-194) and cunfft.cu:106-108 makes q1/q2 depend on `modflt(ng * xg, 1.f)` i.e. on the grid size ng. ls_psi_bug.py output (nyquist_factor=5, nf=3750): default sigma=4 max|d|=7.12e-03 (rel@peak 3.4e-3); use_double 8.31e-03; sigma=2 2.59e-02; fast_grid=False (no psi) 1.50e-05; PATCHED own psi for w-grid 1.32e-05. nyquist_factor=20: default 2.57e-03 -> patched 3.51e-05. At survey scale (ls_profile2.py, N=1000 nf=365000): rel@peak 3.76e-04 shipped -> 1.60e-06 patched. Error is independent of m (m=8 vs 6 identical, 7.12e-03) and of float64, exactly as the wrong-fractional-offset mechanism predicts. Direct sums (5.05e-05) and cufinufft (8.40e-05) are unaffected. The existing tests use atol=rtol=1e-2 (test_lombscargle.py:13-14) and cannot see it.
findings.recommendation: In LombScargleMemory.allocate_grids give nfft_mem_w its own q1/q2 (keep precomp_psi=True and call allocate_precomp_psi(n0=...) for it; q3 can stay shared since it is grid-independent), and let nfft_adjoint_async run precompute_psi for both grids. Then tighten test_lombscargle tolerances to ~1e-4 (the patched path reaches 1.3e-5 vs astropy). Alternative: run precompute_psi for the w grid into separate buffers only when its n differs.

findings.title: use_double=True Lomb-Scargle/NFFT is less accurate than float32: fast_gaussian_grid uses float32 floorf() for the grid index in DOUBLE_PRECISION
findings.method: Device experiment with the psi fix applied so only this error remains: LS(use_double) vs astropy exact at nf=3750 and 365000 (N=1000, T=1095 d, fmax=100/d); then recompiled an in-memory copy of cunfft.cu with `floorf(ng * xval - m)` -> `floor(ng * xval - m)` (monkeypatched cunfft._module_reader; on-disk tree untouched).
findings.evidence: cunfft.cu:151 `int u = (int) floorf(ng * xval - m);` (float32 floor of a double argument) while precompute_psi (cunfft.cu:108) uses double `modflt(ng * xg, 1.f)`, so for ng*xval ~ 1e5-1e6 the float32 rounding moves the floor by one cell for a fraction of points and the Gaussian weights are applied one grid cell off. ls_floorf.py: nf=3750 f64 shipped @peak max|d|=1.65e-03 (rel 9.8e-02) -> floorf->floor 6.68e-09 (rel 4.0e-07); nf=365000 f64 shipped top-band max|d|=1.89e-03 (rel-to-local-max 1.2e-01) -> 9.36e-09 (5.8e-07); float32 shipped is 2.77e-04 / 2.95e-04, i.e. the shipped double path is 6x worse than float32 at the peak and 6x worse at the top of the band. ls_double.py shows the same at nf=50000 and 1e6 (f64 top-band 1.6e-03 / 1.44e-03 vs f32 3.3e-04 / 2.7e-04). estimate_m's docstring (cunfft.py:280-300) promises ~1e-10 tracking in double; that was only true for the standalone NFFT test configuration.
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python ls_floorf.py'  (ls_floorf.py and ls_double.py in the audit-tls-ls-lrt scratch dir)
findings.recommendation: Replace `floorf` with `floor` (type-generic under FLT) in fast_gaussian_grid; audit the other float32 intrinsics/literals in the DOUBLE_PRECISION build (`1.f`, `2.f` literals are harmless, `floorf` is not). Add a test that runs the LS use_double path at a long baseline / high fmax against astropy exact with rtol ~1e-6.

findings.title: NUFFT-LRT casts absolute observation times to float32: BJD-scale input silently returns the wrong period and half the SNR
findings.method: Device experiment: same light curve (N=600, 60 d baseline, injected P=5.3 d box) run through NUFFTLRTAsyncProcess.run with t and with t+2457000 (epochs shifted identically).
findings.evidence: nufft_lrt.py:411 `t = np.asarray(t, dtype=self.real_type)` and :333 (compute_nufft) cast to float32 before anything is epoch-subtracted; _generate_template (:557) folds the float32 times; NFFTMemory.fromdata (:246) also stores float32 t. float32 spacing at 2457000 is 0.25 d (np.spacing). lrt_detA.py part (c): relative t -> best P=5.300, epoch=1.178, SNR=16.61; BJD t -> best P=5.900, epoch=2.356, SNR=8.04; corr(snr grids)=0.50, max|diff|=12.7. Unlike BLS (utils.subtract_epoch) and the TLS fast path, nothing in this module subtracts an epoch.
findings.recommendation: In run(): `t, epoch = subtract_epoch(t)` in float64 before any cast, shift `epochs` by the same epoch (and document that returned/expected epochs are relative to floor(min(t))); apply the same to the systematics basis path (it only depends on ordering, so no change) and to compute_nufft callers. Add a BJD-scale regression test like TLS's.

findings.title: PERF: Baluev FAP is evaluated over the whole frequency grid although only fap[best_index] is used (36 ms vs 0.23 ms per LC at nf=365K)
findings.method: Device timing (medians of 5) of fap_baluev on the full array vs the scalar at the argmax; end-to-end batched_run_const_nfreq with/without only_return_best_freqs.
findings.evidence: lombscargle.py:981-982 `fap = fap_baluev(batch[i][0], batch[i][2], p[mask], np.max(freqs[mask])); significance = 1. - fap[best_index]`. ls_profile.py (N=1000, nf=365000): fap_baluev over full array 35.96 ms; scalar at best 0.227 ms; batched_run_const_nfreq 1 LC/call 36.1 ms -> 76.4 ms with only_return_best_freqs. Also `p[mask]`/`freqs[mask]` copies cost 0.47 ms per LC when no mask is given.
findings.expected_gain: ~36 ms per LC removed (2x on the 1-LC-per-call path; the documented '50-70% FAP overhead' becomes <1%); basis: measured full-array vs scalar fap_baluev at nf=365K.
findings.recommendation: Compute `fap_baluev(t, dy, p[best_index], fmax)` on the scalar; skip the mask indexing when ignore_freq_mask is None. No parity risk (identical value: 1.873e-137 both ways).

findings.title: PERF: NFFT grid sizes sigma*nf hit cuFFT's worst case (large prime factors); padding to next_fast_len makes the FFT 10x faster and the whole LS run 1.8x faster
findings.method: Device timing of cuFFT C2C at the shipped sizes vs 5-smooth / power-of-2 sizes; end-to-end run() with NFFTMemory.allocate_grid monkeypatched to next_fast_len; parity vs shipped and vs astropy exact.
findings.evidence: nfft_memory.py:119 and :192 `self.n = int(self.sigma * self.nf)`; for nf=365000, k0=1 the w grid is n=2,920,004 = 4*730001 (730001 has a large prime factor). ls_profile.py: cuFFT n=2920004 0.826 ms vs n=2927232 (next_fast_len) 0.079 ms vs 4194304 0.083 ms; n=1460000 0.076 ms vs 1463616 0.053 ms; the w-NFFT is 47% of the 1.6 ms run. ls_profile2.py (2): run 1.45 ms -> 0.81 ms padded; LombScargleMemory alloc (incl. plans) 18.1 -> 4.0 ms; max|p_pad - p_orig| = 8.8e-4 and the padded result is slightly closer to astropy exact (3.47e-4 vs 4.00e-4). The kernels use memory.n consistently (grid, shift, normalize), so any n >= sigma*nf is valid.
findings.expected_gain: 1.8x on LS run() at survey nf (1.45 -> 0.81 ms/LC) and 4.5x on per-call allocation; basis: measured with the padded allocate_grid.
findings.recommendation: In NFFTMemory.allocate_grid/allocate use `self.n = scipy.fft.next_fast_len(int(self.sigma*self.nf))` (or a 2^a3^b5^c7^d search) and update memory_requirement accordingly. Parity risk: results change at the 1e-3 level (toward the exact answer); regression tests keyed on bit-exact LS output need re-baselining.

findings.title: PERF: batched_run_const_nfreq rebuilds LombScargleMemory (pinned buffers, device arrays, two cuFFT plans) on every call: 18 ms of setup per 1.6 ms of compute
findings.method: Device timing: batched_run_const_nfreq with 1 and 16 LCs per call, LombScargleMemory.allocate alone, cuFFT plan creation alone, run() with preallocated memory.
findings.evidence: lombscargle.py:945-953 constructs `memory = [LombScargleMemory(...)]` and calls `mem.allocate(nf=nf)` inside every call. ls_profile.py: 1 LC/call 36.1 ms; 16 LC/call 4.77 ms/LC; alloc 18.2 ms (cuFFT plans: n_yw 1.05 ms, n_w 13.2 ms - Bluestein planning, see the padding finding); run() with preallocated memory 1.57 ms. The docstring already warns about this for batch_size>1, but the per-call rebuild happens for batch_size=1 too, and `self.memory` from preallocate() is ignored by this method.
findings.expected_gain: Up to ~20x for callers that invoke the method per light curve (36 -> ~2 ms); ~3x at 16 LC/call; basis: measured alloc vs run() split.
findings.recommendation: Cache the LombScargleMemory list on the process keyed by (nf, k0, n0_buffer, use_fft, nharmonics, use_double, batch_size) and reuse it across calls (grow n0_buffer when needed); or honor self.memory from preallocate(). Combine with next_fast_len padding to cut plan creation to ~1 ms. No parity risk.

findings.title: PERF: tls_transit builds an (nperiods x n_durations) duration table via duration_grid_keplerian that the fast path never uses: 96 ms of a 200 ms Kepler-4yr call, 25 of 44 ms at TESS-year
findings.method: Device stage profile of tls_transit (monkeypatched timers, sync'd kernels) plus direct timing of duration_grid_keplerian vs q_transit at 2486/42001/171688 periods.
findings.evidence: tls.py:953-956 `durations, dur_counts, q_values = tls_grids.duration_grid_keplerian(...)` followed by `qmin = q_values * qmin_fac` - only q_values is used; tls_grids.py:348-353 materializes a 10**(...) table and `list(dur_2d.astype(np.float32))`. tls_profile2.py (a): kepler-4yr nperiods=171688 duration_grid_keplerian 96.1 ms vs q_transit 3.4 ms; tess-yr 24.6 vs 0.85 ms; tess-ffi 1.19 vs 0.06 ms. tls_profile.py kepler-4yr single tls_transit: total 200 ms, KERNEL search 63 ms, 'unaccounted' 107 ms (this table).
findings.expected_gain: ~1.9x on single-LC tls_transit at Kepler-4yr (200 -> ~105 ms), ~2.3x at TESS-year (44 -> ~20 ms); basis: measured table cost vs call total.
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python tls_profile2.py' (section a) and 'python tls_profile.py'
findings.recommendation: Call tls_grids.q_transit directly in tls_transit (as tls_search_batch already does). No parity risk.

findings.title: PERF: tls_search_batch's ThreadPoolExecutor for per-LC statistics is counterproductive (GIL contention): 1 worker is 2.1x faster at TESS-FFI scale, 1.4x at TESS-year
findings.method: Device timing of tls_search_batch on 64 tess-ffi / 16 tess-yr light curves with os.cpu_count monkeypatched to 1 vs default (min(8, cpu)); thread-summed stage timers.
findings.evidence: tls.py:1617-1625 `n_workers = min(8, os.cpu_count() or 1, nc)` -> ThreadPoolExecutor over _finish_lc. tls_profile2.py (b): tess-ffi 64 LCs: 8 workers 101.6 ms (1.59 ms/LC) vs 1 worker 47.9 ms (0.75 ms/LC); tess-yr 16 LCs: 216 vs 154 ms. tls_profile.py: stats(medfilt etc) thread-summed 356 ms per 64-LC call (5.6 ms per LC) vs 0.6 ms when run single-threaded; KERNEL search is only 5.9 ms per 64-LC call. compute_all_statistics is mostly small numpy ops that hold the GIL; scipy.signal.medfilt and ndimage.median_filter are equally fast (0.30 vs 0.16 ms at n=2486, identical results).
findings.expected_gain: 2.1x on the batch path at TESS-FFI scale (published 1.25 ms/LC class), 1.4x at TESS-year; basis: measured 8 vs 1 worker. Vectorizing the statistics across the chunk (2-D medfilt, batched argmax) would remove most of the remaining ~0.6 ms/LC.
findings.recommendation: Drop the thread pool (n_workers=1) now; then vectorize _finish_lc across the chunk (ndimage.median_filter(size=(1,k)) on the (nc, nperiods) SR matrix, vectorized mean/std/argmax) for a further gain. No parity risk.

findings.title: PERF: NUFFT-LRT allocates NFFT memory and a cuFFT plan for every template: 2.5-12 ms per template vs 0.08 ms with reused memory (30-150x)
findings.method: Device timing of proc.nufft_proc.run(data) (default, allocates) vs run(data, memory=mem) with memory allocated once, 40 templates x 3 repeats; NFFTMemory alloc+plan alone.
findings.evidence: nufft_lrt.py:338 `ghat = self.nufft_proc.run([(t, y, int(nf))], **kwargs)[0]` -> cunfft.py:446-447 `if memory is None: memory = self.allocate(data, **kwargs)` (new NFFTMemory + cufft.Plan per template). lrt_detA2.py (N=512, nf=1024): per-call default 12.48 / 4.64 / 2.46 ms vs reused memory 0.09 / 0.08 / 0.08 ms; NFFTMemory alloc+plan alone 0.7-9 ms. lrt_detA.py (d): 40-template loop 219-514 ms (5.5-12.9 ms/template). Secondary: _compute_matched_filter_snr (:600) recomputes np.median(P_s[P_s>0]) per template although run() already floored the PSD (:481).
findings.expected_gain: ~30x per template (measured 2.5-12 ms -> 0.08 ms); raises the practical template budget in docs/NUFFT_LRT_README.md from ~1e3-1e4 to ~1e5 per minute; basis: measured reused-memory timing.
findings.recommendation: In run(): allocate one NFFTMemory via self.nufft_proc.allocate([(t, y, nf)]) and reuse it for the data, basis vectors and all templates (set y in place, `memory=` argument); drop the per-template median. Further: use the gridding kernel's nbatch argument to transform many templates per launch.

findings.title: NUFFT-LRT default (float32) path casts absolute times to float32 before template folding and NFFT gridding: BJD-scale timestamps halve the detection SNR
findings.method: Same synthetic box-transit light curve (n=3000, P=3.3 d, dur=0.15 d, depth 0.01, sigma 0.003, T=100 d) run through NUFFTLRTAsyncProcess.run with t in [0,100] and with t+2455000 (epochs shifted identically); repeated with use_double=True.
findings.evidence: af_nfft.py: 'LRT float32 path: max SNR over epochs t~[0,100]: 30.51 | t+2455000: 16.28'; 'LRT use_double: local 30.60 | bjd 30.60'. float32(2455050.x) has a 0.25-d resolution, i.e. 1.7x the transit duration, so both the template and the data NFFT grid positions are quantised. The same class of defect was fixed for BLS/TLS via utils.subtract_epoch (floor(min(t)) in float64) but nufft_lrt never epoch-subtracts. Note the July-2026 audit only flagged the dead template *kernel* as BJD-unsafe; the live host path has the same flaw.
findings.reproduction: bash scratchpad/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python af_nfft.py'  (section 2; local copy scratchpad/auditf/af_nfft.py)

findings.title: eebls_gpu_fast_adaptive and eebls_transit(use_optimized=True) never use the fused kernel (they load a function dict without it and fall back to the noverlap-pass loop)

findings.title: Fast-path box grid never tests qmax and its phase step (qmin/noverlap) loses 15-50% of the exact power for boxes near qmin; Keplerian window [0.5,2]q0 is searched as only {0.5,1.0,1.5}q0
findings.method: eebls_gpu_fast / _optimized / _adaptive, eebls_transit(use_fast=True)
findings.evidence: bls.cu:64 `max_bin_width = divrndup(nbf, nb0)` and :132 `for (m = 1; m < max_bin_width; m += dnbins(m, dlogq))` (same at bls_optimized.cu:71/135, bls_common.cuh:207/243): the widest box is strictly < nbf/nb0 bins, i.e. q < qmax, while the docstring (bls.py:920) says 'maximum q values to search at each frequency'. Verified on device (exp2.log): qmin=0.025,qmax=0.1 -> `q tested (3) = [0.025 0.05 0.075] max=0.075 (qmax=0.1)`; defaults qmin=0.01,qmax=0.5 -> max tested 0.48 (dlogq 0.3) / 0.44 (dlogq 0.2). Recovery vs exact float64 power at the true frequency with bounds [0.025,0.1] (exp2 (c)): q_inj=0.05 (on the grid!) 77.2%, 0.075 85.8%, 0.095 74.2%, 0.100 73.8% (eebls_gpu with noverlap=3: 86-95%). exp5.log #7: q=qmin box -> 49% of exact (`qmin=0.002: fast@f0 (49%)`). exp11 (CPU, same algorithm): Keplerian-q0 boxes recover 0.71-0.90 of exact in float64. Cause: box starts step 1/(nbf*noverlap) = qmin/2, so a width-m box is misaligned by up to 1/(4m) of its width (25% for m=1, 12.5% for m=2 = the Keplerian q0 box) -> power x(1-x)^2; astropy's default oversample=10 caps this at ~10%.
findings.reproduction: bash scratchpad/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch/blsaudit && python exp2_qgrid.py && python exp5_edge.py'; locally: python3 scratchpad/bls-audit/exp11_f32sweep.py
findings.recommendation: Change the loop bound to `m <= max_bin_width` (and document that qmax is then included, q step = dnbins); for eebls_transit(use_fast) consider qmin_fac=0.25 or noverlap=4 by default -- the fused kernel makes noverlap=4 nearly free (15.6 vs 12.8 ms, 3.2 vs 2.1 ms measured) and halves the misalignment; state the expected power loss in the docstring so users do not compare fast-path power to astropy at face value.

findings.title: float32 phase fold quantizes phases to ulp(T*f): for T*f >~ 7000 (4-yr baseline at f>=5/d, 10-yr at f>=2/d) short boxes lose 3-15% power and CPU/GPU box membership disagrees
findings.method: all binned GPU paths (fast, eebls_gpu, custom) and single_bls
findings.evidence: Fold is `mod1(t[k] * f0)` in float32 (bls_common.cuh:222, bls.cu:82). Verified on device (exp9): the compiled fold equals numpy float32 mod1 bit-for-bit (5000/5000), with `max|gpu - f64 fold| = 2.52e-03` cycles at T=3650 d, f=6.3/d, and only `1977 of 5000` distinct phase values (`ulp(t*f max=23019) = 1.95e-03 cycles`). exp1.log T=3650 d: `ref_fast(f32 fold) vs ref_fast(f64 fold) maxabs=2.4e-03 maxrel=0.58 corr=0.99940`; eebls_gpu: `single_bls(sol) vs eebls_gpu power maxabs=4.0e-04 maxrel=0.20; #freqs where single_bls(sol) deviates >2%: 3 / 92` (vs 0/435 at T=30 d). exp11 (CPU sweep with the verified fold): q=0.01 boxes recover 0.968 (T*f=7000), 0.924 (18250), 0.901 (58400) of the float64 result (worst 0.846); Keplerian-q0 boxes are unaffected (identical to 3 digits). By inspection: the eebls_gpu_custom kernel already has `double epoch` and double freqs available (bls_common.cuh:344-358) but still folds in float32.
findings.reproduction: bash scratchpad/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch/blsaudit && python exp9_fold.py'; python3 scratchpad/bls-audit/exp11_f32sweep.py
findings.recommendation: Fold in double: `phi = (float) mod1d((double) t[k] * (double) f0)` with freqs stored as float64 (or keep float32 t and split f into hi/lo). The fold is one multiply per point-frequency against the atomics that dominate the kernel, so the cost is negligible even at the 4090's 1/64 FP64 rate; or document the T*f limit (phase resolution ~1.2e-7 * T * f cycles) in the BLS docs.

findings.title: No input validation on the standard/fast paths: dy=0 or NaN y silently yields an all-NaN periodogram, constant y yields power > 1, qmin>qmax yields silent zeros (fast) or ZeroDivisionError (eebls_gpu), qmax>1 yields silent zeros

findings.evidence: `_validate_q_bounds` (bls.py:1803) is only called from sparse_bls_cpu/gpu; BLSMemory.setdata (bls.py:586) computes `w = np.power(dy, -2)` unguarded. Verified on device (exp5.log): `dy[10]=0: any NaN=True` (whole periodogram NaN, only numpy RuntimeWarnings); `y[10]=NaN: all NaN=True`; `constant y: sample=[1.2421527 1.2421522 1.2421534]` (P must be <= 1; yy=0 division); `qmin=0.2 > qmax=0.1: max power=0 (all zero=True)`; `qmax=2.0 (nbins0=0): max=0` (device integer division by zero in divrndup); eebls_gpu with qmin>qmax: `EXCEPTION ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero` (count_tot_nbins=0 -> mem_per_f=0). `dy[10]=-0.01` silently accepted (w uses dy^-2). The dy->0 weight-concentration case (`dy[10]=1e-6: median power=0.357` in noise) is documented in the docstring warning, the others are not.
findings.recommendation: In BLSMemory.setdata / eebls_gpu / eebls_gpu_custom: raise ValueError on non-finite y/dy, dy<=0, yy==0 (constant y), and call `_validate_q_bounds` (also reject qmax>1 / nbins0==0) before any GPU work.

findings.title: BLSMemory.fromdata(max_nfreqs=...) raises TypeError and single-LC memory reuse with a different number of frequencies fails
findings.method: BLSMemory, eebls_gpu_fast(memory=...)
findings.evidence: bls.py:638-641 `max_ndata = kwargs.get('max_ndata', len(t)); max_nfreqs = kwargs.get('max_nfreqs', ...); c = cls(max_ndata, max_nfreqs, **kwargs)` passes the same keys twice. bls.py:622-625 `if self.freqs_g is None: ... self.allocate_freqs(nfreqs=nf)` sizes device arrays to the first call's len(freqs), ignoring max_nfreqs, and set_async later fails. Verified on device (exp5b.log): `BLSMemory.fromdata(..., max_nfreqs=1000)` -> `TypeError: BLSMemory.__init__() got multiple values for argument 'max_nfreqs'`; reuse with 50 freqs after allocating 200 -> `ValueError: ary and self must be the same size`; `BLSMemory(ndata, 1000)` then 50 freqs works but a subsequent 120-freq call fails with the same ValueError.
findings.recommendation: Pop max_ndata/max_nfreqs from kwargs in fromdata; in setdata allocate device freq arrays of max_nfreqs and copy only the first len(freqs) (as BLSBatchMemory does), and return bls[:len(freqs)]; document that a BLSMemory is reusable across calls with nfreqs <= max_nfreqs.

findings.title: Docstring drift in the BLS entry points (defaults and semantics do not match the code)

findings.title: Host (float64) and device (float32) dnbins can disagree on the number of q levels in eebls_gpu; currently benign (device count is never larger)
findings.method: eebls_gpu (count_tot_nbins vs nbins_iter)
findings.evidence: bls.py:1355 `n = int(np.floor(dlogq * nbins))` (float64) vs bls_common.cuh:52 `floorf(dlogq * nbins)` (float32 dlogq). Scan over dlogq in [0.05,1.0) step 0.01, nb0 1-5, nbf up to 2000 (exp2.log (b)): 5 mismatching cases, e.g. `(0.52, 5, 2000, host 4112, device 4111)`, `(0.53, 1, 2000, 5752, 5751)`; in every case device < host (float32 rounding re-snaps the product to the integer), so the host-sized layout has an unused trailing slot and results are unaffected: on device with dlogq=0.52, qmin=5e-4: `max|single_bls(sol)-power|/power = 3.7e-06, #>2%: 0/400`.
findings.recommendation: Compute the level table once on the host with float32 emulation (np.float32(dlogq)*np.float32(nb)) or pass an explicit per-level bin-count table to the kernels, so the two can never diverge in the harmful direction.

findings.title: reduction_max reduces in place: the first pass reads and writes the same rows across blocks (theoretical argmax race); not observed
findings.method: eebls_gpu, eebls_gpu_custom (_reduction_max)
findings.evidence: By inspection: bls.py:224-232 calls the kernel with `arr.ptr, arr_args.ptr` as both input and `block_max`/`block_arg_max` output while `grid_size > nfreq`; bls.cu:186-188 reads `arr[fno*stride + b]` and bls.cu:227-232 writes `block_max[fno*stride + blockIdx_local]`, a slot inside block 0's read range of the same frequency, with `init==1` argmax taken as `b`. A block that finishes before an earlier block of the same frequency has read would corrupt that block's candidate/argmax. On device (exp3b.log, 6 repeats x 800 Keplerian freqs, 23 blocks/freq): 7-12 solutions differ per run but every difference is an exact power tie (`max rel power difference between the two (q,phi) = 0.00e+00`), i.e. atomic-order tie-breaking, not the race.
findings.recommendation: Reduce into a separate scratch buffer (ping-pong) instead of in place; cheap and removes the hazard. Optionally break ties deterministically (smallest index) so solutions are run-to-run reproducible.

findings.title: eebls_gpu_custom results depend on the absolute time epoch because phi_values are interpreted in the original timescale (documented but surprising)
findings.method: eebls_gpu_custom, hone_solution
findings.evidence: bls_common.cuh:373 `phi0 = (float)mod1d(phi_values[pb] - (epoch * freqs[...]))`: the user's phase grid is re-referenced by epoch*f, so the same 200-point phase grid samples different absolute phases for t and t+2.46e6. Verified on device (exp1.log): `custom(BJD): single_bls(sol) vs power maxabs=3.1e-08` (internally consistent) but `custom BJD vs t0=0 maxabs=2.137e-03 maxrel=0.82 corr=0.99904`. hone_solution (exp7.log) still converges on both (honed power 0.10443 vs exact 0.10466, |df|*T=0.005 cycles, 5 iterations, 0.7-0.9 s of which ~0.4 s is the uncached compile).
findings.reproduction: bash scratchpad/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch/blsaudit && python exp1_reference.py'  (lines 'custom BJD vs t0=0'); python exp7_hone.py
findings.recommendation: State in the eebls_gpu_custom docstring that phi_values are absolute phases (t*f mod 1 in the input timescale) and that a coarse phi grid therefore gives epoch-dependent power at low-power frequencies; hone_solution should use the kernel cache.

findings.title: sparse_bls.cu decodes each pair index with an O(N) while-loop: closed-form decode is bit-identical and 3x (N=300) to 22x (N=500) faster
findings.method: Built a variant kernel in scratch (string-replace of the two decode loops with sqrt-based closed forms + +/-1 fixups), verified bitwise-equal output, timed both at block sizes 64-512.
findings.evidence: sparse_bls.cu:239 `while (idx >= (N - i)) { idx -= (N - i); i++; }` and :265 `while (idx >= i)` run O(i) iterations for every one of N^2 pairs -> O(N^3/blockDim) per frequency (same in sparse_bls_simple.cu). Device (sparse_speed.py, 2000 freqs, min of 5): N=500 bs=64 orig 0.0945 s vs decode-opt 0.0043 s (21.8x), bitwise-equal True; N=300 0.0132 vs 0.0041 (3.2x), bitwise-equal True; N=100 no gain (0.79x, ms-level noise). Also: the per-frequency weight normalization, ybar and YY (Steps 2-4) are recomputed for every frequency although they are frequency-independent, and the prefix scan runs on thread 0 only.
findings.expected_gain: ~20x at N=500, ~3x at N=300 on the sparse kernel (basis: measured 0.0945 -> 0.0043 s at N=500, 2000 freqs); still 15x slower than the binned kernel
findings.reproduction: pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python sparse_speed.py' (block-size sweep); variant source is the new_nw/new_w strings in sparse_speed.py
findings.recommendation: Replace both while-loop decodes with the closed-form row index (row i of the non-wrapped triangle starts at i*N - i*(i-1)/2; wrapped row i at i*(i-1)/2), hoist the frequency-independent normalization to a one-time host/device pre-pass.

findings.title: float32 phase fold in sparse BLS: statistic depends on sort order at tied float32 phases (26% at one frequency, N=300/365 d) and loses up to 30% at f_inj for 10-yr baselines at 4.7 c/d (ulp = 20% of q)
findings.method: Float64-fold vs float32-fold reference, stable vs reverse-stable tie ordering, and comparison with cpu/gpu-full/gpu-simple at the worst frequencies; injection at long baselines.
findings.evidence: bls.py:1863/2079 `t = t.astype(np.float32)` and the kernels' `mod1(t[i]*freq)` give phase resolution ulp(t*f): 3e-5 at 365 d x 1.3 c/d, 2e-3 at 3650 d x 4.7 c/d. sparse_drill.py section 1 (N=300, 365 d, f=1.29125, 2 tied phase groups): ref(stable sort)=0.058451, ref(reverse order)=0.073598, cpu(np.argsort quicksort)=0.073598, gpu-full(bitonic)=0.073598, gpu-simple(bubble)=0.058451 -- the three shipped implementations disagree by 26% at that frequency purely through tie order, because a box boundary that splits two points with identical float32 phase is a candidate. sparse_fold.py: at 3650 d, f=4.7, q=0.01, N=300: |cpu-ref64|/ref64 at the injected frequency max 0.295, in-transit set size differs in 2/16 LCs; at 1000 d or 365 d the effect vanishes (max 0.000). Peak-frequency argmax was unaffected in every run of sparse_exp.py.
findings.recommendation: For N<=500 a double-precision fold is free: upload t (epoch-subtracted) and freqs as float64, compute `phi = (float) mod1d((double)t*(double)f)` or keep phases in double through the sort; on the CPU fold in float64 and use a stable argsort keyed on (phi, t) so ties are deterministic. Document that the exact-set property holds only to float32 phase resolution if left as is.

findings.title: Reported sparse duration q is biased low by ~half the mean phase gap and differs from both the paper (Eqs 8-10) and the docs (phi_j - phi_i); the Keplerian qmin/qmax filter is applied to this biased estimate
findings.method: Read paper Sec. 3.2; compared reported q vs injected q and vs the paper's ingress/egress-midpoint definition over 20 LCs per N; counted LCs whose peak power changes under the eebls_transit-style qmin/qmax filter between the two definitions.
findings.evidence: Kernel: phi0 = sh_phi[i] (first in-transit point) and q to the egress midpoint only (sparse_bls.cu:248 `q = 0.5f*(sh_phi[j]+sh_phi[j-1]) - phi0`; CPU bls.py:1930, :1973). Paper Eq. 8 puts ingress at the midpoint of phi[i1-1] and phi[i1]. Docs bls.rst:117-119 say 'phi_0 = phi_i, q = phi_j - phi_i' (neither). Device (sparse_q_semantics.py, q_true=0.04): N=100 reported q - q_true = -0.0084 (sd 0.0086) vs paper-def +0.0010; N=200 -0.0041 vs -0.0000; N=400 -0.0019 vs +0.0001 -- i.e. bias ~ -1/(2N)..-1/N (21% of q at N=100). With qmin=0.5q/qmax=2q the peak power differs between definitions in 3/20 (N=50) and 2/20 (N=100) LCs. Power values are unaffected (same sets); only the returned q and the filter boundary are.
findings.recommendation: Use the paper's symmetric definition (ingress midpoint, wrap-aware) for both the reported (q, phi0) and the qmin/qmax test, keeping single_bls semantics consistent (phi0 = ingress midpoint, box [phi0, phi0+q) still contains exactly the run); fix the docs paragraph.

findings.title: eebls_gpu_batch(noverlap=0) silently returns an all-zero periodogram (eebls_gpu_fast raises); no noverlap validation on the batch path
findings.method: Device call + inspection.
findings.evidence: _validate_noverlap is only called at bls.py:669 (fast impl); eebls_gpu_batch computes bls.py:2649 `n_passes = 1 if batch_use_fused else noverlap` -> zero kernel launches, then reads back the untouched (zero, or stale on memory reuse) bls_g. Device (sparse_edge.py): "noverlap=0 -> [0. 0. 0. ...]" while "fast noverlap=0 -> ValueError noverlap must be a positive integer". A non-integer noverlap (e.g. 3.0) would hit range(3.0) TypeError.
findings.recommendation: Call _validate_noverlap(noverlap) at the top of eebls_gpu_batch.

findings.title: Non-finite inputs (NaN t/y, dy=0, constant y) silently produce all-zero (batch), all-NaN (fast) or garbage (sparse GPU) periodograms with no error; the three paths disagree
findings.method: Fed degenerate arrays (one NaN in t or y, one dy=0, dy<0, constant y, N=1) to sparse cpu/gpu/simple, eebls_gpu_fast and eebls_gpu_batch on the device.
findings.evidence: sparse_edge.py: 'one NaN t' -> cpu 0, gpu-full 0.2034, gpu-simple 0.1742, fast 0, batch 0 (subtract_epoch's t.min() is NaN so every phase is NaN; CUDA float->int of NaN lands in bin 0); 'one dy=0' -> cpu/gpu/batch all 0, fast all NaN (bls_memory.py:160 `w = np.power(dy,-2)` -> inf/inf); 'one NaN y' -> sparse/batch 0, fast NaN; 'constant y' -> fast NaN, batch returns RAW un-normalized power 1.609 because bls_memory.py:292 `if self.yy[i] > 0` skips the division; 'negative dy' accepted everywhere. eebls_gpu's docstring warns about near-zero dy but nothing raises. A single NaN timestamp zeroing an entire survey light curve's periodogram is the dangerous case.
findings.recommendation: Validate in one place (subtract_epoch or a shared _check_lc): require finite t/y/dy, dy>0, len>=2 (sparse) and raise ValueError; make batch's yy==0 case return NaN or raise like the fast path.

findings.title: sparse_bls_gpu fails with a bare 'cuLaunchKernel failed: invalid argument' above ndata~2000 (shared memory > 48 KB), no size check or message
findings.method: Device sweep of ndata with the default kernel.
findings.evidence: bls.py:2131 `shared_mem_size = (3*n_pow2 + 2*max_ndata + 3*block_size)*4` is never compared to MAX_SHARED_MEMORY_PER_BLOCK (49152 on the 4090). sparse_edge.py: N=2000 ok; N=2500/3000/4000 -> `LogicError: cuLaunchKernel failed: invalid argument`. Reachable via eebls_transit(use_sparse=True) or sparse_threshold>2000.
findings.recommendation: Compare shared_mem_size with the device attribute and raise ValueError('ndata too large for sparse GPU BLS; use the standard kernel') -- or opt into >48 KB dynamic shared memory with cuFuncSetAttribute.

findings.title: No minimum in-transit-point floor in sparse BLS: in pure noise 30% of trial frequencies pick a single-point 'transit' (paper recommends >=3 points)
findings.method: Float64 reference with per-frequency best-set size on 10 pure-noise N=100 light curves x 200 frequencies.
findings.evidence: Paper Sec. 2: 'We recommend setting a lower limit to the number of points in transit, to reduce the chance of false detections caused by spurious outliers ... lower limit of three'. cuvarbase has no such option; only qmin (Keplerian 0.5*q) indirectly filters. sparse_more.py D: 'best box is a single point at 600/2000 (30%) of trial frequencies; mean periodogram max 0.1920' for N=100 pure noise. Since a single k-sigma outlier scores ~k^2/N, this inflates the noise floor of exactly the sparse regime the method targets.
findings.recommendation: Add `min_points` (default 3 per the paper, or 1 for backward compatibility) to sparse_bls_cpu/gpu and eebls_transit; in the kernels it is a `(j - i) < min_points -> continue` test.

findings.title: eebls_gpu_batch sorts light curves by ndata 'to minimize padding' but pads every chunk to the global max_ndata anyway; per-chunk H2D transfer is max_ndata*batch_n
findings.method: Inspection.
findings.evidence: bls.py:2522 `sorted_indices = sorted(lc_indices, key=lambda i: lc_ndatas[i])` but the single BLSBatchMemory is built with `max_ndata_all` (bls.py ~2570) and transfer_to_gpu copies `self.max_ndata * n_act` floats (bls_memory.py transfer_to_gpu). A batch of 255 x 200-point LCs plus one 20000-point LC uploads 100x more data than needed; the kernel itself only loops to ndata_lc so compute is unaffected (ragged parity verified clean).
findings.expected_gain: transfer-bound only; up to ~max/median ndata ratio in H2D bytes for very ragged batches; negligible for uniform surveys
findings.reproduction: inspection; batch_exp.py section 2 shows correctness is unaffected
findings.recommendation: Either size each chunk's stride to its own max ndata (chunk-local BLSBatchMemory or a stride argument) or remove the misleading sort/comment.

findings.title: No free baseline term: a 0.5-sigma flux-normalization offset halves or doubles the SDE (shared with the reference, but cuvarbase is more sensitive)
findings.method: experiment on device (exp_d_semantics.py, exp_k_followup.py (a))
findings.evidence: Model is 1 - d*T with a fixed baseline of 1 (tls_fast.cu:8-10, tls.py:1162 `resid = 1.0 - y64`). P=7.3 d, rp=0.05, sigma=1e-3, 60 d: y*(1+off): off=0 -> SDE 21.49; +2e-4 -> 25.56; +5e-4 -> 29.33 (depth 0.0024 vs true 0.0031); +1e-3 -> 24.02 with 2916/6157 periods failed (depth 0.0019); +2e-3 -> SDE 5.29, 6057/6157 failed; -5e-4 -> SDE 10.09; -1e-3 -> SDE 5.86 and wrong period 2.437. Reference on the same data: 0 -> 22.36, -5e-4 -> 14.30, +5e-4 -> 3.25 with wrong period 1.217 (cuvarbase 20.78 / 9.70 / 28.06). A mean- vs median-normalized light curve, or a detrender bias, routinely leaves offsets of this size for Kepler/TESS-quality noise.
findings.reproduction: pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python exp_d_semantics.py' (baseline offset section); python exp_k_followup.py (section (a))
findings.recommendation: Fit the out-of-transit level jointly with the depth: chi2 = sum w (y - c + d T)^2 has a 2x2 closed form needing only the totals sum(w), sum(w y) (per-LC constants) plus per-window sum(wT) = sum_k B_k dS1_k, which the binned kernel already forms alongside num/den; same in the refine kernel. Until then, document that y must be normalized to ~0.1 sigma/point and that the failure mode is asymmetric (positive offsets inflate SDE, negative ones destroy it).

findings.title: SR statistic is 1 - chi2/chi2_max, not the reference's chi2_min/chi2: identical under the null but 2x different SDE for strong signals, contradicting 'identical SDE statistic' in the docs
findings.method: experiment on device (exp_a_refcompare.py, exp_c_null.py, exp_k_followup.py (c)) + reference source
findings.evidence: tls_stats.py:46 `SR = 1.0 - chi2 / (chi2_null + 1e-10)` with chi2_null = max(chi2); reference stats.py: `SR = numpy.min(chi2) / chi2; SDE_raw = (1 - mean(SR)) / std(SR)`. Both are linear in delta-chi2 only when score << chi2_0. Null LCs: reference spectra() applied to cuvarbase's own chi2 vs cuvarbase SDE: 'corr=1.000 mean abs diff=0.05'. Strong signal (P=3 d, rp=0.10, sigma=1e-3, SNR~110, score_best/chi2_0=0.79): 'cuvarbase SDE=21.83 | reference spectra() on cuvarbase chi2: SDE=45.38'; in the full comparison the reference reported SDE 44.67 vs cuvarbase 21.62 on the same data and grid, while all moderate-SNR cases agree to 5-10%. The reference's SDE_MEDIAN_KERNEL_SIZE*oversampling (91 at OS=3, 151 at OS=5) is hard-capped at 91 in cuvarbase regardless of oversampling_factor.
findings.reproduction: pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python exp_k_followup.py' (section (c)); exp_a.log row P3_rp0.10_b0
findings.recommendation: Adopt SR = chi2_min/chi2 (chi2_min of the coarse spectrum is available) so SDE values are comparable with the literature and any reference FAP table; tie the median kernel to oversampling_factor*30 like the reference; state the definition in tls.rst.

findings.title: Unsorted/descending user period grid silently corrupts period_uncertainty (negative) and the SDE (shuffled grid) — the reference's results.periods is descending
findings.method: experiment on device (exp_k_followup.py (d)) + inspection
findings.evidence: No path sorts or validates `periods` (tls.py:564 / :1284 just cast to float32); the SDE median detrend (tls_stats.py:139 medfilt) and the uncertainty neighbour-walk (tls_stats.py:441-451) assume period-ordered neighbours. Same LC and grid: 'ascending: P=7.2992 SDE=21.49 unc=0.00893 | descending: P=7.2992 SDE=21.49 unc=-0.00893 | shuffled: P=7.2992 SDE=20.27 unc=0.35269'. transitleastsquares returns results.periods in descending order, so passing it through is a natural user action.
findings.recommendation: argsort the grid on entry (and scatter per-period outputs back to the caller's order), or raise on non-monotonic input.

findings.title: scipy.signal.medfilt zero-padding biases the SR trend at the grid edges, inflating 'power' there; null peaks land near the grid ends 2.3x more often than expected
findings.method: experiment on device (exp_c_null.py, exp_k_followup.py (c)) + reference source
findings.evidence: tls_stats.py:139 `signal.medfilt(SR, kernel_size)` zero-pads; the reference's running_median extends with the first/last median. On a real spectrum: 'SR trend at edges: scipy medfilt(zero-pad) first5=[0.00046 0.00069 0.0008 0.0008 0.0008] ... running_median first/last=2.997e-03/1.701e-02 ; typical SR=4.807e-03', i.e. the trend is 4-6x too low over the first ~45 periods so power=SR-trend is raised by ~half a typical SR there. Null run: 'peak within 45 grid points of an edge: 0.035 (uniform expectation 0.015)' (14 vs 6 of 400 LCs).
findings.recommendation: Use scipy.ndimage.median_filter(SR, size=k, mode='nearest') (same cost) or the reference's edge-extended running median.

findings.title: Coarse epoch grid (t0_oversample=3) costs more than the documented 'few percent' for narrow transits and makes SDE/SNR/depth jitter with the injected epoch
findings.method: experiment on device (exp_b_t0phase.py, exp_e_window.py, exp_k_followup.py (b))
findings.evidence: Sweeping the injected epoch across 1.5 coarse strides (P=7.3 d, q=0.021, sigma=1e-3): 'SDE range fast3: 19.77..23.44 (rel spread 17.1%), fast33: 20.89..22.28 (6.5%)', legacy exact kernel identical to fast within 1%; SNR (from the coarse chi2) 17.8-20.1 and refined depth 0.0027-0.0031 with epoch. Narrow-transit regime (M dwarf, duration 0.071 d = 3.4 cadences of 30 min): t0_oversample=3 -> SDE 29.07, 10 -> 32.85, 33 -> 32.71, correct Keplerian window -> 34.5, reference -> 38.81 (-11% vs oversample 10, -25% vs reference). docs/source/tls.rst:125 and tls.py:154/:492 claim the reference steps '~33x finer'; reference core.py uses T0_FIT_MARGIN=0.01 -> every data point or duration/100 (tls.py:1224 correctly says ~100).
findings.recommendation: Consider t0_oversample=10 as the default (matches 33 within 1% here) or document the narrow-transit loss quantitatively; fix the '33x' statements to '~100x / every cadence'; derive SNR from the refined chi2 at the chosen period (or state it is coarse).

findings.title: SNR uses chi2_null = max(chi2 over the grid) and the coarse chi2 at the best period, inconsistent with the refined chi2_min
findings.method: experiment on device (exp_d_semantics.py) + inspection
findings.evidence: tls_stats.py:358 `chi2_null = np.max(chi2)` (worst trial period, not the constant-model chi2_0 that the batch path already holds in float64) and :359 `chi2_best = chi2[best_period_idx]` (coarse). Measured: 'SNR=17.50 sqrt(max(chi2)-chi2_best)=18.20 ; sqrt(chi2_0 - chi2_best)=18.39'. SNR then jitters 17.8-20.1 with the injected epoch (exp_b) while 'chi2_min' is refined.
findings.recommendation: SNR = sqrt(chi2_0 - chi2_min_refined) on the batch path (both numbers already exist); document that it is a delta-chi2 significance, not the reference's depth/std*sqrt(n).

findings.title: pink_noise_correction ignores its n_transits argument and its docstring formula is dimensionally meaningless
findings.method: experiment on device + inspection
findings.evidence: tls_stats.py:485-486 `correction = np.sqrt(correlation_length); snr_pink = snr / correction` — n_transits unused. Verified: pink_noise_correction(10.0, 1) = pink_noise_correction(10.0, 100) = 10.0; (10.0, 100, correlation_length=4) = 5.0. Docstring claims 'correction ~ sqrt(correlation_length / n_points_per_transit)'. Not called by any path.
findings.recommendation: Remove it, or implement the Pont et al. (2006) red-noise scaling (sigma_r from binned residuals at the transit duration) as the reference's snr_pink_per_transit does.

findings.title: odd_even_mismatch is never populated in any result and returns (0, 0) even when the depths differ but each group is constant
findings.method: experiment on device + inspection
findings.evidence: compute_all_statistics only computes odd/even when depths_per_transit is passed; neither tls.py:771 nor :1578 passes it, so no result dict ever carries 'odd_even_mismatch' despite docs/TLS_GPU_README.md:247 listing odd/even tests. odd_even_mismatch([0.010,0.010],[0.012,0.012]) -> (0.0, 0.0): combined_std=0 short-circuits to zero mismatch AND zero depth_diff (should be -0.002 / undefined significance); uses ddof=0 population std.
findings.recommendation: Either compute per-transit depths at the best solution (cheap: one masked pass) and populate the statistic, or drop it from the API/docs; return depth_diff unconditionally and NaN for the significance when the std is zero.

findings.title: period_uncertainty is grid-spacing-limited, not the documented 1-sigma; the no-points-below branch is dead
findings.method: experiment on device + inspection
findings.evidence: Delta-chi2=1 threshold (tls_stats.py:426) against a spectrum whose neighbouring grid points differ by 25-145 chi2 ('chi2 around min: [87.5 46.2 24.7 0. 68.5 105.3 144.6]') always terminates at the adjacent points, so the walk returns ~1.5 grid spacings ('unc=0.00893 grid spacing there=0.00596'); `below[best_idx]` is always True so the `if not np.any(below)` fallback (tls_stats.py:431-436) is unreachable. The reference uses the FWHM of the detrended power peak.
findings.recommendation: Use the FWHM of the power peak (as the reference) or interpolate the chi2 parabola between grid points; document that the result is resolution-limited.

findings.title: Flat/noiseless light curve raises RuntimeError on every path instead of returning a null result
findings.method: experiment on device
findings.evidence: y == 1 exactly gives num = 0 for every trial, the `num > 0` gate rejects all, every period fails: 'fast flat -> RuntimeError TLS kernel returned no valid solution for any of the 200 trial periods'; batch returns {'error': ...}; legacy raises too. The reference returns SDE=0 with a warning.
findings.recommendation: Return SDE=0/NaN with a warning (as the reference does) rather than raising; keep the per-LC 'error' dict on the batch path but document it.

findings.title: Dead API surface: tls_search_gpu accepts unused R_planet_min/R_planet_max/duration_grid_step; duration_grid/t0_grid/estimate_n_evaluations unused, duration_grid IndexErrors on inverted bounds; nonlinear/uniform LD coefficients are not validated
findings.method: inspection + CPU experiment (exp_f_template.py, exp_g_grid.py)
findings.evidence: grep: R_planet_min/R_planet_max/duration_grid_step appear only in the signature and docstring of tls_search_gpu (tls.py:426-427, 477-480). duration_grid/t0_grid are called by no search path (only estimate_n_evaluations calls t0_grid). duration_grid(periods) with defaults returns only 2 durations per period ('counts [2 2]'); duration_grid([1.0], R_planet_min=5, R_planet_max=0.5) -> IndexError. validate_limb_darkening_coeffs only checks 'quadratic'/'linear'; 'nonlinear' with 4 coefficients and 'uniform' with u=[] pass validation and template generation silently.
findings.reproduction: grep -n 'R_planet_min\|duration_grid_step' cuvarbase/tls.py; pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python exp_g_grid.py; python exp_f_template.py'
findings.recommendation: Warn/deprecate the dead parameters (as was done for `durations`), remove or test the unused grid helpers, validate nonlinear (4 coeffs) and uniform (0 coeffs) laws.

findings.title: period_grid_ofir returns sub-Roche periods when the baseline is shorter than 2 Roche periods
findings.method: CPU experiment + inspection
findings.evidence: When f_max < f_min the computed n_freq is negative and is floored to 10 (tls_grids.py:178-179); the grid then starts at f_min and walks UP in frequency ignoring f_max: 1-day baseline, Sun-like star -> 'period_grid_ofir ... [0.4197683 0.42779358 0.43602474] ...' (Roche limit is 0.60 d). The reference falls back to a 5-day-span default grid in this case.
findings.reproduction: python -c 'from cuvarbase import tls_grids; import numpy as np; print(tls_grids.period_grid_ofir(np.array([0,1.0])))' (works on the CPU stub or the pod)
findings.recommendation: Raise or warn when f_max <= f_min; clip the grid at the Roche limit.

findings.title: docs/TLS_GPU_README.md still carries the EXPERIMENTAL banner, the 3,500-point cap and 30-epoch-grid 'known issues', 'SDE > 7 robust', and the wrong '33x' reference-grid claim
findings.method: inspection
findings.evidence: docs/TLS_GPU_README.md:3-9: 'EXPERIMENTAL - not recommended for science use ... fixed 30-point epoch grid ... light curves above ~3,500 points exceed the kernel's shared-memory budget ... A rework is planned for v1.1' — all superseded by the July rewrite (README.md:24 calls TLS a headline feature; exp_h ran 504,000 points). :221 'SDE > 7 typically indicates a robust detection' (23-25% of null LCs exceed 7 in exp_c). tls.rst:125 / tls.py:154 / :492 '~33x finer' vs reference T0_FIT_MARGIN=0.01 (100x or every cadence).
findings.recommendation: Rewrite or delete TLS_GPU_README.md; fix the 33x statements.

findings.title: _module_reader leaks a file handle per kernel compile (ResourceWarning on every band compile)
findings.method: experiment on device (exp_h_bands_long.py warnings capture) + inspection
findings.evidence: utils.py:115 `txt = open(fname, 'r').read()` never closes; a Kepler-length grid compiles 6 bands and emitted 6x "unclosed file <_io.TextIOWrapper name='/workspace/cuvarbase/cuvarbase/kernels/tls_fast.cu' mode='r' encoding='utf-8'>" under warnings.simplefilter('always').
findings.recommendation: `with open(fname) as f: txt = f.read()`.

findings.title: Band boundaries put sub-sigma steps in the raw score spectrum ('uniform fidelity' is uniform only within a band); removed by the median detrend
findings.method: experiment on device (exp_h_bands_long.py)
findings.evidence: 1400-d null LC, 178,532 periods, 6 bands (256..8192 bins). Mean score of the 200 periods on each side of a boundary: P=16.6 d 16.33/16.84, P=47.0 d 18.76/17.99, P=133 d 19.23/19.99, P=376 d 20.58/21.95, against a per-period scatter of 2.2-2.6 (0.2-0.6 sigma steps); detrended power is continuous (1.05e-4 vs 1.05e-4). SDE=9.24 for this null LC.
findings.recommendation: No action needed for detection; note in tls.rst that fidelity is uniform per band and that the 91-point median detrend absorbs the boundary steps.

findings.title: Single-lightcurve calls rebuild the batman template tables and per-band GPU inputs every call (~30% of a small tls_search_gpu call; batch path is 3.5x cheaper per LC)
findings.method: experiment on device (exp_i_perf.py; repeated-measurement medians on a shared 4090, relative only)
findings.evidence: 2880 pts x 6157 periods, median of 5: 'generate_template_tables (batman): 1.2 ms'; 'tls_search_gpu full call: 7.9 ms'; 'tls_search_gpu with cached tables: 5.5 ms' (monkeypatched cache); 'tls_search_batch 64 LCs: 2.19 ms/LC'. tls_search_batch (tls.py:1399) regenerates T/S1/S2 via batman on every call and re-uploads periods/qmin/qmax/period_map per band (tls.py:1379-1382) plus fresh output buffers (tls.py:1433-1458), so a per-LC loop over tls_search_gpu pays ~3.5 ms of fixed host/upload overhead per call.
findings.recommendation: Memoize generate_template_tables on (limb_dark, tuple(u), n_table) (one-line lru_cache); optionally expose a reusable plan (grid + bands + device buffers) for per-LC loops. Timings are noisy (shared GPU, 4090 not the archived A5000) and reported only as relative.
findings.expected_gain: ~30% on small single-LC calls (7.9 -> 5.5 ms measured with a cached table); larger fraction for tiny LCs/grids; no gain on the batch path

findings.title: batched_run_const_nfreq returns significance = 1 - FAP, which saturates to exactly 1.0 for any FAP < 1e-16, undoing the issue-#14 log-space FAP fix
findings.method: batched_run_const_nfreq(only_return_best_freqs=True) on a strong signal (N=1000, amp 0.5, noise 0.05) and direct fap_baluev of the same peak.
findings.evidence: lombscargle.py:982-984 `significance = 1. - fap[best_index]` ... `best_freq_significances.append(significance)`. exp6: best z=0.9435, fap_baluev=0.0 (below float64), returned significance=1.0, 1-significance=0.0; any FAP between 1e-308 and 1e-16 is likewise unrecoverable from the returned value. fap_baluev itself matches astropy _statistics.fap_baluev to <1e-13 relative for N=20..20000 (exp4) but underflows to 0.0 once (1-z)^(N_K/2) < 1e-308 (e.g. N=1000, z=0.8).
findings.recommendation: Return the FAP (or log10 FAP) instead of 1-FAP, and add a log_fap/return_log option to fap_baluev computed as logaddexp(log(-expm1(-tau)), log_Psing_c - tau) so values below 1e-308 survive.

findings.title: cufinufft backend raises TypeError with use_double=True and is float32-only by construction
findings.method: LombScargleAsyncProcess(use_cufinufft=True, use_double=True).run on N=100.
findings.evidence: cufinufft_backend.py:72 `dtype='complex64'`, :174-175 float32 scale/shift, :177 `x_cu = memory.t_g * scale + shift` is float64 when the memory is double. exp5: TypeError("Argument `x` does not have the correct dtype: float64 was given, but <class 'numpy.float32'> was expected."). Otherwise the backend is correct: vs astropy 4e-04..3e-03 for N=100..20000 on all bands incl. k0/nf=4, 7.2e-03 at T=3650/fmax=50 (float32 phase), plan cache reuse across alternating N=100/700 gives identical results, batched path identical.
findings.recommendation: Select dtype='complex128' and float64 scale/shift when memory.use_double (key the plan cache on dtype), or raise a clear ValueError at construction.

findings.title: float32 error floor of the (fixed) NFFT GLS: 1.7e-4 (f*T ~ 7e3) to 2.6e-3 (f*T ~ 2e5) absolute power error; direct-sums float32 8e-4 at T=3650
findings.method: After the three fixes, compared float32 vs float64 vs astropy on k0=1 grids for T=365/fmax=20 and T=3650/fmax=50, m=2..12; direct sums (use_fft=False) at T=3650 fmax 19-20.
findings.evidence: exp2c: FIXED f32 sigma=4 m=4..12 maxabs 1.72e-04 (m-independent), T=3650/fmax=50 2.6e-03 (double: 4.0e-08); exp1 E: dirsum float32 T=3650 maxabs 8.0e-04 vs double 1.9e-09. Sources: float32 storage of t (2.4e-4 d resolution at |t|~1825 d = 0.05 grid cells at ng=3.65M), float32 un-reduced phases in normalize (cunfft.cu:239-244 theta up to 2*pi*f*|tmin|) and (t+0.5)*f*2*pi in lomb.cu:29. The estimate_m docstring (cunfft.py:294-299) describes the ~1e-3 floor; it is not stated in the LS docs.
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python exp2c_fixed.py'  (float32 m sweep) and exp1_gls.py section E/F
findings.recommendation: Document in lomb.rst that float32 is accurate to ~1e-4 for f*T <~ 1e4 and ~1e-3 at survey scale, recommend use_double=True for FAP-grade work at large f*T; optionally shift the time origin to tmin (theta=0 in normalize, power is shift-invariant) to remove the largest float32 phase term.

findings.title: floating_mean=False and window=True conventions differ from astropy and are undocumented (classic LS on unweighted-mean-centred data; window = 4x the LS of ones)
findings.method: Compared run(floating_mean=False) with astropy fit_mean=False (center_data True/False) on heteroscedastic data, and run(window=True) with astropy LombScargle(ones, fit_mean=False, center_data=False) (with fixes applied).
findings.evidence: normalize_light_curves (utils.py:236-247) subtracts the UNWEIGHTED nanmean of y; lspow0 (lomb.cu:116-122) then normalises by YY+Y^2 = sum w (y-mean_unw)^2: exp1 G maxabs 3.7e-02 vs astropy fit_mean=False/center_data=True, 2.1e-02 vs center_data=False on y-mean(y). lomb.cu:144 `lspow0(C, S, C2, S2, C, S, 0.f, 1.f, NULL)` sets YCh=C so YCh+Y*C=2C: exp3b window/astropy-LS-of-ones ratio percentiles (1,50,99) = 3.99999985, 4.0, 4.00000016.
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python exp1_gls.py'  (sections G, H); exp3b_mh_fixed.py
findings.recommendation: Document both conventions (or pass YCh=0.5*C for a conventional window normalisation and centre by the weighted mean when floating_mean=False).

findings.title: Invalid inputs produce silent all -1 or huge powers instead of errors: dy=0, NaN y, N<=3, constant t/y, dy=None; nf=1 raises IndexError
findings.method: run() on 300-pt LC with one dy=0, one NaN y, one NaN t, N=1/2/3, identical times, constant y, dy=None, nf=1; duplicate times vs astropy.
findings.evidence: exp6: dy with one zero -> all 9124 powers == -1 (kernel NaN sentinel, lomb.cu:86-87) with no warning; y NaN -> all -1; t NaN -> finite but silently on a corrupted grid; N=2 -> max power 9.9e+09; N=3 -> 1.6e+04; N=1, all-t-identical, constant y -> all -1; dy=None -> TypeError in setdata (lombscargle_memory.py:297) although normalize_light_curves' docstring (utils.py:232-233) advertises dy=None pass-through; nf=1 -> IndexError at lombscargle.py:418 (`freqs[1]`). Duplicate times are fine (7.3e-03 vs astropy = the psi-bug level). fap_baluev(z=-1) -> nan, N<=3 -> FAP>1 (exp4: N=2 gives 1.05, 3.16).
findings.recommendation: Validate in setdata/run: finite t,y,dy>0, N>=4 (or >= d_K+1), len(freqs)>=2, tmax>tmin; implement or remove the dy=None path; make fap_baluev clip z to [0,1] and require N>d_K.

findings.title: batched_run_const_nfreq builds the default mask as np.array([True]*nf): 8-17 ms per call at survey nf
findings.method: cProfile of batched_run_const_nfreq (10 LCs, nf=219K) and direct timing of the expression vs np.ones(nf, bool).
findings.evidence: lombscargle.py:969 `default_mask = np.array([True] * len(freqs))`. cProfile (exp8, ZTF-like): 71 numpy.array calls 17 ms of a 49 ms call; exp9: np.array([True]*219000) 8.5-9.4 ms vs np.ones 0.005 ms. Per-call fixed costs dominate this API at small call sizes: 26 ms for a single-LC call (2 cuFFT plans 14 ms + plan __del__ 3 ms + mask) vs 0.6 ms of GPU work; measured 4.7 ms/LC at 10 LCs/call vs 2.2 ms/LC at 50 LCs/call.
findings.recommendation: np.ones(len(freqs), dtype=bool); and reuse self.memory / cuFFT plans across calls when nf and max_ndata are unchanged (E2 is documented but still costs ~26 ms per call).
findings.expected_gain: 8-17 ms per call (measured); plus ~20 ms/call if memory/plans are cached

findings.title: Frequency-grid conventions: autofrequency truncates the minimum frequency below the requested value and stops one bin short of maximum_frequency; batched_run_const_nfreq(freqs=None) drops one more frequency; grids starting at 0 are rejected
findings.method: Compared utils.autofrequency and batched_run_const_nfreq's regenerated grid with astropy autofrequency for the same arguments.
findings.evidence: utils.py:189 `nf0 = max([nf0, int(minimum_frequency / df)])`, :192 `Nf = int(maximum_frequency / df) - nf0`: exp6 autofreq(minf=0.1,maxf=20) -> f[0]=0.09946, f[-1]=19.99939 (astropy 0.10000/19.99993); lombscargle.py:932 `nf = int(round(np.max(freqs)/df)) - k0` gives nf=3749 where run() gives 3750; get_k0 (lombscargle.py:32) clamps k0>=1 so freqs[0]=0 fails check_k0. check_k0 only inspects freqs[0], freqs[1] (geomspace happened to be rejected here, but a grid with uniform first spacing and non-uniform rest would pass).
findings.recommendation: Use ceil for nf0 and round for Nf (so f[0]>=fmin and f[-1]~fmax), use len(freqs) in batched_run_const_nfreq, allow k0=0, and have check_k0 assert np.allclose(np.diff(freqs), df).

findings.title: NFFTAsyncProcess docstring and release notes misstate defaults/accuracy: sigma default is 4 (doc says 2), autoset_m default False (doc says True); 'multiharmonic ... machine precision' was only true CPU-side
findings.method: Inspection of cunfft.py vs its docstring; device measurement of the H=2,3 path.
findings.evidence: cunfft.py:177 `sigma: float, optional (default: 2)` vs :212 `kwargs.get('sigma', 4)`; :183 `autoset_m ... (default: True)` vs :214 `kwargs.get('autoset_m', False)`. RELEASE_NOTES_v1.0.0.md:75 claims H=2,3 match direct sums to machine precision; on device (exp3) H=2 maxabs 8.8e-03, H=3 6.6e-03 as shipped (2e-08 after the fixes). test_lombscargle.py:180 passes a no-op kwarg use_cpu_nfft=True; lomb.cu:174 lomb_dirsum_custom_frq is never prepared (dead kernel). memory_requirement(autoadjust_sigma=...) (lombscargle.py:589-596) has no counterpart in allocation.
findings.recommendation: Fix the docstrings; re-verify the release-note claim on device after the NFFT fixes; delete the dead kernel/kwargs or wire them.

findings.title: The kernel receives k0 as a float (f0*spp*T) instead of the integer k0; check_k0's 1% tolerance permits a fractional-mode shift that the periodic grid cannot represent
findings.method: Bare NFFTAsyncProcess with minimum_frequency = (10+eps)/T for eps = 0, 0.01, 0.1, 0.5 vs exact DFT at the fractional and at the integer frequencies.
findings.evidence: cunfft.cu:79 `FLT k0 = f0 * spp * (xf - x0)` and :240 same in normalize; lombscargle.py:35-43 check_k0 accepts |f0 - k0 df| < 1e-2 df. exp2 sec.3 (||y||_1~160): eps=0 err 1.3e-05; eps=0.01 err 5.3e-02 (3e-4 relative); eps=0.1 err 0.52; eps=0.5 err 1.67 - the ifft of a periodic gridded sequence at a non-integer mode is a Dirichlet-leakage mixture, not the transform.
findings.recommendation: Pass np.int32(k0) to nfft_shift/normalize (as lomb already does) and tighten check_k0 to ~1e-6 df.

findings.title: CE: use_fast=True silently ignores balanced_magbins (uniform dm used), and balanced_magbins silently overrides compute_log_prob
findings.method: Conditional Entropy option combinations
findings.evidence: The fast kernels have no mag_bwf argument (ce.cu:214 uses dm0=(mag_overlap+1)/nmag), and conditional_entropy() (ce.py:69-72) dispatches `if balanced_magbins: ce_dpdm elif compute_log_prob: ce_logp`, so log_prob is dropped when both are set. Neither combination is in the docs' 'Unsupported option combinations' list and no ValueError is raised (ce.py:228 only guards use_fast+weighted). Verified on device (ce_followup.py balanced): 'use_fast=True + balanced_magbins(run kwarg): max|fast - standard(constdpdm)|=3.715e-02 (no error raised)'; 'compute_log_prob=True + balanced_magbins: max|result - constdpdm|=0.000e+00'.
findings.recommendation: Raise ValueError for use_fast+balanced_magbins and balanced_magbins+compute_log_prob (same pattern as the existing guards) and list them in docs/source/ce.rst.

findings.title: CE balanced_magbins: bin width = y[last]-y[first] of the members -> zero width for a bin of identical values -> CE = -inf at every frequency
findings.method: Conditional Entropy, balanced_magbins (constdpdm_ce)
findings.evidence: ce_memory.py:272 `mag_bwf[i] = y[inds[-1]] - y[inds[0]]`; ce.cu:435 `Hc += N * log((mag_bwf[m] * Nphi) / N)` -> log(0). Quantized/discrete magnitudes (common for catalog photometry rounded to 0.01 mag with N >> distinct values) trigger it. Verified on device (ce_followup2.py zerowidth): 'y with 5 distinct values, balanced_magbins=True: mag_bwf=[0.25 0.25 0.   0.25 0.25] -> CE finite=False n(-inf)=100'. Also the widths exclude inter-bin gaps and do not sum to 1 (sum=0.993 in the continuous case), which the docs do not mention.
findings.recommendation: Define bin widths from edges at midpoints between adjacent groups (so widths tile [0,1] and are > 0), or clamp `mag_bwf = max(mag_bwf, 1/(mag_bins*N))`; raise a clear error if any width is 0.

findings.title: CE fast path launches only floor(2*shmem_lim/shmem) blocks (5-34 on a 128-SM GPU); fast is slower than standard, and 128-512 blocks are 1.5-3.6x faster than the default grid
findings.method: Conditional Entropy use_fast=True (ce_classical_faster grid sizing)
findings.evidence: ce.py:140 `grid = (int(np.floor(2 * float(shmem_lim) / shmem)), 1)` whenever the light curve fits in shared memory; each block then loops over all frequencies with stride gridDim.x. Verified on device (ce_followup.py grid): 'device SMs=128 shmem_lim=49152'; 'ndata=300: shmem/block=2840 B -> default grid=34 blocks', 'ndata=1000 -> 11 blocks', 'ndata=2000 -> 5 blocks'. Timings (nf=200000, min of 7, shared 4090 -- noisy, relative only): ndata=300 standard=0.1405 fast(default)=0.2946 nblocks=128:0.1311; ndata=2000 standard=0.2566 fast(default)=0.4415 nblocks=512:0.1224 (results identical, d=0). ce_audit.py timing (nf=50000): standard 0.118-0.126 s vs fast shmem 0.14-0.50 s, i.e. the documented 'speed up' path (ce.py:190-192 'perfect for large Nfreqs and nobs <~ 2000') is slower than the standard path in every measurement. A second min-of-15 run (ce_followup2.py grid2) showed 1.1-1.5x under heavier contention; the other job on the GPU makes absolute numbers unreliable.
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python ce_followup.py grid && python ce_followup2.py grid2'
findings.recommendation: Size the grid from the device: `nblocks = min(nf, occupancy_blocks_per_sm * MULTIPROCESSOR_COUNT)` (pycuda's func.get_attribute / cuOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor, or simply 8*SM count), and apply max_nblocks consistently; re-benchmark fast vs standard and fix the docstring.
findings.expected_gain: 1.5-3.6x for use_fast runs (repeated relative measurements on a shared RTX 4090; A5000 not measured)

findings.title: CE rejects float32 (and any non-Python-float) frequency arrays with a misleading 'number of frequency grids does not match number of lightcurves' error
findings.method: Conditional Entropy run()/allocate()/large_run() frequency handling
findings.evidence: ce.py:508 `elif isinstance(frqs[0], float): frqs = [frqs] * len(data)` -- np.float32 is not a subclass of float (np.float64 is), so a float32 grid is treated as a list of per-lightcurve grids. Verified on device (ce_audit.py edge): 'float32 freqs {} -> EXC ValueError: number of frequency grids (50) does not match number of lightcurves (1)' for standard, use_fast and weighted. pdm.py:339 already uses `(float, np.floating)` and accepts float32 ('float32 freqs (explicit) -> ok').
findings.recommendation: Use `np.ndim(freqs) == 1` (or isinstance(frqs[0], (float, np.floating, np.integer))) in the three places; add a float32-freqs test.

findings.title: PDM folds in float32 with float32 frequencies and has no double option: at t*f ~ 1e5 cycles the statistic is off by up to 3.8e-2 and the argmax moves
findings.method: PDM (all kinds); CE float32 default likewise
findings.evidence: pdm.py:152 `t_g.set_async(np.asarray(t).astype(np.float32))`, pdm.py:258 `freqs_g = gpuarray.to_gpu(np.asarray(freqs).astype(np.float32))`, pdm.cu:7 `#define PHASE(x,f) (x * f - floorf(x * f))`. Mean-subtraction (normalize_light_curves) makes BJD offsets harmless (BJD run identical to t0=0), but the phase error is ~6e-8 * |t*f| cycles. Verified on device (pdm_audit.py precision, N=500, nbins=10 unless noted): baseline 365 d, fmax 20/d: max|gpu-ref64| 3.4e-3; baseline 3650 d, fmax 50/d: 1.1e-2 (argmax unchanged); baseline 3650, fmax 50, nbins=50: max|d|=3.81e-2, 'argmax ref=1056 gpu=759'. CE (ce_audit.py edge): 'baseline=3650 fmax=50: float32 vs double: max|d|=1.123e-02 argmin32=1941 argmin64=1837'. For ordinary data (30 d, f<5/d) the GPU matches a float32-phase reference to <6e-7 and deviates from float64 only through bin-edge flips (up to 3.6e-2 at single frequencies for gappy data, nbins=25; pdm_audit.py ref32).
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python pdm_audit.py precision && python pdm_audit.py ref32'
findings.recommendation: Either add a DOUBLE_PRECISION template path to pdm.cu (as ce.cu/lomb.cu have) exposed as use_double, or at minimum document the |t*f| <~ 1e4-cycle guidance in docs/source/pdm.rst and ce.rst (10-year baselines with f > 10/d exceed it).

findings.title: PDM returns 1 - SS_within/SS_total without Stellingwerf's degrees-of-freedom correction; docs/notebook quote the (N-M)/(N-1) formulas and claim Theta ~ 1 for noise
findings.method: PDM binned_step / binned_linterp (and by extension binless)
findings.evidence: pdm.cu:227 `power[i] = 1.f - var_step_function(...) / var;` with var = sum w (y-ybar)^2 (no dof terms). The notebook defines sigma^2 = sum(x-xbar)^2/(N-1), s^2 = sum(n_j-1)s_j^2/(sum n_j - M) and states cuvarbase returns 1-Theta; pdm.rst:19 says 'Theta ~ 1 for noise'. Verified on device (pdm_audit.py theta, white noise, nbins=10): 'N=20: mean(returned P)=0.399 (expect (M-1)/(N-1)=0.474) mean(1-theta_S78)=-0.003 max|P-(1-theta_S78)|=1.075'; 'N=50: 0.185 vs 0.001, max diff 0.453'; 'N=1000: 0.009'. So for the 'few irregularly spaced observations' regime PDM is advertised for, the returned power has an nbins- and N-dependent positive bias, the values are not comparable across nbins, and (since M = number of occupied bins varies with frequency for gappy data) the ranking can differ from Stellingwerf's.
findings.recommendation: Document the exact statistic (weighted SS ratio, no dof correction, noise expectation (M-1)/(N-1)) in pdm.rst and the notebook; optionally add a `dof_correction=True` option that scales by (N-1)/(N-M_occupied) per frequency (trivial to add on the host for binned kinds since M can be computed in-kernel).

findings.title: PDM deprecated (t, y, w, freqs) path silently returns power == 1.0 everywhere when the weights are not normalized to sum 1
findings.method: PDM run() legacy input format
findings.evidence: pdm.py:147-148 `ybar = np.dot(w, y); var = np.float32(np.dot(w, np.power(y - ybar, 2)))` assume sum(w)=1; nothing normalizes user-supplied w and neither the run() docstring (pdm.py:290) nor pdm.rst:110 says so. Verified on device (pdm_audit.py formats, w = 1/err^2 unnormalized): every kind returns 'unnorm min/max=1/1' (flat spectrum of 1.0) versus reference peak 0.92-0.93; with w=weights(err) the deprecated and modern paths agree exactly (max|dep-modern|=0).
findings.recommendation: Normalize inside run()/pdm_async (`w = w / np.sum(w)`) -- the statistic is scale-invariant in w so this is always safe -- or document the requirement and raise if |sum(w)-1| > 1e-3.

findings.title: CE run(memory=..., set_data=False) never zeroes bins_g, so histograms accumulate across calls (atomicInc wraps; log_prob not scale-invariant)
findings.method: Conditional Entropy run() with pre-allocated memory
findings.evidence: ce.py:527-530 only call set_gpu_arrays_to_zero() inside `elif set_data:`; conditional_entropy() (ce.py:32) runs the histogram kernel without a fill. Verified on device (ce_followup.py accum, N=60, 50 freqs): 'run 0 set_data=True: total bins=3000 ... run 1 set_data=False: total bins=6000, max bin=14 ... run 3: total bins=12000, max bin=28' while ce[0] stays -0.43332 (CE is invariant to a uniform count scale, which hides the bug). The atomicInc limit (PO+1)(MO+1)*ndata (ce.cu:96) wraps a bin to 0 once it exceeds N, and log_prob (Poisson likelihood) is not scale-invariant, so repeated set_data=False calls silently corrupt those outputs.
findings.recommendation: Zero bins_g on memory.stream at the top of conditional_entropy()/conditional_entropy_fast() (a gpuarray.fill), independent of set_data.

findings.title: PDM binned_step (non-fast) reads bin_means[NBINS] out of bounds when a float32 phase rounds to exactly 1.0
findings.method: PDM kind='binned_step' (var_step_function)
findings.evidence: pdm.cu:36 applies `bin = bin % NBINS` in the accumulation loop but the second loop (pdm.cu:49-50 `bin = (int) (PHASE(t[i], freq) * NBINS); var_tot += w[i] * (y[i] - bin_means[bin]) ...`) does not. PHASE(x,f)=x*f-floorf(x*f) equals 1.0f in float32 when x*f is in (-2^-25, 0) (mean-subtracted t is negative for half the points), giving bin = NBINS. Verified on device (pdm_audit.py phase1b; data with one point at t=-1e-9, f=2,3,0.5): '30 seeds, per-frequency max|binned_step - ref32| = [0.019 0.014 0.017 0.024]' vs 'binned_step_fast - ref32 = [1.8e-02 1.5e-08 2.1e-08 3.1e-08]' and a control without the phase==1 point '[4.1e-02 3.4e-07 2.7e-07 2.7e-07]' (f=1 column is contaminated by exact-edge rounding in my reference; the f=2,3,0.5 columns isolate the OOB read). Practically rare (|t*f| < 3e-8 cycles) but undefined behaviour.
findings.recommendation: Add `bin = bin % NBINS;` (or `min(bin, NBINS-1)`) after pdm.cu:49, matching every other kernel.

findings.title: Docs overstate the _fast kernels: PDM 'substantially quicker on large datasets' and CE use_fast 'perfect for large Nfreqs' are not borne out (0.7-2x, ~1.0x for binned PDM; CE fast slower than standard)
findings.method: PDM *_fast kinds; CE use_fast
findings.evidence: pdm.rst:53 'The fast kernels are substantially quicker on large datasets'. Verified on device (pdm_followup.py timing2, min of 10, nf=20000 binned / 2000 binless, shared 4090 -- relative only): binned_step/linterp nbins=10 fast/orig = 1.64x, 1.03x (N=200); 1.01x, 0.99x (N=1000); 1.02x, 1.05x (N=5000); 1.09x, 1.01x (N=20000); binless_tophat 0.73-0.75x (fast SLOWER); binless_gauss 1.3-2.0x. The numerical-equivalence claim ('~1e-6') does hold: max|fast-orig| <= 1.2e-6 over all configs. The binless *_fast kernels (pdm.cu:358 onward) reload the whole light curve into shared memory once per outer point j, so they do ndata/blockDim extra tile loads per j versus the L1/L2-cached original. CE: ce.py:190-192 docstring vs ce_audit.py timing 'standard=0.1179s fast shmem=0.1399s ... ndata=3000: standard=0.1176s fast shmem=0.5007s' (see the grid-size finding for the cause).
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python pdm_followup.py timing2 && python ce_audit.py timing'
findings.recommendation: Re-benchmark on the A5000 and soften/correct both statements; for binless_*_fast, load the light curve once when ndata*12 B fits in shared memory instead of per-j.
findings.expected_gain: docs only; binless fast could recover the 0.75x regression (small)

findings.title: No input validation in PDM/CE: constant y, NaN, dy=0 and oversized fast-CE histograms produce silent NaN / silently mis-binned points / cryptic cuLaunchKernel errors
findings.method: PDM and CE input handling
findings.evidence: Verified on device (pdm_audit.py edge; ce_audit.py edge/constant): PDM constant y -> all NaN (var=0, pdm.py:148), NaN in y -> all NaN, dy=0 at one point -> all NaN (utils.py:9 weights inf/inf), N=1 -> NaN; no warning or error. CE: constant y -> yscale=0 (ce_memory.py:300) -> all NaN; NaN in y -> Python builtin max()/min() skip NaN positionally, floor(NaN)->uint32 0 (ce_memory.py:317) so the NaN point is silently counted in mag bin 0 and a finite spectrum is returned ('NaN in y (standard) -> finite=True'); weighted with dy=0 everywhere -> NaN. use_fast with phase_bins=200, mag_bins=100 -> 'LogicError: cuLaunchKernel failed: invalid argument' (shared-memory request 80 KB > 48 KB limit, no check at ce.py:119). N < nbins/mag_bins works in both (PDM returns finite, CE returns log(1/mag_bins) constants).
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python pdm_audit.py edge && python ce_audit.py edge && python ce_audit.py constant'
findings.recommendation: Validate finite t/y/dy and yscale>0 / var>0 up front with a clear ValueError (shared helper in utils); in conditional_entropy_fast raise ValueError if shmem > shmem_lim before launching.

findings.title: CE returned value is Graham's H(m|phi) + log((mag_overlap+1)/mag_bins) (i.e. -log(mag_bins) by default); log_prob direction and several docstring/hygiene mismatches undocumented
findings.method: Conditional Entropy documentation/hygiene
findings.evidence: ce.rst:9 gives H = sum p log(p(phi)/p(m,phi)) but ce.cu:396 computes `Hc += N * log((dm * Nphi) / N)` with dm=(MAG_OVERLAP+1)/NMAG. Verified on device (ce_audit.py hist): 'graham offset (gpu - H_graham) mean=-1.6069 expect log(1/5)=-1.6094' (residual is the y==1 misbinning). log_prob (ce.cu:490) is the Poisson log-likelihood under the phase-independent null and is MINIMIZED at the true frequency (ce_audit.py logprob: 'argmin gpu=165 (f=1.299)' for injected 1.3) -- not stated anywhere; matches a numpy re-implementation to 8e-5 given the mis-binned max point. ce.py:176 docstring 'mag_bins ... (default: 10)' vs ce.py:214 default 5. conditional_entropy_fast (ce.py:92, 149) launches on `stream=None` (legacy null stream) instead of memory.stream, serializing multi-lightcurve fast runs. ce_classical_faster loads y into y_sh but reads global `y[i]` (ce.cu:304). Weighted-CE `widen_mag_range` is only reachable via run(**kwargs).
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python ce_audit.py hist && python ce_audit.py logprob'
findings.recommendation: Document the dm normalization and the log_prob sign convention in ce.rst and the class docstring; fix the mag_bins default text; pass memory.stream in conditional_entropy_fast; use y_sh in ce_classical_faster.

findings.title: PDM docs/notebook hygiene: dphi semantics ambiguous in run() docstring, notebook never passes dphi and labels binless plots chi^2, dead macros in pdm.cu
findings.method: PDM documentation
findings.evidence: pdm.py:299-300 'dphi: Phase width for binless PDM' while pdm.cu uses it as the tophat HALF-width (`phase_diff(...) < dphi`, pdm.cu:120) and as the Gaussian sigma (pdm.cu:141 `GAUSSIAN(dphase / dphi)`); pdm.rst:45-48 describes this correctly. The notebook's binless cells set `dphi = 0.05` but call run(..., nbins=nbins) without dphi, and label the y-axis '$\chi^2$' although the value is 1-Theta; the notebook also quotes the dof-corrected Stellingwerf formulas (see the statistics finding). pdm.cu:2-5 define WEIGHT, WEIGHTED_LININTERP, SKIP_BIN which are never used. By inspection.
findings.recommendation: Reword the docstring ('half-width of the tophat / sigma of the Gaussian, in phase'), pass dphi in the notebook and fix labels, delete the dead macros.

findings.title: NFFTAsyncProcess.run(memory=...) reuse path returns unsynchronized data and accumulates onto the un-zeroed grid; the default path only works because dropping the per-call gpuarrays forces cuMemFree's implicit device sync
findings.method: Device: 50 immediate reads of the returned pinned buffer vs after synchronize, for the default (fresh memory) path and the kept-memory path; inspection of fast_gaussian_grid and nfft_adjoint_async for zeroing/sync.
findings.evidence: exp7: 'immediate-read mismatches: current path 0/50, kept-memory path 49/50' at n=600, 5000, 50000. cunfft.py:164-168 `memory.transfer_nfft_to_cpu(); return memory.ghat_c` with no stream.synchronize (only the just_return_gridded_data branch at :127 syncs); cunfft.cu:158-162 ATOMIC_ADD into `grid` with no zeroing anywhere in nfft_adjoint_async - the grid is zero only because allocate() creates it with gpuarray.zeros. nufft_lrt.py:339 `np.asarray(ghat, dtype=self.complex_type)` is a no-copy view of the pinned buffer.
findings.recommendation: In nfft_adjoint_async: zero ghat_g before gridding (memory.ghat_g.fill(0, stream)) and synchronize the stream before returning when transfer_to_host=True (or document that callers must sync). This unblocks the buffer-reuse performance fix above.

findings.title: Under irregular sampling the statistic is over-dispersed even with the ORACLE PSD (null std 2.0-2.2 on ground-based sampling); the README's explanation (estimated-PSD correlation) is wrong and the harness expects ~N(0,1)
findings.method: Monte-Carlo null on device: 200 white-noise realizations, fixed template, true white PSD vs estimated PSD (windows 1/5/21/101/global), uniform vs ground sampling; OU red noise with an oracle PSD (mean |S_k|^2 over 200 independent realizations) vs estimated.
findings.evidence: exp2 ground sampling: 'true white PSD nf=600 std=2.155', 'nf=1200 std=2.650', 'estimated PSD window=5 std=2.440', 'window=global std=2.628'; red noise 'oracle PSD std=3.055 | estimated(win=5) std=2.776'. exp10 ground: 'k<nf/2 only: true-white-PSD std=2.032'. Uniform sampling with k<nf/2: 1.04. So the residual over-dispersion is the spectral-window mode correlation of irregular sampling, not the PSD estimate. README:116-121 says 'measured std ~1.7 ... the estimated-PSD modes are correlated and shared between numerator and normalization'; campaign.log 'mean=0.007 std=1.812 (want ~0, ~1)'. The std depends on the sampling pattern (1.8 vs 2.4 for two ground realizations).
findings.reproduction: bash scratchpad/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch/lrtaud && python lrtaud_exp2_null.py; python lrtaud_exp10.py'
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the caveat: the statistic is a whitened correlation whose null scale depends on nf/n and on the sampling pattern; it is not an SNR. Longer term, compute the exact time-domain GLS statistic tau^T C^-1 y / sqrt(tau^T C^-1 tau) with C_ij built from the estimated PSD (autocorrelation at lags t_i - t_j via one NFFT) - N(0,1) by construction for n up to a few thousand.

findings.title: Self-whitening (PSD estimated from the signal-containing data) costs 24-28% of SNR already at the detection threshold, not 'mild'
findings.method: Device: same red+white noise realization, box transits of depth 0.003-0.1 at the true template; SNR with the default estimated PSD vs the PSD of the transit-free noise.
findings.evidence: exp8: 'depth 0.003: est-PSD 4.38 | clean-PSD 5.80 (ratio 0.76)', 'depth 0.010: 14.53 | 20.18 (0.72)', 'depth 0.030: 28.61 | 61.29 (0.47)', 'depth 0.100: 34.14 | 205.29 (0.17)'. Prior audit finding 5 calls the effect 'mild for shallow transits'.
