findings.recommendation: Quantify in the README; consider a robust smoother (running median x 1/ln2 for chi2_2 bins) or a leave-template-out PSD (subtract the best-fit box before re-estimating) as an option.

findings.title: eps_floor=1e-12*median is not a floor: a zero bin in a user PSD yields SNR=1e6 (matched) or nan (marginal, where the floor is never applied)
findings.method: Device: run() with estimate_psd=False and psd=ones with every 7th bin zero, detector='matched' vs 'marginal'.
findings.evidence: t4.log: 'user psd with zeros: matched=[1053138.25]  marginal=[nan]'. :600 floors at eps_floor*median only in _compute_matched_filter_snr; _whitened_inner (:42) divides by psd directly and the user-supplied branch (:483-485) applies no floor. test_power_spectrum_floor_prevents_blowup only checks finiteness with eps_floor=1e-6.
findings.recommendation: Floor the PSD once in run() for every path (default eps_floor ~1e-3 of the median, which caps any single bin's weight at 1000x) and validate len(psd)==nf.

findings.title: Singular coeff_prior_cov is inverted with pinv, which turns a zero prior variance into an improper flat prior (the opposite limit)
findings.method: CPU: _marginal_statistic with prior diag(1,0) vs the K=1 statistic (v2 fixed) and vs diag(1,1e-12) and diag(1,1e12).
findings.evidence: t4.log: 'Detector A prior_cov=diag(1,0): got 0.922339 | correct limit (v2 fixed, K=1) 0.727811 | cov=diag(1,1e-12) 0.727811 | cov=diag(1,1e12) (flat on v2) 0.922339'. :79 `M = np.linalg.pinv(np.linalg.pinv(prior_cov) + G)`. np.cov of population fits with few lightcurves or a degenerate PCA mode gives exactly this case.
findings.reproduction: python3 scratchpad/lrt/lrtaud_exp4_detectors.py (CPU section) or on pod: bash scratchpad/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch/lrtaud && python lrtaud_exp4_detectors.py'
findings.recommendation: Use the singular-safe form (C^-1 + G)^-1 = C (I + G C)^-1 via np.linalg.solve, which never inverts C; raise on non-PSD input.

findings.title: API/docs: PSD convention for psd= undocumented (psd=ones gives a statistic in data units), run() return shape docstring wrong for epochs=None, README validation section is an empty placeholder pointing at a non-existent results directory
findings.method: Inspection plus device measurement of the psd=ones null scale.
findings.evidence: exp2: 'psd=ones (README example 4 style) white noise: std=0.0337 (uniform) / 0.0649 (ground)' - the required convention is E|S_k|^2 of the UNnormalized adjoint NFFT (n*sigma^2 for white noise) over all nf modes k/(tmax-tmin), stated nowhere. :407-408 'shape (len(periods), len(durations), len(epochs))' but exp3 shows shape=(32, 1) for epochs=None. README:160 '<!-- VALIDATION_RESULTS -->' unfilled; README:78,168 cite benchmarks/results/nufft_lrt_validation_jul2026/ which does not exist (`ls` -> No such file or directory).
findings.recommendation: Document the PSD convention with a formula and a white-noise example; fix the return-shape docstring; fill or remove the validation placeholder and the dead path reference.

findings.title: cuvarbase cannot be called from a thread other than the one that first touched the GPU: ensure_context() never makes the primary context current in new threads
findings.method: base.context.ensure_context; all GPU entry points when called from worker threads
findings.evidence: context.py:34-40 caches the pycuda.autoprimaryctx module and returns it; the CUDA driver context stack is per-thread, so the kernel LRU cache (bls.py:110-165, lock-protected, 'Thread-safe for concurrent access from multiple threads') hands out functions that cannot be launched. Device (h4 threads): 4 worker threads calling eebls_gpu_fast all raise 'LogicError: explicit_context_dependent failed: invalid device context - no currently active context?' while the main thread keeps working; with `ensure_context().context.push()` at thread start all threads return results matching the main thread to 3e-8 (h9 thread_push).
findings.reproduction: bash pod.sh 'cd /workspace/cuvarbase && python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h4_state.py threads && python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h9_last.py thread_push'
findings.recommendation: In ensure_context(): after the first-call setup, `if cuda.Context.get_current() is None: _autoctx.context.push()` (track per-thread via threading.local so pops happen once), and document that CUDA contexts do not survive os.fork (child gets 'cuDeviceGetAttribute failed: initialization error', h7 context2; multiprocessing 'spawn' works).

findings.title: After any kernel fault the process is permanently poisoned with confusing errors and nothing in cuvarbase detects or reports it
findings.method: base.context.ensure_context and every GPU entry point after a sticky CUDA error
findings.evidence: After eebls_transit_gpu(N=3, use_fast=True) faults, a valid eebls_gpu_fast call raises 'cuMemAlloc failed: an illegal memory access was encountered', later calls in the same run raised 'cuModuleLoadDataEx failed: an illegal memory access', 'UnicodeDecodeError: utf-8 codec can't decode byte 0xe0' (from pycuda's compile-cache path) and 'RuntimeError: make_default_context() wasn't able to create a context'; ensure_context() keeps returning the cached module (h4 sticky_nanfreq, h2_edge.out first run). Users will not connect these to the earlier NaN input.
findings.recommendation: Wrap kernel launches/syncs in the entry points so a pycuda LogicError/LaunchError is re-raised as a cuvarbase RuntimeError that says the CUDA context is dead and the process must be restarted; combined with the input validation above this becomes unreachable on valid input.

findings.title: sparse_bls_gpu fails with a cryptic 'cuLaunchKernel failed: invalid argument' above ~2000 points (48 KB static shared-memory limit, no opt-in) and recompiles its kernel on every call
findings.method: bls.sparse_bls_gpu, eebls_transit(use_sparse=True)
findings.evidence: bls.py:2131 shared = (3*n_pow2 + 2*N + 3*block)*4: N=2000 -> 41344 B ok; N=2500 -> 69920 B and N=3000/6000/20000 -> 'LogicError: cuLaunchKernel failed: invalid argument' (h3 sparse_big, h7 sparse_limit), no size check and no set_attribute(MAX_DYNAMIC_SHARED_SIZE_BYTES) opt-in as tls.py:1085 does. Per-call compile: bls.py:2102 `kernel = compile_sparse_bls(...)` is not cached; repeated calls 0.155/0.151/0.138/0.157 s vs 0.024 s with kernel= (h8 perf_compile; relative timings, shared 4090).
findings.expected_gain: ~6x per sparse_bls_gpu call at N=600/100 freqs (0.15 s -> 0.024 s) by caching the compiled kernel
findings.reproduction: bash pod.sh 'cd /workspace/cuvarbase && python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h7_followups.py sparse_limit && python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h8_more.py perf_compile'
findings.recommendation: Raise a ValueError with the N limit (or opt in to >48 KB dynamic shared memory on sm_70+ like compile_tls_fast) before launching; cache compile_sparse_bls in _kernel_cache keyed by (block_size, use_simple).

findings.title: Lomb-Scargle host preprocessing uses Python built-in sum/min/max over numpy arrays: 77% of run() wall time at N=1e6
findings.method: LombScargleMemory.setdata / memory.lombscargle_memory.weights (all LS entry points)
findings.evidence: lombscargle_memory.py:31 `return w/sum(w)`, :325-326 `self.tmin = min(t); self.tmax = max(t)`. Device profile of LombScargleAsyncProcess.run for N=1e6, nf=2000 (h8 perf_host): total 0.392 s of which builtins.min 0.145 s, builtins.sum 0.096 s, builtins.max 0.059 s (np.sum: 0.0006 s; np.min/max: 0.0003 s). Relative timings on a shared 4090.
findings.expected_gain: ~3x end-to-end for run() at N=1e6 (0.39 s -> ~0.09 s), negligible below N~1e5
findings.recommendation: Use np.sum(w), t.min(), t.max() (also utils.weights uses np.sum already; make memory.weights identical).

findings.title: use_fft=False and python_dir_sums=True silently compute the single-harmonic periodogram when nharmonics>1
findings.method: LombScargleAsyncProcess(nharmonics=H).run(..., use_fft=False) and run(..., python_dir_sums=True)
findings.evidence: lombscargle.py:442 `if not use_fft:` launches lomb_dirsum (H=1 only, lomb.cu:168-190) and :434 `return lomb_scargle_direct_sums(t, yw, w, freqs, memory.yy)` omits nharms. Device (h10): with nharmonics=2 and 3, use_fft=False output equals the H=1 CPU direct sums to 1.5e-6 and differs from the H=2/3 reference by rel 0.98 (corr 0.60); the NFFT multiharmonic path itself agrees with lomb_scargle_direct_sums(nharms=H) to 2.8e-3 (k0/nf=0.03).
findings.recommendation: Pass nharms=memory.nharmonics to lomb_scargle_direct_sums for python_dir_sums, and either raise NotImplementedError for use_fft=False with nharmonics>1 or fall back to the CPU multiharmonic direct sums.

findings.title: batched_run_const_nfreq(only_return_best_freqs=True) returns significance = 1 - FAP (exactly 1.0 for any real peak) and uses the H=1 degrees of freedom for multiharmonic runs
findings.method: LombScargleAsyncProcess.batched_run_const_nfreq(only_return_best_freqs=True)
findings.evidence: lombscargle.py:981-982 `fap = fap_baluev(batch[i][0], batch[i][2], p[mask], np.max(freqs[mask])); significance = 1. - fap[best_index]` with the default d_K=3. Device (h9 fap_mh): nharmonics=2 on the test signal returns significance=1 (implied FAP 0) while fap_baluev gives 2.6e-90 (d_K=3) and 4.9e-87 with the correct d_K=2H+1=5; the log-space rewrite of fap_baluev (issue #14) is defeated by the 1-fap return. fap_baluev itself matches astropy's Baluev formula for H=1 (astropy underflows to 0 where cuvarbase returns 1.05e-89).
findings.recommendation: Return the FAP (or log10 FAP) instead of 1-FAP, and pass d_K=2*self.nharmonics+1 to fap_baluev.

findings.title: Binned BLS and TLS results change by up to ~10% (BLS) / 2% (TLS chi2) depending only on the fractional part of min(t) (phase-bin/t0-grid alignment to floor(min(t)))
findings.method: eebls_gpu_fast/optimized/adaptive/eebls_gpu/eebls_gpu_batch/eebls_transit(_gpu), tls_search_gpu/tls_search_batch
findings.evidence: utils.py:74 epoch = floor(min(t)) anchors the phase grid. Device (h1b): t+0.5 vs t (no BJD): eebls_gpu_fast maxabs=0.0257 rel=0.10 corr=0.970 (noverlap=1: 0.11; 4: 0.091; 8: 0.076), eebls_gpu rel 0.10, eebls_transit argmax DIFF; tls_fast rel 0.018, tls t+0.3333 argmax DIFF; t+2457000.5 equals t+0.5 to 1e-8 (so this is discretization, not precision). sparse_bls_gpu (no binning) is invariant to 4.7e-4. Integer shifts are bit-exact.
findings.recommendation: Document in the BLS/TLS docstrings and the subtract_epoch note that peak heights/locations are stable only to the phase-oversampling level (noverlap/t0_oversample) and recommend refining candidates with sparse_bls or eebls_gpu_custom/hone_solution; optionally offer an epoch= argument.

findings.title: float32 inputs are accepted and silently cast; float32 absolute-scale times destroy every method's result with no warning
findings.method: all entry points
findings.evidence: h1 'f32' variant (float32 t,y,dy at t~0..100) matches float64 to <=1e-5 for BLS/LS/PDM, 7.7e-3 for CE (float32 phase quantization), 2.4e-5 TLS; the 'f32_bjd' variant (float32 t at 2457000.5, i.e. 0.25-day resolution) gives corr 0.58 (BLS), 0.72 (LS), 0.61 (CE), 0.63 (PDM), 0.93 (TLS) and no warning. utils.subtract_epoch documents float64 subtraction but cannot recover precision already lost by the caller's dtype.
findings.reproduction: bash pod.sh 'cd /workspace/cuvarbase && python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h1_invariance.py bls_fast ls ce pdm_linterp tls_fast'
findings.recommendation: In subtract_epoch/normalize_light_curves warn (or raise) when t.dtype is float32/float16 and max|t| > ~1e4; state in every docstring that inputs are cast to float32 on device after epoch subtraction.

findings.title: Memory-reuse and buffered paths fail with unhelpful messages or silently mix stale data
findings.method: eebls_gpu_fast(memory=...), TLSMemory reuse, LombScargleAsyncProcess.preallocate, PDMAsyncProcess.run(gpu_data=...)
findings.evidence: h4 bls_memory/tls_state/ls_state/ce_pdm_state: BLSMemory reused with nf=700<alloc 1500 or nf=2500>1500 -> 'ValueError: ary and self must be the same size'; ndata 1200>900 -> 'could not broadcast input array from shape (1200,) into shape (900,)'; TLS legacy memory with a shorter LC -> 'ary and self must be the same size'; LS preallocate(max_nobs=700) then N=900 -> 'requirement `self.n0 <= len(self.t)` not satisfied'; PDM gpu_data sized for N=600 reused for N=900 -> 'ary and self must be the same size'. eebls_gpu_fast(memory=m, transfer_to_device=False) with arrays of a different length launches with np.uint32(len(t)) of the caller's arrays (bls.py:781) over the memory's stale tail: result matched neither LC (rel 0.19 vs snr(A)). Correct reuse cases (same sizes, chunked BLSBatchMemory reuse with fewer LCs / fewer freqs) all matched fresh results to <=2e-7.
findings.reproduction: bash pod.sh 'cd /workspace/cuvarbase && python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h4_state.py bls_memory; python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h4_state.py tls_state; python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h4_state.py ls_state'
findings.recommendation: Check ndata<=max_ndata and nf<=max_nfreqs in BLSMemory.setdata/TLSMemory.setdata/LombScargleMemory.setdata and raise a ValueError naming the allocation; on transfer_to_device=False use the memory's recorded ndata/nfreqs instead of len(t)/len(freqs).

findings.title: Confusing error messages for common mistakes and large sizes
findings.method: various
findings.evidence: Integer dy -> 'Integers to negative integer powers are not allowed' (BLS/LS/PDM); empty freqs -> 'error: required argument is not an integer' (BLS fast/std/custom, CE, tls legacy) or 'zero-size array to reduction operation maximum' (eebls_gpu_batch); LS single-element freqs -> 'IndexError: index 1 is out of bounds'; LS freqs given as a Python list to batched_run_const_nfreq -> 'number of frequency grids (300) does not match number of lightcurves (1)' (lombscargle.py:834 treats any list as per-LC grids); CE run() at N=1e6 x nf=1e6 -> 'OverflowError: Number of streams is too large' (it is threads, and large_run handles it: 667 s); tls_search_batch with period<=0 or NaN -> 'nbins must be a power of two' while tls_search_gpu returns finite chi2 at period 0; NUFFT-LRT N<=2 -> 'operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (4,) (5,)'; eebls_transit N=0 -> ZeroDivisionError. Large inputs otherwise behave: eebls_gpu_fast/batch N=1e6 or nf=1e6 ok, LS 1e6x1e6 ok, TLS fast N=1e6 and 1e6 periods ok, legacy TLS N=20000 raises a clear shared-memory message, qmin=1e-5 raises a clear message.
findings.reproduction: bash pod.sh 'bash /workspace/scratch/xcut/h2_driver.sh'; bash pod.sh 'cd /workspace/cuvarbase && python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h2f_freqs.py; for w in bls_bigN bls_bignf sparse_big tls_big ls_big ce_big pdm_big; do python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h3_large.py $w; done'
findings.recommendation: Covered by the shared validator above plus: cast dy with np.asarray(dy, float64) before the -2 power; accept 1-D array-likes for freqs in batched_run_const_nfreq; reword the CE overflow message.

findings.title: Run-to-run non-determinism from float atomics (BLS fast/batch, TLS fast) and fork/thread semantics are undocumented
findings.method: eebls_gpu_fast*, eebls_gpu_batch, tls_search_gpu/tls_search_batch, base.context
findings.evidence: Same input twice: eebls_gpu_fast maxabs 1.3e-8 (not bitwise), eebls_gpu_batch not bitwise (rel 9e-8), tls chi2 spread 4.6e-5 absolute (3e-8 rel) with SDE/period/t0 stable; CE, PDM, LS(single LC) and sparse BLS are bitwise. Fork after context creation: child raises 'cuDeviceGetAttribute failed: initialization error', spawn pool works (h7 context2). ensure_context is idempotent and no context is created at import (verified).
findings.reproduction: bash pod.sh 'cd /workspace/cuvarbase && python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h4_state.py bls_batch_det; python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h7_followups.py tls_batch_consistency; python /workspace/scratch/xcut/h7_followups.py context2'
findings.recommendation: State the ~1e-7 relative run-to-run tolerance in the BLS/TLS docstrings and tests; document 'no fork after first GPU use; use multiprocessing spawn' in base/README.

findings.title: eebls_gpu / eebls_gpu_custom default max_memory = 0.9 x free device memory: every call allocates and zero-fills up to ~19 GB (4 arrays x 5 streams) on a 24 GB card, hostile on shared GPUs and pure overhead
findings.method: Arithmetic from the shipped sizing code + measured allocation under a cap (monkeypatched gpuarray.zeros)
findings.evidence: On the pod (free 21.1 GB) default_max_memory would be 19.0 GB; for TESS 1788 freqs the default allocation is 333 MB (fbs 107,911 > nfreq), for any grid with nfreq > fbs (ZTF 60K, HAT 300K, Kepler) the allocation is ~0.9 x free regardless of need. Measured with max_memory=1.5e9/3e9: 1499.4 / 2999.5 MB of gpuarray.zeros per call, 11-17 ms CPU in the zero-fill launches per call, plus 4 .fill() memsets per batch. ZTF eebls_gpu kernels total ~53 ms GPU vs 512-1095 ms wall per call.
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python parity_paths.py'  (eebls_gpu_default_memory block) and prof2_*.json ['std']
findings.recommendation: Size gs from the actual need (nfreq x max-batch nbins_tot x noverlap) and cap the default max_memory at e.g. min(0.5 x free, needed); allocate once per call, not per stream when nstreams > batches; document that default eebls_transit(ndata>=500) can take most of the device.

findings.title: Per-frequency Python loops after the GPU work: solutions re-phasing list comprehensions cost 25-37 ms per call at survey nfreq (sparse_bls_gpu, sparse_bls_cpu, eebls_gpu)
findings.method: Local timing of the exact list-comprehension pattern vs np.mod; device wall-vs-kernel gap
files: cuvarbase/bls.py:2138-2145 (sparse_bls_gpu: new cuda.Stream() and 6 gpuarray.to_gpu per call)
findings.evidence: Local: n=60121 -> 24.7 ms (loop) vs 2.8 ms (np.mod vectorized); n=117403 (eebls_transit default ZTF grid) -> 37.3 vs 4.3 ms. On device sparse_bls_gpu with the kernel supplied: wall 132-175 ms, process CPU 66 ms, kernel (event) 20.2 ms -> ~110 ms of host work around a 20 ms kernel.
findings.reproduction: /usr/bin/python3 -c (see transcript command: python solutions loop vs np.mod);  prof2_ZTF_TESS.json ['ZTF']['sparse']
findings.recommendation: Return solutions as two arrays (or a structured array) computed with np.mod(best_phi.astype(float64) + epoch*freqs64, 1.0); keep the list-of-tuples API via a lazy view if needed. Bit-parity: yes (same float64 ops).

findings.title: BLSMemory.setdata does two full host passes for one normalization (chi2_0 recomputed by _chi2_null although chi2_0 = yy * sum(dy^-2)), recomputes the scatter permutation every call, and re-uploads freqs+nbins when transfer_to_device=True with a reused memory
findings.method: Stage timing + lean-setdata prototype with bitwise array comparison
files: cuvarbase/bls.py:729-732 (memory given + transfer_to_device=True -> setdata with freqs -> nbins recompute + freq re-upload)
findings.evidence: TESS (20000 pts): setdata host 1.12 ms of a 1.43 ms reuse call; _chi2_null alone 0.41 ms, conflict_scatter_perm 0.14 ms. Lean prototype (chi2_0 = yy*wsum, cached perm): setdata 1.12 -> 0.59 ms (min), reuse call 1.44 -> 0.95 ms; t/yw/w/nbinsf bit-identical, yy identical, chi2_0 rel diff 1.2e-15. ZTF 0.19 -> 0.11 ms. HAT prototype was NOT faster with freqs given (0.74 -> 1.57 ms, noisy section; the prototype also carried a stray extra gather) - treat the HAT number as unverified. transfer_to_device=True on a reused memory: ZTF 0.50 -> 0.68 ms, TESS 1.43 -> 1.97, HAT 11.7 -> 12.4.
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python host_proto.py'  (lean_setdata_* keys); prof2_*.json ['fast'] C2/C4/C3 and TOTAL_fast_reuse(transfer_to_device=True)
findings.recommendation: Derive chi2_0 from yy and the un-normalized weight sum; cache conflict_scatter_perm by n (small dict); skip nbins recompute/upload when the freqs object is the one already loaded (identity/hash check). Document (or fix) that memory= with transfer_to_device=True re-uploads the grid.

findings.title: Shared-memory float atomicAdd is a CAS spin loop on sm_89 (ATOMS.CAST.SPIN); packing (yw,w) into one 64-bit CAS is 5x SLOWER - negative result, do not pursue
findings.method: SASS inspection of the shipped kernels compiled with nvcc -arch=sm_89 + prototype kernel with event timing and parity
files: cuvarbase/kernels/bls_common.cuh:229-230 (two atomicAdd per point in full_bls_no_sol_fused)
findings.evidence: cuobjdump -sass bls.cubin: 4 x ATOMS.CAST.SPIN (the shared float atomics in full_bls_no_sol / _fused) and 76 x RED.E.ADD.F32 (global atomics in the bin_and_phase_fold kernels); registers 30/40, no spills. Packed float2 64-bit atomicCAS prototype (same float adds): ZTF 0.205 -> 0.200 ms (1.03x), TESS 0.205 -> 1.05 ms (0.19x), HAT 9.17 -> 44.4 ms (0.21x); parity within run-to-run nondeterminism. Fused kernel vs one pass of the standard kernel: ZTF 0.196 vs 0.218 ms, TESS 0.197 vs 0.276, HAT 8.28 vs 11.8 ms - the July fusion left no per-pass overhead to recover.
findings.recommendation: Record the negative result in analysis/ so it is not retried; the remaining kernel-side headroom for large ndata is in the CAS-loop histogram (privatized/warp-aggregated binning or a sort-based fold), which is a large change with no demonstrated gain here.

findings.title: eebls_gpu_batch docstring overstates batch gains: on the 4090 batch kernel time per LC equals the single-LC fused kernel; the benefit is host-overhead removal only
findings.method: CUDA-event kernel timing single vs batch at three sizes
files: cuvarbase/bls.py:2500-2506 docstring ('~10x at ndata=200, ~6x at 2,000, ~5x at 20,000')
findings.evidence: Batch kernel events (full_bls_batch_fused, 1 launch): ZTF 8 LCs 1.54-1.61 ms = 0.20 ms/LC vs single fused 0.196 ms; TESS 8 LCs 1.26-1.29 ms = 0.16 ms/LC vs 0.197; HAT 4 LCs 33.9-37.2 ms = 8.5-9.3 ms/LC vs 8.28-8.88. Whole-call: batch_reuse ZTF 3.47 ms/8 = 0.43 ms/LC vs fast_reuse 0.40-0.50 ms; batch with a fresh BLSBatchMemory 7.8 ms min / 87 ms median (pinned alloc under contention).
findings.recommendation: State the batch benefit as 'removes per-call host overhead (allocation, launches); kernel throughput per LC is the same once one LC fills the GPU' and cite the reuse-vs-reuse ratio; keep the memory= advice.

findings.title: Docstring/default mismatches in the BLS API
findings.method: Inspection + one device measurement
files: cuvarbase/bls.py:1436 ('dlogq ... default: 0.5' vs signature dlogq=0.2 at :1424)
findings.evidence: eebls_gpu_fast_optimized and eebls_gpu_fast launch the identical full_bls_no_sol_fused kernel at the default noverlap=2 (event time 0.205 vs 0.196 ms ZTF; 0.210 vs 0.197 TESS; 8.27 vs 8.28 HAT).
findings.reproduction: grep -n 'default: 200\|default: 0.5\|Expected speedup' cuvarbase/bls.py ; prof2_*.json optimized_kernel_events vs E_kernel_events
findings.recommendation: Fix the two defaults in the docstrings; replace the speedup claim with 'identical kernel at power-of-two noverlap; differs only for the multi-pass fallback'.

findings.title: BLSBatchMemory computes bin counts from float32 1/qmin while BLSMemory uses float64: off-by-one bin at e.g. qmin=1e-3 (999 vs 1000)
findings.method: Local numpy check of both expressions
findings.evidence: local_checks.py: qmin=0.001 -> f64 1000 bins, f32 999; qmin in {0.01,0.02,0.03,0.05,0.07,0.1,0.003,0.005} agree; on the four Keplerian survey grids nbinsf/nbins0 differ at 0 frequencies.
findings.recommendation: Broadcast qmin/qmax as float64 in set_freqs before the reciprocal so batch and single paths bin identically.

findings.title: Detector A ('marginal') with the default estimate_psd=True whitens with a PSD that still contains the systematics power -> statistic collapses ~7x
findings.method: Device injection experiment (60 nights x 40 pts, sigma=3e-3, three shared systematics modes at 3-6 sigma, PCA basis + coefficient prior estimated from a 60-LC population as in the validation harness): marginal detector with (i) PSD estimated from y - V mu (shipped default), (ii) PSD estimated from the OLS-cotrended residual, (iii) the true white PSD; 4 null and 4 injected (5-sigma depth) light curves, 40 periods x 8 epochs.
findings.evidence: nufft_lrt.py:437-441 subtracts only the prior MEAN (`y = y - V @ mu`) before :466-481 estimate the PSD from |Y_k|^2 of that data, so the realized systematics V(c - mu) are in P(k) AND in Cov_c: the whitening 1/P(k) then suppresses exactly the modes the marginalization is meant to handle. lrt_detC.py: null max-stat psd-from-raw-y [0.52 0.60 1.01 1.05] vs psd-from-cotrended-residual [4.72 4.73 4.69 5.97] vs true psd [5.88 6.33 5.21 6.98]; injected (5 sigma) raw-y [2.73 2.85 6.31 5.01] vs residual [21.2 19.7 17.3 27.0] vs true [43.9 36.2 36.1 55.3]. lrt_detB.py (8 null / 8 inj): marg_est null median 1.02 p95 2.06, injected median 7.52; marg_true null median 6.21, injected median 52.5; sequential-with-true-PSD 52.6 (the marginal and sequential detectors coincide when the prior is wide relative to the noise, as expected). Detection counts (3/8 each) are too small to claim a completeness loss; the collapse of the statistic's scale and margin is the verified effect.
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python lrt_detC.py'  (and lrt_detB.py; both in the audit-tls-ls-lrt scratch dir)
findings.recommendation: For detector='marginal' (and as an option for 'matched'), estimate P(k) from the sequentially cotrended residual (_sequential_detrend(t, y, V)) or from a signal-free population, not from y - V mu; document in NUFFT_LRT_README that the shipped estimate double-counts the basis. Consider exposing psd estimation as a separate call so a survey can reuse one PSD.

findings.title: Frequency-domain whitened inner products overcount the time-domain ones by ~2.2-2.4x, so Detector A's prior Cov_c is effectively ~2.3x wider than specified (small effect on the statistic)
findings.method: Device experiment: for white noise with a supplied flat PSD = N*sigma^2, compared _whitened_inner Gram entries and _marginal_statistic against the exact time-domain Detector A (dense Cov_z = sigma^2 I + V Cov_c V^T) for prior widths 0.03-10 sigma, uniform and irregular sampling.
findings.evidence: lrt_detA.py: Gram freq/time = 2.186 (uniform), 2.350 (irregular); lrt_detA2.py: 2.417. The one-sided sum over nf=2N modes (nufft_lrt.py:39-42, 490 `weights = np.ones(nf)`) counts the aliased upper half band a second time and the upper-band deconvolution error adds more. Because the same factor does not apply to Cov_c^{-1} in `np.linalg.pinv(prior_cov) + G` (line 79), the prior is effectively g*Cov_c. Measured effect: freqA/timeA(Cc) = 1.54, 1.51, 1.50, 1.49, 1.53, 1.50 (+-0.02-0.1) for k = 0.03..10 sigma, i.e. the statistic is a near-constant multiple of the exact one; using g*Cov_c in the time domain changes the ratio by <=2%. The existing CPU test (test_nufft_lrt_import.py TestDetectorAlgebra) only checks the Woodbury algebra against a dense inverse in the SAME realified frequency space, not against the time-domain statistic.
findings.recommendation: Document that the SNR scale is not the time-domain SNR (already stated as 'not N(0,1)') and that the prior is effectively inflated by the transform's Gram factor; optionally normalize the whitened inner products by nf/N (or by the measured Gram ratio of a unit vector) before adding Cov_c^{-1}. Add a CPU test comparing _marginal_statistic to the time-domain Detector A on uniform sampling with a flat PSD.

findings.title: batched_run_const_nfreq(only_return_best_freqs=True) returns significance = 1 - FAP, which rounds to exactly 1.0 for every significant peak
findings.method: Inspection + device run of the option on a 300-point sinusoid.
findings.evidence: lombscargle.py:982 `significance = 1. - fap[best_index]`. ls_parity.py: `only_return_best_freqs: best f=3.100532 ... sig=1 ; fap(full arr)[best]=1.873e-137`. fap_baluev was rewritten in log space specifically so significant peaks do not underflow (issue #14, lines 1029-1050), but the only public consumer of it collapses the result back to 1.0, so users cannot rank or threshold detections from this API.
findings.recommendation: Return the FAP itself (or log10 FAP) alongside the best frequency, keep `1 - fap` only as a documented convenience; note the change in CHANGELOG since it alters the return value.

findings.title: TLS result key 'T0' means transit PHASE in tls_search_gpu/tls_transit but ABSOLUTE mid-transit time in tls_search_batch
findings.method: Inspection + device run of both entry points on the same injected light curve.
findings.evidence: tls.py:631 `'T0': r['t0_phase'],` (legacy dict) vs tls.py:1589 `'T0': epochs[lc_idx] + best_t0 * best_period,`; tls_check.py: tls_transit gives T0=0.2999 (phase) while the injected mid-transit is 2.31 d; reconstructing epoch + T0*P gives 2.3091 (within 0.001 d of truth). A user reading 'T0' from tls_transit as a time (the transitleastsquares meaning) gets a wrong ephemeris.
findings.recommendation: Add 't0_phase' and an absolute 'T0' (epoch + phase*period) to the tls_search_gpu/tls_transit dict, document the epoch (floor(min(t))), and deprecate the phase meaning of 'T0' in the legacy dict.

findings.title: cuvarbase TLS 'SDE' is not the transitleastsquares SDE (different SR transform): thresholds calibrated for the reference package do not transfer
findings.method: Device comparison against transitleastsquares 1.32 on the same injected light curve and grid limits.
findings.evidence: tls_stats.py:46 `SR = 1.0 - chi2 / (chi2_null + 1e-10)` with chi2_null = max(chi2) (peak SR < 1) whereas the reference uses SR = min(chi2)/chi2 (peak SR = 1). tls_check.py: GPU SDE=14.84 vs reference SDE=19.65 for the same P=7.70 detection; null SDEs on 5 noise-only draws: 4.77-6.81. analysis/TLS_COST_ANALYSIS.md states parity only after recomputing SDE with cuvarbase's formula on both spectra.
findings.recommendation: State in the tls_search_* docstrings and tls.rst that SDE uses the 1 - chi2/max(chi2) transform and is ~25% lower than the reference package on the same spectrum; optionally offer the reference's min(chi2)/chi2 SR as an option so published thresholds (SDE>9) apply.

findings.title: batched_run_const_nfreq(freqs=None) drops the last frequency of the autofrequency grid
findings.method: Local numpy reproduction of the arithmetic in lombscargle.py:927-933 with utils.autofrequency.
findings.evidence: lombscargle.py:932 `nf = int(round(np.max(freqs) / df)) - k0` gives nf = nf0+Nf-1-k0 = Nf-1 for freqs = df*(nf0+arange(Nf)). Local check: autofrequency len=3750; rebuilt nf=3749 (last freq 7.544122 vs rebuilt 7.542110).
findings.reproduction: python3 - <<'EOF' (local): t=sorted(rand(300)*100); freqs=autofrequency(t); df=freqs[1]-freqs[0]; k0=max(1,int(round(freqs[0]/df))); print(len(freqs), int(round(freqs.max()/df))-k0) EOF
findings.recommendation: Use `nf = len(freqs)` (the grid from autofrequency already satisfies the k0*df constraint) or `+ 1` in the rebuild.

findings.title: NFFTAsyncProcess docstring says sigma defaults to 2 but the code uses 4; and sigma=2 is NOT usable with the one-sided mode layout (top quartile of the band loses accuracy)
findings.method: Inspection + device sweep of sigma/m with the psi fix applied.
findings.evidence: cunfft.py:177 `sigma: float, optional (default: 2)` vs :212 `self.sigma = kwargs.get('sigma', 4)`. ls_psi_bug.py PATCHED rows: sigma=2 max|d| by frequency quartile 1.0e-06 1.3e-05 8.0e-06 2.7e-02 (float32) and 8.4e-10 1.8e-09 4.6e-06 2.7e-02 (double) - the top quartile is wrong regardless of m or precision because the kernel evaluates modes 0..nf-1 (not -nf/2..nf/2) on a grid of sigma*nf, so the effective oversampling at the band top is sigma/2. sigma=4 (= standard NFFT sigma 2) is accurate across the band (1.3e-05).
findings.recommendation: Fix the docstring (default 4) and state that sigma must be >= 4 for full-band accuracy in this layout (or halve the mode range convention). Also document that floating_mean=False corresponds to astropy fit_mean=False, center_data=True (ls_parity.py: max|d|=9e-3 vs that model, 0.99 vs center_data=False).

findings.title: scripts/tls_profile_stages.py references the deleted tls._auto_nbins and no longer runs
findings.method: grep
findings.evidence: scripts/tls_profile_stages.py:73 `nb = nbins or tls._auto_nbins(qmin_g, 3.0, bs)`; `grep -n _auto_nbins cuvarbase/tls.py` returns nothing (removed by the July TLS audit, finding #1).
findings.recommendation: Port the script to the banded path (replicate tls_search_batch's nbins_per logic) or delete it; the attached tls_profile.py/tls_profile2.py in the scratch dir do stage timing via monkeypatching and can replace it.

findings.title: Test gaps that let the above through: LS tests at atol=rtol=1e-2, no time-domain check of Detector A, no BJD-scale NUFFT-LRT test
findings.method: Inspection of test files.
findings.evidence: test_lombscargle.py:13-14 `lsrtol = 1E-2 / lsatol = 1E-2` (the psi bug is 7e-3, the double floorf bug 1.7e-3); test_nufft_lrt_import.py TestDetectorAlgebra compares only against a dense inverse in the same frequency space; grep for 'BJD|2457' in test_nufft_lrt*.py: none.
findings.recommendation: After fixing F1/F2, set LS tolerances to ~1e-4 (float32) / 1e-8 (double) against astropy exact; add an LRT BJD regression and a time-domain Detector A comparison (uniform sampling, flat PSD, ratio must be constant across prior widths).

findings.title: PERF: LombScargleMemory.setdata uses Python builtins min()/max()/sum() over numpy arrays: 15-60 ms at N=50-65K, 197 ms at N=200K, versus ~1-2 ms of GPU work
findings.method: Device/host timing of setdata and its components at N=20K/50K/65K/200K (min of 7 and medians).
findings.evidence: lombscargle_memory.py:31 `return w/sum(w)` (builtin sum), :325-326 `self.tmin = min(t); self.tmax = max(t)` (builtins over a float32 numpy array). ls_profile3.py: N=200000 builtin min 12.6 ms, max 12.3 ms, weights 21.7 ms vs np.min 0.03 ms; setdata total 197 ms; N=50000: 93 ms (ls_profile3) / 14.9 ms (ls_double, min of 7 - the pod CPU is shared, so the absolute number is noisy but the builtins alone are 6-16 ms at N=50-65K). Stage split at N=50000 (ls_profile2): setdata 97.9 ms of a 99.9 ms run.
findings.expected_gain: Removes tens of ms per LC for N >= 50K (Kepler-like) light curves; basis: measured builtin vs numpy reductions.
findings.recommendation: Use np.min/np.max/np.sum (and do the weighting in float32 once). Also cunfft's NFFTMemory.fromdata (:243-244) has the same builtin min/max.

findings.title: PERF: single-LC TLS calls are 96% host overhead: template tables regenerated and 27 device buffers allocated per call (tess-ffi: 7.5-9.4 ms/call with 0.31 ms of kernel)
findings.method: Device stage profile of tls_transit / tls_search_gpu at tess-ffi with monkeypatched timers on gpuarray.to_gpu/empty/set/get, template generation, preprocessing and statistics.
findings.evidence: tls.py:1399 `T_tab, S1_tab, S2_tab = tls_models.generate_template_tables(...)` runs batman + interpolation on every call (0.6-0.9 ms); tls.py:1424-1457 allocate periods/qmin/qmax/map per band, T/S1/S2, 4 chunk buffers, 4 outputs and 5 refine arrays per call. tls_profile.py tess-ffi single (refine off): total 7.53 ms = to_gpu 1.28 (12 calls) + .set 0.99 (18) + template_tables 0.94 + stats 0.60 + KERNEL search 0.31 + period_grid 0.22 + d2h 0.20 + empty 0.14 (10) + ... + 2.6 ms unaccounted Python; tls_single.py: 27 device allocations per tls_transit call; default tls_transit 9.38 ms (min 8.21), tls_search_gpu 6.35 ms vs 0.75 ms/LC in a 64-LC batch.
findings.expected_gain: 2-4x on single-LC calls (~9 -> 2-4 ms at tess-ffi); basis: measured per-stage overheads.
findings.recommendation: Cache generate_template_tables keyed on (limb_dark, tuple(u), n_table) (module-level LRU like the kernel cache); keep a per-process buffer pool for the static (T/S1/S2, periods, qmin/qmax, map) and chunk arrays; upload periods/qmin/qmax once as one array; skip return_arrays D2H when the caller only wants the best fit. No parity risk.

findings.title: PERF: the coarse TLS kernel is dominated by re-folding the whole light curve once per trial period (100% of kernel time at TESS-year, 87% at Kepler-4yr), not by the (duration, t0) trial scan
findings.method: Device timing of tls_search_batch (refine off) vs n_durations = 2, 5, 15, 30 at tess-yr and kepler-4yr with a linear fit (intercept = fold + fixed, slope = per-duration scan); input-order permutation test (time-sorted vs utils.conflict_scatter_perm vs random).
findings.evidence: tls_fast.cu:227-239 reads t_hi/t_lo/a/b (16 B) for every point in every block (one block per period): kepler-4yr = 171688 periods x 65440 points x 16 B ~ 180 GB of L2/global traffic per light curve. tls_profile2.py (c): tess-yr nd=2 18.1, nd=5 12.1, nd=15 13.9, nd=30 15.9 ms -> fit 14.9 ms + 0.00 ms/duration; kepler-4yr 78.8 / 83.0 / 91.1 / 102.1 ms -> 78.2 ms + 0.81 ms/duration (87% intercept at nd=15). tls_profile3.py: conflict_scatter_perm / random input order changed the coarse time inconsistently (tess-yr 23.5 -> 15.3 ms coarse-only in one run but the default path was 15.7 either way; kepler 96 vs 98 vs 106 ms; tess-ffi 6.1 vs 5.8 vs 4.5), i.e. shared-memory atomic contention is not the main lever (results identical to 3e-3 of chi2 ~ 7.5e4). Bands: kepler 102K periods at 256 bins, so the scan is cheap and the per-period data re-read dominates.
findings.expected_gain: Up to 2-4x on the coarse kernel for long-baseline regimes if the light curve is read once per group of G periods (fold G periods per block into G small bin arrays: 256 bins x 2 x 4 B = 2 KB per period, so G~16 fits shared memory) or, for uniform cadence, if the fold uses index arithmetic instead of reading t_hi/t_lo; basis: 87-100% of kernel time is the fold/fixed intercept.
findings.reproduction: bash <scratchpad>/pod.sh 'cd /workspace/scratch && python tls_profile2.py' (section c) and 'python tls_profile3.py'
findings.recommendation: Medium-effort kernel change: process a band of G adjacent periods per block (shared A/B arrays of G x NBINS for the 256/512-bin bands), reading each point once; keep the existing per-period scan. Parity risk: low (same arithmetic per period), but re-run the multi-band parity and golden tests.

findings.title: Negative results (do not pursue): sigma=2 for LS is not free speed; lowering m below 8 buys nothing at survey nf; ndimage.median_filter is no faster than medfilt
findings.method: Device sweeps: LS accuracy vs astropy for sigma in {2,4}, m in {3,4,5,6,8} (psi-fixed); run() timing for m in {4,5,6,8}; medfilt vs ndimage at n=2486/25K/172K.
findings.evidence: ls_psi_bug.py: sigma=2 top quartile error 2.7e-2 (any m, float or double) vs 1.3e-5 at sigma=4. ls_profile2.py (3): m=8/6/5/4 with the psi fix all give rel@peak ~2e-6 and top-band 3.5e-4 (float32 floor), and ls_profile.py m=8/6/5/4 run times 1.71/2.09/1.80/1.77 ms (gridding is 0.018 ms of the 1.6 ms run at N=1000; 0.16 ms at N=50K). tls_profile.py: medfilt 0.30/1.37/9.17 ms vs ndimage 0.16/1.33/9.09 ms, identical output.
findings.expected_gain: none
findings.recommendation: Leave sigma=4, m=8 (or m=5 for a tiny memory saving only); document why sigma cannot be lowered in this mode layout.

findings.title: NFFTAsyncProcess.run() returns the pinned host buffer before the async D2H copy lands, and on reused memory the grid is never zeroed so results accumulate; nufft_lrt.compute_nufft is correct only because dropping the fresh GPUArrays triggers cuMemFree's implicit device sync
findings.method: 40 repeated run(memory=mem) calls with the host buffer pre-zeroed: immediate snapshot vs post-sync value; second run on the same memory vs a fresh run; same test on the default (fresh-memory) path.
files: cuvarbase/cunfft.py:421-456 (run: no synchronize; docstring does not say to call finish())
cuvarbase/kernels/cunfft.cu:161 (fast_gaussian_grid accumulates with ATOMIC_ADD into a grid nobody zeroes on the NFFT path; LombScargleMemory.set_gpu_arrays_to_zero does it for LS)

findings.title: Detector A treats a zero/singular coeff_prior_cov as a FLAT prior (pinv(0)=0) instead of the matched-filter limit
findings.method: _marginal_statistic evaluated with prior_cov = 1e-12 I, exactly 0, and 1e12 I against the dense construction, matched filter, and whitened projection.
findings.evidence: af_nfft.py: 'prior_cov -> 0 (1e-12 I): -2.936541 (expect matched -2.936541); prior_cov == 0 exactly: -2.909201 (pinv(0)=0 => flat prior => -2.909201); prior_cov -> inf: -2.909201 (expect projection -2.909201)'. A user passing a diagonal prior with a zero entry (mode 'switched off') silently gets full projection along that mode.
findings.recommendation: Validate coeff_prior_cov is symmetric positive-definite (raise otherwise) and use np.linalg.solve/cholesky; document that zero-variance modes must be dropped from the basis.

findings.title: float32 GLS peak power deviates from astropy by 0.4-1.3% at the top of dense high-frequency grids (unreduced float32 phase arguments in nfft_shift/normalize and fast-math trig); FAP is exponentially sensitive to that
findings.method: GPU LS vs astropy LombScargle(method='cython', fit_mean, center_data, normalization='standard') at 7 configurations (n=1000..65000, T=365..3650 d, nf up to 912K, k0 up to 18250), max/p95 |dP| by frequency band and relative error at the injected peak.
files: cuvarbase/kernels/cunfft.cu:81 (nfft_shift phi ~ 2*pi*i*k0/ng evaluated in float32, up to ~1e5 rad)
findings.evidence: af_ls.py: 'modest hi-f signal f=18 n=1000 T=365 nf=36317 k0=183: max|d|=6.70e-03 p95=7.39e-05 peak(astropy)=0.5558 gpu=0.5625 rel=1.21e-02' with band errors ['1.4e-04@f<4.1', ..., '6.7e-03@f<20.0']; 'survey f<50 sig f=40: max|d|=2.24e-03 peak rel=3.87e-03'; 'kepler-like 65000pts: max|d|=1.70e-03 peak rel 2.91e-03'; all argmax match astropy; fap_baluev itself matches astropy exactly (ratio 1.000 at z=0.05..0.3). d ln FAP/dz ~ -N/2 so a 1% power error at z~0.3, N=300 is a ~2x FAP error.
findings.recommendation: Reduce the shift/normalize phases modulo 1 cycle before the multiply (compute (i*k0 mod ng) as an integer, then 2*pi*that/ng), and evaluate lomb.cu phases as 2*pi*frac(t*f); once the floorf fix lands, recommend use_double for FAP-sensitive work in lomb.rst.
